questions.content: A company runs an ecommerce web application on AWS. The web application is hosted as a static website on Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront for content delivery. An Amazon API Gateway API invokes AWS Lambda functions to handle user requests and order processing for the web application The Lambda functions store data in an Amazon ROS for MySQL DB cluster that uses On-Demand instances. The DB cluster usage has been consistent in the past 12 months.  Recently, the website has experienced SQL injection and web exploit attempts. Customers also report that order processing time has increased during periods of peak usagDuring these periods, the Lambda functions often have cold starts. As the company grows, the company needs to ensure scalability and low-latency access during traffic peaks. The company also must optimize the database costs and add protection against the SQL injection and web exploit attempts.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure the Lambda functions to have an increased timeout value during peak periods. Use RDS Reserved Instances for the databasUse CloudFront and subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to protect against the SQL injection and web exploit attempts.
answers.explanation: Increasing Lambda timeout does not reduce cold starts; AWS Shield Advanced does not specifically mitigate SQL injection attacks.

answers.content: Increase the memory of the Lambda functions, Transition to Amazon Redshift for the databasIntegrate Amazon Inspector with CloudFront to protect against the SQL injection and web exploit attempts.
answers.explanation: Amazon Redshift is designed for analytics, not transactional workloads like order processing; Amazon Inspector does not integrate with CloudFront for web exploit protection.

answers.content: Use Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency for compute during peak periods, Transition to Amazon Aurora Serverless for the databasUse CloudFront and subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to protect against the SQL injection and web exploit attempts.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora Serverless may not be the best cost optimization for consistently used workloads; AWS Shield Advanced is less suitable than AWS WAF for SQL injection prevention.

answers.content: Use Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency for compute during peak periods. Use RDS Reserved Instances for the databasIntegrate AWS WAF with CloudFront to protect against the SQL injection and web exploit attempts.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency reduces cold starts and improves latency during peak periods, addressing the order processing time issuUsing RDS Reserved Instances optimizes cost for a database with consistent usage over 12 months. Integrating AWS WAF with CloudFront provides targeted protection against SQL injection and web exploits, aligning with security best practices for web application protection. AWS Shield Advanced provides DDoS protection but does not specifically address SQL injection, whereas AWS WAF is designed for application-layer security.

questions.content: A company has an application that stores user-uploaded videos in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard storage. Users access the videos frequently in the first 180 days after the videos are uploaded. Access after 180 days is rare.Named users and anonymous users access the videos.Most of the videos are more than 100 MB in size. Users often have poor internetconnectivity when they upload videos, resulting in failed uploads. The company uses multipart uploads for the videos.A solutions architect needs to optimize the S3 costs of the application.Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Configure the S3 bucket to be a Requester Pays bucket.
answers.explanation: Configuring the bucket as Requester Pays does not reduce storage or transfer costs for the company and does not optimize costs based on access patterns.

answers.content: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to upload the videos to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload performance but does not directly reduce storage costs or optimize cost based on object lifecycle.

answers.content: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration o expire incomplete multipart uploads 7 days after initiation.
answers.explanation: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration o expire incomplete multipart uploads 7 days after initiation.This action directly addresses the cost optimization requirement regarding failed uploads. The problem states that users often have poor internet connectivity resulting in failed uploads, and the company uses multipart uploads. Incomplete multipart uploads consume storage and incur charges until they are explicitly deleted or expired via a lifecycle rule. Setting a rule to expire them after 7 days minimizes unnecessary storage costs from incomplete uploads, which is a common cause of unexpected S3 charges.(Source: <https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/s3-incomplete-multipart-uploads>, <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws-cloud-financial-management/discovering-and-deleting-incomplete-multipart-uploads-to-lower-amazon-s3-costs/>)

answers.content: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 day.
answers.explanation: Transitioning to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 day is premature and not aligned with the requirement that users access videos frequently in the first 180 days.

answers.content: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Standard-infrequent Access (S3 Standard- IA) after 180 days.
answers.explanation: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Standard-infrequent Access (S3 Standard- IA) after 180 days.This action addresses the cost optimization for stored videos based on their access pattern. The scenario states that videos are accessed frequently in the first 180 days, but access is rare afterward. S3 Standard-IA is designed for long-lived, infrequently accessed data that requires millisecond access. Transitioning the objects to S3 Standard-IA after 180 days significantly reduces storage costs, while still providing the required low latency for the occasional access.(Source: <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/>, <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/>)

questions.content: A company hosts an application that uses several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). During the initial startup of the EC2 instances, the EC2 instances run user data scripts to download critical content for the application from an Amazon S3 bucket.  The EC2 instances are launching correctly. However, after a period of time, the EC2 instances are terminated with the following error message: “An instance was taken out of service in response to an ELB system health check failure.” EC2 instances continue to launch and be terminated because of Auto Scaling events in an endless loop.  The only recent change to the deployment is that the company added a large amount of critical content to the S3 bucket. The company does not want to alter the user data scripts in production.  What should a solutions architect do so that the production environment can deploy successfully?

answers.content: Increase the size of the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Increasing instance size does not address the health check timing issue directly.

answers.content: Increase the health check timeout for the ALB.
answers.explanation: Increasing ALB health check timeout is not the standard solution for Auto Scaling termination due to health check failures.

answers.content: Change the health check path for the ALB.
answers.explanation: Changing the health check path is unrelated to startup delays caused by large content initialization.

answers.content: Increase the health check grace period for the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: The error indicates instances are failing ELB health checks and getting terminated by Auto Scaling. Adding a large amount of critical content to S3 likely increased the startup time of EC2 instances. Increasing the health check grace period allows instances more time to become healthy before Auto Scaling considers them unhealthy and terminates them. This avoids altering user data scripts in production while addressing the root cause of early termination.

questions.content: A company has an application that uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt and decrypt data. The application stores data in an Amazon S3 bucket in an AWS Region. Company security policies require the data to be encrypted before the data is placed into the S3 bucket. The application must decrypt the data when the application reads files from the S3 bucket.  The company replicates the S3 bucket to other Regions. A solutions architect must design a solution so that the application can encrypt and decrypt data across Regions. The application must use the same key to decrypt the data in each Region.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a KMS multi-Region primary key. Use the KMS multi-Region primary key to create a KMS multi-Region replica key in each additional Region where the application is running. Update the application code to use the specific replica key in each Region.
answers.explanation: AWS KMS multi-Region keys allow for a single logical key to be used across multiple regions securely. The question requires using the same key to encrypt and decrypt data across regions, which is exactly what multi-Region primary and replica keys enablUpdating application code to use the regional replica key aligns with best practices to securely perform encryption and decryption locally in each region.

answers.content: Create a new customer managed KMS key in each additional Region where the application is running. Update the application code to use the specific KMS key in each Region.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because separate keys per region do not meet the requirement of using the same key to decrypt data across regions.

answers.content: Use AWS Private Certificate Authority to create a new certificate authority (CA) in the primary Region. Issue a new private certificate from the CA for the application’s website URL. Share the CA with the additional Regions by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Update the application code to use the shared CA certificates in each Region.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because AWS Private CA and certificates do not address KMS encryption/decryption or key replication across Regions.

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to create a parameter in each additional Region where the application is running. Export the key material from the KMS key in the primary Region. Store the key material in the parameter in each Region. Update the application code to use the key data from the parameter in each Region.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because exporting KMS key material and storing it in Parameter Store is a security risk and not a managed service best practice.

questions.content: A global ecommerce company has many data centers around the world. With the growth of its stored data, the company needs to set up a solution to provide scalable storage for legacy on-premises file applications. The company must be able to take point-in-time copies of volumes by using AWS Backup and must retain low-latency access to frequently accessed data. The company also needs to have storage volumes that can be mounted as Internet Small Computer System Interface (iSCSI) devices from the company’s on-premises application servers.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Configure the tape gateway to store data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy AWS Backup to take point-in-time copies of the volumes.
answers.explanation: Tape gateway is for backup and archive workloads and does not provide iSCSI volumes with low-latency access.

answers.content: Provision an Amazon FSx File Gateway and an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Deploy AWS Backup to take point-in-time copies of the data.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx File Gateway and S3 File Gateway are file-based and do not offer native iSCSI volume mounts.

answers.content: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway in cache modBack up the on-premises Storage Gateway volumes with AWS Backup.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway in cached mode provides iSCSI block storage volumes accessible from on-premises servers. Cached mode ensures low-latency access to frequently accessed data by keeping it on-premises. AWS Backup supports taking point-in-time backups of Storage Gateway volumes, fulfilling the backup requirement. Volume gateway is explicitly designed for iSCSI connectivity, unlike file gateway or tape gateway.

answers.content: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in cache modDeploy AWS Backup to take point-in-time copies of the volumes.
answers.explanation: File gateway provides file-level access via NFS/SMB and is not suitable for mounting via iSCSI.

questions.content: A company is using AWS CloudFormation as its deployment tool for all applications. It stages all application binaries and templates within Amazon S3 buckets with versioning enabled. Developers have access to an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts the integrated development environment (IDE). The developers download the application binaries from Amazon S3 to the EC2 instance, make changes, and upload the binaries to an S3 bucket after running the unit tests locally. The developers want to improve the existing deployment mechanism and implement CI/CD using AWS CodePipelin The developers have the following requirements: • Use AWS CodeCommit for source control. • Automate unit testing and security scanning. • Alert the developers when unit tests fail. • Turn application features on and off, and customize deployment dynamically as part of CI/CD. • Have the lead developer provide approval before deploying an application.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS CodeBuild to run unit tests and security scans. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to send Amazon SNS alerts to the developers when unit tests fail. Write AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) constructs for different solution features, and use a manifest file to tum features on and off in the AWS CDK application. Use a manual approval stage in the pipeline to allow the lead developer to approve applications.
answers.explanation: AWS CodeBuild is the managed service designed to run unit tests and security scans in CI/CD pipelines, ensuring automation and integration with CodePipelinAmazon EventBridge integrates well with CodeBuild to detect failed builds and trigger SNS alerts to notify developers promptly. AWS CDK allows feature toggling through constructs and manifest files, enabling dynamic customization of deployments as required. A manual approval stage in CodePipeline supports the lead developer's approval step before deployment, enforcing control and security.

answers.content: Use AWS Lambda to run unit tests and security scans. Use Lambda in a subsequent stage in the pipeline to send Amazon SNS alerts to the developers when unit tests fail. Write AWS Amplify plugins for different solution features and utilize user prompts to tum features on and off. Use Amazon SES in the pipeline to allow the lead developer to approve applications.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Lambda for unit tests and security scans is not appropriate; Lambda is not designed to replace build services like CodeBuild.

answers.content: Use Jenkins to run unit tests and security scans. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule in the pipeline to send Amazon SES alerts to the developers when unit tests fail Use AWS CloudFormation nested stacks for different solution features and parameters to turn features on and off. Use AWS Lambda in the pipeline to allow the lead developer to approve applications.
answers.explanation: Jenkins is a third-party tool, not a fully managed AWS service, and using Lambda to allow lead developer approval is not a standard mechanism.

answers.content: Use AWS CodeDeploy to run unit tests and security scans. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm in the pipeline to send Amazon SNS alerts to the developers when unit tests fail. Use Docker images for different solution features and the AWS CLI to turn features on and off. Use a manual approval stage in the pipeline to allow the lead developer to approve applications.
answers.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy is for deployment, not running tests or security scans, and CloudWatch alarms are not typically used for send alerts for unit test failures in pipelines.

questions.content: A solutions architect is importing a VM from an on-premises environment by using the Amazon EC2 VM Import feature of AWS Import/Export. The solutions architect has created an AMI and has provisioned an Amazon EC2 instance that is based on that AMI. The EC2 instance runs inside a public subnet in a VPC and has a public IP address assigned.  The EC2 instance does not appear as a managed instance in the AWS Systems Manager consol Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Verify that Systems Manager Agent is installed on the instance and is running.
answers.explanation: Verify that Systems Manager Agent is installed on the instance and is running.The AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) must be installed and running on an EC2 instance for it to be recognized as a managed instance by Systems Manager. Since the VM was imported from an on-premises environment using VM Import, the SSM Agent is likely not preinstalled or running, even though it is preinstalled on most Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). Verifying the installation and operational status of the SSM Agent is a critical first step in troubleshooting this issue.

answers.content: Verify that the instance is assigned an appropriate IAM role for Systems Manager.
answers.explanation:
Verify that the instance is assigned an appropriate IAM role for Systems Manager.
For an EC2 instance to communicate with the AWS Systems Manager service, it must have an IAM instance profile (role) attached with the necessary permissions (e.g., the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy). Without this role, the SSM Agent cannot register the instance with the Systems Manager console. This is a fundamental requirement for managing EC2 instances with Systems Manager.

answers.content: Verify the existence of a VPC endpoint on the VPC.
answers.explanation: A VPC endpoint is not mandatory if the instance has a public IP and internet access.

answers.content: Verity that the AWS Application Discovery Agent is configured.
answers.explanation: The AWS Application Discovery Agent is unrelated to Systems Manager managed instances.

answers.content: Verify the correct configuration of service-linked roles for Systems Manager.
answers.explanation: Service-linked roles are not specified as necessary for Systems Manager managed instances in the key facts.

questions.content: A company is developing a latency-sensitive application. Part of the application includes several AWS Lambda functions that need to initialize as quickly as possiblThe Lambda functions are written in Java and contain initialization code outside the handlers to load libraries, initialize classes, and generate unique IDs.  Which solution will meet the startup performance requirement MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Move all the initialization code to the handlers for each Lambda function. Activate Lambda SnapStart for each Lambda function. Configure SnapStart to reference the $LATEST version of each Lambda function.
answers.explanation: SnapStart cannot reference the $LATEST version; it requires published versions, and moving initialization code to handlers is against performance best practices.

answers.content: Publish a version of each Lambda function. Create an alias for each Lambda function. Configure each alias to point to its corresponding version. Set up a provisioned concurrency configuration for each Lambda function to point to the corresponding alias.
answers.explanation: Provisioned concurrency on aliases is less direct and does not involve SnapStart, which is needed for startup improvement in Java Lambdas.

answers.content: Publish a version of each Lambda function. Set up a provisioned concurrency configuration for each Lambda function to point to the corresponding version. Activate Lambda SnapStar for the published versions of the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps Lambda functions initialized and ready to respond quickly, reducing startup latency. Publishing versions for Lambda functions creates immutable deployment artifacts needed for provisioned concurrency and SnapStart. Activating Lambda SnapStart on published versions speeds up cold starts by snapshotting the initialized execution environment. Using provisioned concurrency with SnapStart on published versions applies best practices for performance optimization in Java Lambda functions.

answers.content: Update the Lambda functions to add a pre-snapshot hook. Move the code that generates unique IDs into the handlers. Publish a version of each Lambda function. Activate Lambda SnapStart for the published versions of the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Adding pre-snapshot hooks and moving unique ID generation into handlers increases complexity and code execution time on invocation, reducing startup speed.

questions.content: A company is running a serverless ecommerce application on AWS. The application uses Amazon API Gateway to invoke AWS Lambda Java functions. The Lambda functions connect to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database to store data.  During a recent sale event, a sudden increase in web traffic resulted in poor API performance and database connection failures. The company needs to implement a solution to minimize the latency for the Lambda functions and to support bursts in traffic.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the application?

answers.content: Update the code of the Lambda functions so that the Lambda functions open the database connection outside of the function handler. Increase the provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Opening connections outside the handler and using provisioned concurrency improves cold start latency but does not address database connection pooling or scalability during bursts effectively.

answers.content: Create an RDS Proxy endpoint for the databasStore database secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Set up the required IAM permissions. Update the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS Proxy endpoint. Increase the provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Provisioned concurrency is more costly and less flexible than reserved concurrency; reserved concurrency better aligns with Lambda best practices for controlling function bursts.

answers.content: Create a custom parameter group. Increase the value of the max_connections parameter. Associate the custom parameter group with the RDS DB instance and schedule a reboot. Increase the reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Increasing max_connections in RDS parameter group and reserved concurrency does not address efficient connection management; it risks database overload and lacks connection pooling.

answers.content: Create an RDS Proxy endpoint for the databasStore database secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Set up the required IAM permissions. Update the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS Proxy endpoint. Increase the reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon RDS Proxy is a managed service designed to improve application scalability by pooling and sharing database connections, which minimizes latency and connection failures caused by sudden traffic bursts. Storing database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager adheres to security best practices by avoiding hard-coded or plaintext credentials. Setting up IAM permissions for RDS Proxy access enforces least privilege security. Increasing reserved concurrency for Lambda functions helps handle bursts in traffic without throttling, and reserved concurrency provides more precise concurrency control compared to provisioned concurrency. Updating the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS Proxy endpoint requires minimal code changes, meeting the requirement of least amount of change.

questions.content: A company hosts its primary API on AWS by using an Amazon API Gateway API and AWS Lambda functions that contain the logic for the API methods. The company’s internal applications use the API for core functionality and business logic. The company’s customers use the API to access data from their accounts. Several customers also have access to a legacy API that is running on a single standalone Amazon EC2 instanc The company wants to increase the security for these APIs to better prevent denial of service (DoS) attacks, check for vulnerabilities, and guard against common exploits.  What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS WAF to protect both APIs. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the legacy API. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor for malicious attempts to access the APIs.
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector cannot analyze the API Gateway API; it targets EC2 and similar compute resources.

answers.content: Use AWS WAF to protect the API Gateway API. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze both APIs. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to block malicious attempts to access the APIs.
answers.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty cannot block malicious attempts; it only monitors and alerts.

answers.content: Use AWS WAF to protect the API Gateway API. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the legacy API. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor for malicious attempts to access the APIs.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF is designed to protect API Gateway APIs from DoS attacks and common exploits, making it suitable for securing the API Gateway API. Amazon Inspector is used to analyze the security posture of EC2 instances, so it is appropriate to analyze the legacy API running on a standalone EC2 instancAmazon GuardDuty monitors and detects malicious activity but does not block it; therefore, it is suitable for monitoring malicious attempts to access the APIs. Option C correctly assigns each service based on their security functions and service scope.

answers.content: Use AWS WAF to protect the API Gateway AP! Configure Amazon Inspector to protect the legacy API. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to block malicious attempts to access the APIs.
answers.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty cannot block malicious attempts; also, there is a typo in 'API' which indicates less care in the option.

questions.content: A company plans to migrate many VMs from an on-premises environment to AWS. The company requires an initial assessment of the on-premises environment before the migration, a visualization of the dependencies between applications that run on the VMs, and a report that provides an assessment of the on-premises environment.  To get this information, the company has initiated a Migration Evaluator assessment request. The company has the ability to install collector software in its on-premises environment without any constraints  Which solution will provide the company with the required information with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Install the AWS Application Discovery Agent on each on-premises VM. After the data collection period ends, use AWS Migration Hub to view the application dependencies. Download the Quick insights assessment report from Migration Hub.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Agent is designed to collect detailed system and application dependency data on on-premises VMs. AWS Migration Hub integrates with Application Discovery Service to visualize application dependencies and provides assessment reports like Quick Insights, minimizing manual effort. Using Migration Hub with the Application Discovery Agent offers a managed, low-overhead solution without the need for manual data exports or additional report generation steps. The question specifies the company requires visualization of dependencies and assessment reports, which Migration Hub plus the Application Discovery Agent directly provide.

answers.content: Install the Migration Evaluator Collector on each on-premises VM. After the data collection period ends, use Migration Evaluator to view the application dependencies. Download and export the discovered server list from Migration Evaluator. Upload the list to Amazon QuickSight When the QuickSight report is generated, download the Quick Insights assessment report.
answers.explanation: Involves manual upload to Amazon QuickSight and exporting server lists, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Setup the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector in the on-premises environment. After the data collection period ends, use AWS Migration Hub to view the application dependencies. Export the discovered server list from Application Discovery ServicUpload the list to Migration Evaluator. When the Migration Evaluator report is generated, download the Quick Insights assessment.
answers.explanation: Agentless collector may provide less detailed dependency data and requires complex export/import steps, increasing overhead.

answers.content: Set up the Migration Evaluator Collector in the on-premises environment. Install the AWS Application Discovery Agent on each VM. After the data collection period ends, use AWS Migration Hub to view the application dependencies. Download the Quick Insights assessment report from Migration Evaluator.
answers.explanation: Combines two collectors unnecessarily, increasing complexity and operational overhead.

questions.content: A company recently completed a successful proof of concept of Amazon WorkSpaces. A solutions architect needs to make the solution highly available across two AWS Regions. Amazon WorkSpaces is deployed in a failover Region, and a hosted zone is deployed in Amazon Route 53.  What should the solutions architect do to configure high availability for the solution?

answers.content: Create a connection alias in the primary Region and in the failover Region. Associate the connection aliases with a directory in each Region. Create a Route 53 failover routing policy. Set Evaluate Target Health to Yes.
answers.explanation: Creating connection aliases in both primary and failover Regions and associating each with a directory in its respective Region ensures that each Region can independently authenticate WorkSpaces users, supporting true high availability. Using a Route 53 failover routing policy with Evaluate Target Health set to Yes allows automatic DNS failover based on the health of the endpoints, which is essential for highly available solutions and aligns with AWS best practices of avoiding single points of failure.

answers.content: Create a connection alias in the primary Region and in the failover Region. Associate the connection aliases with a directory in the primary Region. Create a Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
answers.explanation: Associating both connection aliases with a directory only in the primary Region does not leverage the failover Region properly, risking a single point of failure.

answers.content: Create a connection alias in the primary Region. Associate the connection alias with a directory in the primary Region. Create a Route 53 weighted routing policy.
answers.explanation: Only creating a connection alias and associating it in the primary Region neglects the failover Region, which does not ensure high availability across Regions.

answers.content: Create a connection alias in the primary Region Associate the connection alias with a directory in the failover Region. Create a Route 53 failover routing policy. Set Evaluate Target Health to Yes.
answers.explanation: Creating a connection alias only in the primary Region but associating it with a directory in the failover Region is inconsistent and would likely cause operational issues; connection aliases should be region-specific.

questions.content: A utility company wants to collect usage data every 5 minutes from its smart meters to facilitate time-of-use metering. When a meter sends data to AWS, the data is sent to Amazon API Gateway, processed by an AWS Lambda function. and stored in an Amazon DynamoDB tablDuring the pilot phase, the Lambda functions took from 3 to 5 seconds to complet As more smart meters are deployed, the engineers notice the Lambda functions are taking from 1 to 2 minutes to completThe functions are also increasing in duration as new types of metrics are collected from the devices. There are many ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors while performing PUT operations on DynamoDB, and there are also many TooManyRequestsException errors from Lambda.  Which combination of changes will resolve these issues? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Increase the write capacity units to the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: The problem states "There are many ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors while performing PUT operations on DynamoDB." This error explicitly means that the provisioned write capacity of the DynamoDB table is being exceeded by the incoming requests. To resolve this, you must increase the write capacity units (WCU) for the DynamoDB table, or change the table to use on-demand capacity mode if the traffic is unpredictable and highly variable. This directly addresses the DynamoDB throttling issue.

answers.content: Increase the memory available to the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Increasing memory does not address throughput or throttling issues in DynamoDB or Lambda.

answers.content: Increase the payload size from the smart meters to send more data.
answers.explanation: Increasing payload size would increase processing time and load, worsening the issue.

answers.content: Stream the data into an Amazon Kinesis data stream from API Gateway and process the data in batches.
answers.explanation:
Stream the data into an Amazon Kinesis data stream from API Gateway and process the data in batches.
The problem describes a high-volume, real-time data ingestion scenario (usage data every 5 minutes from smart meters) that is overwhelming both Lambda ("TooManyRequestsException") and DynamoDB ("ProvisionedThroughputExceededException"). Implementing Kinesis Data Streams introduces a buffer and a highly scalable ingestion mechanism (up to 1,000 requests per second per shard for writes, and virtually unlimited ingress capacity with on-demand mode). Instead of having Lambda functions individually process and write data for every single meter reading immediately, the data can be streamed into Kinesis and then processed downstream in batches (e.g., using a Kinesis consumer Lambda function or Kinesis Data Firehose) which drastically reduces the request rate to DynamoDB and Lambda, thereby resolving the throttling issues for both services. This decouples the ingestion layer from the processing layer and allows for better handling of spiky traffic.

answers.content: Collect data in an Amazon SQS FIFO queue, which triggers a Lambda function to process each message
answers.explanation:
Collect data in an Amazon SQS FIFO queue, which triggers a Lambda function to process each message
Amazon SQS FIFO queues guarantee ordering and prevents duplicate message delivery, but they are not designed for high-throughput stream ingestion. More critically, Lambda functions processing messages from an SQS FIFO queue scale only based on Message Group ID, potentially limiting concurrency drastically and delaying processing, especially in a high-volume scenario like this where many concurrent writes are needed. Furthermore, using SQS standard or FIFO doesn't inherently batch the writes to DynamoDB or solve the throughput exceeded error, as Lambda is still processing messages individually which leads to a high rate of PUT requests to DynamoDB. Kinesis is the superior solution for high-volume, time-series data stream ingestion that requires batching before storage.

questions.content: A company needs to use an AWS Transfer Family SFTP-enabled server with an Amazon S3 bucket to receive updates from a third-party data supplier. The data is encrypted with Pretty Good Privacy (PGP) encryption. The company needs a solution that will automatically decrypt the data after the company receives the data. A solutions architect will use a Transfer Family managed workflow. The company has created an IAM service role by using an IAM policy that allows access to AWS Secrets Manager and the S3 bucket. The role’s trust relationship allows the transfer amazonaws.com service to assume the rol What should the solutions architect do next to complete the solution for automatic decryption?

answers.content: Store the PGP public key in Secrets Manager. Add a nominal step in the Transfer Family managed workflow to decrypt files. Configure PGP encryption parameters in the nominal step. Associate the workflow with the Transfer Family server.
answers.explanation: Storing the public key and configuring PGP encryption parameters is incorrect because decryption requires the private key, not the public key.

answers.content: Store the PGP private key in Secrets Manager. Add an exception-handling step in the Transfer Family managed workflow to decrypt files. Configure PGP encryption parameters in the exception handler. Associate the workflow with the SFTP user.
answers.explanation: Using an exception-handling step and associating the workflow with the SFTP user is less correct than using a nominal step for automatic processing and associating the workflow at the server level for consistent application.

answers.content: Store the PGP private key in Secrets Manager. Add a nominal step in the Transfer Family managed workflow to decrypt files. Configure PGP decryption parameters in the nominal step. Associate the workflow with the Transfer Family server.
answers.explanation: The company needs to decrypt PGP-encrypted data, which requires the private key to perform decryption, so the private key must be stored in Secrets Manager. Transfer Family managed workflows support adding nominal steps for processing files, including decryption. Configuring PGP decryption parameters in the nominal workflow step aligns with automatic processing upon file receipt. Associating the workflow with the Transfer Family server ensures automatic invocation for all relevant file transfers.

answers.content: Store the PGP public key in Secrets Manager. Add an exception-handling step in the Transfer Family managed workflow to decrypt files. Configure PGP decryption parameters in the exception handler. Associate the workflow with the SFTP user.
answers.explanation: Storing the public key and using exception handling is incorrect since decryption requires the private key, and the exception handler is not appropriate for standard processing.

questions.content: A company is running several applications in the AWS Cloud. The applications are specific to separate business units in the company. The company is running the components of the applications in several AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations.  Every cloud resource in the company’s organization has a tag that is named BusinessUnit. Every tag already has the appropriate value of the business unit nam The company needs to allocate its cloud costs to different business units. The company also needs to visualize the cloud costs for each business unit.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: In the organization's management account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. Also in the management account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure the S3 bucket as the destination for the AWS CUR. From the management account, query the AWS CUR data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon QuickSight for visualization.
answers.explanation: Cost allocation tags must be created and activated to appear in cost allocation reports. Creating the cost allocation tag 'BusinessUnit' in the management account ensures centralized management and reporting across the organization. Using AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR) with an S3 bucket in the management account consolidates cost data from all accounts. Querying CUR data with Amazon Athena and visualizing with Amazon QuickSight provides a managed, scalable, and secure solution aligned with AWS best practices.

answers.content: In each member account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. In the organization’s management account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure the S3 bucket as the destination for the AWS CUR. Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for visualization.
answers.explanation: Creating tags in each member account is redundant; CloudWatch dashboards are not designed for detailed cost visualization compared to QuickSight.

answers.content: In the organization's management account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. In each member account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure each S3 bucket as the destination for its respective AWS CUR. In the management account, create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for visualization.
answers.explanation: Configuring separate CURs and S3 buckets per member account complicates cost aggregation unnecessarily; central CUR is preferred.

answers.content: In each member account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. Also in each member account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure each S3 bucket as the destination for its respective AWS CUR. From the management account, query the AWS CUR data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon QuickSight for visualization.
answers.explanation: Creating CUR and S3 buckets in each member account introduces complexity; CUR should be centralized in management account for consolidated reporting.

questions.content: A company is migrating infrastructure for its massive multiplayer game to AWS. The game’s application features a leaderboard where players can see rankings in real timThe leaderboard requires microsecond reads and single-digit-millisecond write latencies. The datasets are single-digit terabytes in size and must be available to accept writes in less than a minute if a primary node failure occurs.  The company needs a solution in which data can persist for further analytical processing through a data pipelin Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an Amazon ROS database with a read replica. Configure the application to point writes to the writer endpoint. Configure the application to point reads to the reader endpoint.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS does not provide microsecond read latency and read replicas add complexity and latency due to replication lag.

answers.content: Create an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster in Muit-AZ mode Configure the application to interact with the primary node.
answers.explanation: Amazon MemoryDB for Redis is a fully managed, durable, in-memory database service designed for microsecond read latencies and single-digit millisecond writes. MemoryDB supports Multi-AZ deployments to provide less than a minute failover for write availability, meeting high availability requirements. It offers persistence, allowing data to be retained for further analytical processing through integration with data pipelines. MemoryDB requires less operational overhead than managing Redis on EC2 instances or configuring complex read replicas. While DynamoDB delivers single-digit millisecond latencies, it does not meet the microsecond read latency requirement, ruling it out.

answers.content: Create multiple Redis nodes on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure backups to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Managing Redis on EC2 instances increases operational overhead and risk, violating the requirement for least operational overhead.

answers.content: (Amazon DynamoDB with Global Secondary Index): DynamoDB delivers single-digit millisecond latency for both reads and writes, but the requirement is microsecond reads. While DynamoDB is fully managed and supports leaderboards, MemoryDB is the only one that meets the strict microsecond read latency.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB only delivers single-digit millisecond latency, not microsecond latency, failing the key performance requirement.

questions.content: A company needs to move some on-premises Oracle databases to AWS. The company has chosen to keep some of the databases on premises for business compliance reasons.  The on-premises databases contain spatial data and run cron jobs for maintenancThe company needs to connect to the on-premises systems directly from AWS to query data as a foreign tabl Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create Amazon DynamoDB global tables with auto scaling enabled. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to move the data from on premises to DynamoDB. Create an AWS Lambda function to move the spatial data to Amazon S3. Query the data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule jobs in DynamoDB for maintenancUse Amazon API Gateway for foreign table support.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB and Lambda do not natively support Oracle spatial data or foreign tables well; the solution is overly complex and lacks direct foreign table support.

answers.content: Create an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instancUse native replication to move the data from on premises to the DB instancUse the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to modify the SQL Server schema as needed after replication. Move the spatial data to Amazon Redshift. Use stored procedures for system maintenancCreate AWS Glue crawlers to connect to the on-premises Oracle databases for foreign table support.
answers.explanation: AWS Glue crawlers cannot connect to on-premises Oracle databases for foreign table support and moving the spatial data to Redshift is not ideal for spatial queries.

answers.content: Launch Amazon EC2 instances to host the Oracle databases. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use AWS Application Migration Service to move the data from on premises to the EC2 instances and for real-time bidirectional change data capture (CDC) synchronization. Use Oracle native spatial data support. Create an AWS Lambda function to run maintenance jobs as part of an AWS Step Functions workflow. Create an internet gateway for foreign table support.
answers.explanation: Hosting Oracle on Amazon EC2 does not use managed AWS database services and creating internet gateway for foreign table support is insecure and not a best practice.

answers.content: Create an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instancUse the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to move the data from on premises to the DB instancUse PostgreSQL native spatial data support. Run cron jobs on the DB instance for maintenancUse AWS Direct Connect to connect the DB instance to the on-premises environment for foreign table support.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL supports native spatial data capabilities, which suits the requirement for spatial data handling. Using AWS SCT and DMS to move data from on premises provides a managed solution for migration. Running cron jobs directly on the DB instance aligns with maintenance needs without complex workarounds. AWS Direct Connect establishes a secure and reliable network link between AWS and on-premises infrastructure, supporting foreign table connections securely. This approach leverages managed AWS services such as Amazon RDS, DMS, and SCT, following best practices for security and operational efficiency stated in the provided key facts.

questions.content: A company is migrating its blog platform to AWS. The company's on-premises servers connect to AWS through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The blog content is updated several times a day by multiple authors and is served from a file share on a network-attached storage (NAS) server.  The company needs to migrate the blog platform without delaying the content updates. The company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones to run the blog platform behind an Application Load Balancer. The company also needs to move 200 TB of archival data from its on-premises servers to Amazon S3 as soon as possibl Which combination of stops will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a weekly cron job in Amazon EventBridgUse the cron job to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update the EC2 instances from the NAS server.
answers.explanation: Using a cron job with Lambda to update EC2 instances from the NAS is not suitable because it does not address continuous content updates or scalable shared storage.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volume for the EC2 instances to share for content access. Write code to synchronize the EBS volume with the NAS server weekly.
answers.explanation: Amazon EBS Multi-Attach volumes cannot be used as shared file systems across multiple EC2 instances for file sharing like NAS or EFS; also, synchronizing with the NAS weekly causes delays.

answers.content: Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to the on-premises servers to act as the NAS server. Copy the blog data to the EFS file system. Mount the EFS file system to the C2 instances to serve the content.
answers.explanation:
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze the source databases for changes that are required.
AWS SCT is the primary tool used in a heterogeneous database migration (e.g., Oracle/SQL Server/MySQL to Amazon RDS, possibly changing engine types, which is common in a mixed-fleet migration to RDS). Since the question specifically mentions databases having "custom schemas and stored procedures," AWS SCT is required to analyze and convert the schema and procedural code (like stored procedures, functions, etc.) that may be incompatible with the target Amazon RDS engines.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devicCopy the static data artifacts to the devicShip the device to AWS.
answers.explanation:
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the source databases to Amazon RDS.
AWS DMS is the dedicated service for migrating data from various sources (including Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle) to AWS targets, such as Amazon RDS, with minimal downtime. DMS handles the actual data migration (full load and ongoing replication/CDC) after the schema conversion by AWS SCT is complete. For this scenario, where a fleet of databases needs to be migrated to Amazon RDS, DMS is the standard, correct tool for the data migration phase.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowcons SSD devicCopy the static data artifacts to the devicShip the device to AWS.
answers.explanation: AWS Snowcons SSD device is not a valid AWS service/device for data transfer; thus, it cannot be used.

questions.content: A company needs to migrate its on-premises database fleet to Amazon RDS. The company is currently using a mixture of Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle databases. Some of the databases have custom schemas and stored procedures.  Which combination of steps should the company take for the migration? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use Migration Evaluator Quick Insights to analyze the source databases and to identify the stored procedures that need to be migrated.
answers.explanation: Migration Evaluator Quick Insights is not used to analyze stored procedures or schemas for database migration.

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration Service to analyze the source databases and to identify the stored procedures that need to be migrated.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service is intended for server migration, not analyzing stored procedures for database migration.

answers.content: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze the source databases for changes that are required
answers.explanation:
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze the source databases for changes that are required.
AWS SCT is the primary tool used in a heterogeneous database migration (e.g., Oracle/SQL Server/MySQL to Amazon RDS, possibly changing engine types, which is common in a mixed-fleet migration to RDS). Since the question specifically mentions databases having "custom schemas and stored procedures," AWS SCT is required to analyze and convert the schema and procedural code (like stored procedures, functions, etc.) that may be incompatible with the target Amazon RDS engines.

answers.content: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the source databases to Amazon RDS.
answers.explanation:
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the source databases to Amazon RDS.
AWS DMS is the dedicated service for migrating data from various sources (including Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle) to AWS targets, such as Amazon RDS, with minimal downtime. DMS handles the actual data migration (full load and ongoing replication/CDC) after the schema conversion by AWS SCT is complete. For this scenario, where a fleet of databases needs to be migrated to Amazon RDS, DMS is the standard, correct tool for the data migration phase.

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the source databases to Amazon RDS.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is for file data transfer, not for migrating database contents.

questions.content: A company requires that all internal application connectivity use private IP addresses. To facilitate this policy, a solutions architect has created interface endpoints to connect to AWS Public services. Upon testing, the solutions architect notices that the service names are resolving to public IP addresses, and that internal services cannot connect to the interface endpoints.  Which step should the solutions architect take to resolve this issue?

answers.content: Update the subnet route table with a route to the interface endpoint.
answers.explanation: Each subnet route table must have a route that sends traffic destined for the service to the gateway endpoint using the prefix list for the service Updating the subnet route table to direct traffic to the interface endpoint ensures that the service names resolve to private IP addresses and internal services can connect Enabling private DNS or modifying security groups may not resolve the routing of service traffic to the interface endpoint

answers.content: Enable the private DNS option on the VPC attributes.
answers.explanation: Enabling private DNS on the VPC attributes is not a valid or sufficient step to route traffic to the interface endpoint

answers.content: Configure the security group on the interface endpoint to allow connectivity to the AWS services.
answers.explanation: Configuring security group allows traffic but does not resolve DNS resolution nor routing issues

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone with a conditional forwarder for the internal application.
answers.explanation: Creating a Route 53 private hosted zone with a conditional forwarder is unnecessary when using interface endpoints

questions.content: A company is collecting data from a large set of IoT devices. The data is stored in an Amazon S3 data lakData scientists perform analytics on Amazon EC2 instances that run in two public subnets in a VPC in a separate AWS account.  The data scientists need access to the data lake from the EC2 instances. The EC2 instances already have an assigned role with permissions to access Amazon S3. According to company policies, only authorized networks are allowed to have access to the IoT data.  Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the data scientists’ VPC.
answers.explanation: Creating a gateway VPC endpoint in the data scientists’ VPC is not possible across different AWS accounts, and the question states the data lake is in a separate AWS account.

answers.content: Create an S3 access point in the data scientists' AWS account for the data lake.
answers.explanation: Creating a cross-account S3 Access Point in the data scientists' (consumer) account simplifies sharing a specific subset of data and allows the data scientists to use a unique endpoint (the Access Point ARN) in their resource policies. Access Points can be configured to restrict access to a specific VPC, which addresses the requirement that "only authorized networks are allowed to have access to the IoT data.

answers.content: Update the EC2 instance rolAdd a policy with a condition that allows the s3:GetObject action when the value for the s3:DataAccessPointArn condition key is a valid access point ARN.
answers.explanation: Updating the EC2 instance role with a condition on the s3:DataAccessPointArn is unnecessary if the bucket policy already restricts access via access points; role policies generally do not restrict by DataAccessPointArn to enforce network restrictions.

answers.content: Update the VPC route table to route S3 traffic to an S3 access point.
answers.explanation: Route tables cannot be updated to route to S3 access points; access points are not targets for routing but are managed via bucket policies and IAM policies.

answers.content: Add an S3 bucket policy with a condition that allows the s3:GetObject action when the value for the s3:DataAccessPointArn condition key is a valid access point ARN.
answers.explanation: For cross-account access using S3 Access Points, the bucket policy on the data lake (owner) account must explicitly permit the access point in the consumer account to access the data. Using the s3:DataAccessPointArn condition key ensures that access is only granted when the request is made through a specific, authorized Access Point, which aligns with the security requirement. This configuration is necessary to establish the trust relationship for cross-account data sharing via Access Points.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate its website to AWS. The website uses containers that are deployed in an on-premises, self-managed Kubernetes cluster. All data for the website is stored in an on-premises PostgreSQL databas The company has decided to migrate the on-premises Kubernetes cluster to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster will use EKS managed node groups with a static number of nodes. The company will also migrate the on-premises database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databas A solutions architect needs to estimate the total cost of ownership (TCO) for this workload before the migration.  Which solution will provide the required TCO information?

answers.content: Request access to Migration Evaluator. Run the Migration Evaluator Collector and import the data. Configure a scenario. Export a Quick Insights report from Migration Evaluator.
answers.explanation: Migration Evaluator (formerly TSO Logic) is the AWS service specifically designed to estimate total cost of ownership (TCO) for migration scenarios by collecting usage data and generating reports. Running the Migration Evaluator Collector gathers on-premises environment data needed for an accurate AWS TCO estimation. Configuring a scenario and exporting a Quick Insights report provides a detailed analysis of cost estimates for migrating Kubernetes and databases. The other options either do not provide integrated TCO estimations (AWS DMS, Pricing Calculator alone) or do not focus on TCO reporting (Application Migration Service is for migration execution, not cost estimation).

answers.content: Launch AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) for the on-premises databasGenerate an assessment report. Create an estimate in AWS Pricing Calculator for the costs of the EKS migration.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS and Pricing Calculator do not directly provide comprehensive TCO estimations for migrating both Kubernetes clusters and RDS databases.

answers.content: Initialize AWS Application Migration ServicAdd the on-premises servers as source servers. Launch a test instancOutput a TCO report from Application Migration Service.
answers.explanation: Application Migration Service is designed for migration execution and testing, not for generating TCO reports.

answers.content: Access the AWS Cloud Economics Center webpage to assess the AWS Cloud Value Framework. Create an AWS Cost and Usage report from the Cloud Value Framework.
answers.explanation: AWS Cloud Economics Center and Cost and Usage reports do not directly generate TCO estimates for migration scenarios.

questions.content: An events company runs a ticketing platform on AWS. The company’s customers configure and schedule their events on the platform. The events result in large increases of traffic to the platform. The company knows the date and time of each customer’s events.  The company runs the platform on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The ECS cluster consists of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The Auto Scaling group uses a predictive scaling policy.  The ECS cluster makes frequent requests to an Amazon S3 bucket to download ticket assets. The ECS cluster and the S3 bucket are in the same AWS Region and the same AWS account. Traffic between the ECS cluster and the S3 bucket flows across a NAT gateway.  The company needs to optimize the cost of the platform without decreasing the platform's availability.  Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Creating a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 removes the need for a NAT gateway for S3 traffic, significantly reducing data transfer and NAT gateway costs without affecting availability.

answers.content: Add another ECS capacity provider that uses an Auto Scaling group of Spot Instances. Configure the new capacity provider strategy to have the same weight as the existing capacity provider strategy.
answers.explanation: Adding an ECS capacity provider backed by Spot Instances lowers compute costs, while keeping the same weight ensures availability is maintained by balancing Spot and On-Demand capacity.

answers.content: Create On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the applicable instance type for the time period of the scheduled scaling policies.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations increase cost and are used for capacity guarantees, not cost optimization.

answers.content: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration improves performance for long-distance uploads but adds cost and provides no benefit within the same Region.

answers.content: Replace the predictive scaling policy with scheduled scaling policies for the scheduled events.
answers.explanation: Replacing predictive scaling with scheduled scaling reduces flexibility and does not directly optimize infrastructure or networking costs.

questions.content: A company has multiple AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to store AWS account activity and query the data from a central location by using SQL.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS CloudTraii trail in each account. Specify CloudTrail management events for the trail. Configure CloudTrail to send the events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure CloudWatch cross-account observability. Query the data in CloudWatch Logs Insights.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch Logs cross-account observability does not provide native SQL querying capability similar to CloudTrail Lake.

answers.content: Use a delegated administrator account to create an AWS CloudTrail Lake data storSpecify CloudTrail management events for the data storEnable the data store for all accounts in the organization. Query the data in CloudTrail Lake.
answers.explanation: AWS CloudTrail Lake is designed to store and query account activity centrally using SQL. Using a delegated administrator account to create a CloudTrail Lake data store and enable it for all accounts in the AWS Organization centralizes collection and querying efficiently. This approach aligns with best practices of centralized logging and querying for multiple accounts within an organization.

answers.content: Use a delegated administrator account to create an AWS CloudTral trail. Specify CloudTrail management events for the trail. Enable the trail for all accounts in the organization. Keep all other settings as default. Query the CloudTrail data from the CloudTrail event history page.
answers.explanation: Querying CloudTrail event history page is limited to individual accounts and is not centralized for multiple accounts.

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy AWS CloudTrail Lake data stores in each account. Specify CloudTrail management events for the data stores. Keep all other settings as default, Query the data in CloudTrail Lake.
answers.explanation: Deploying CloudTrail Lake data stores individually to each account is less efficient than using CloudTrail Lake's organization integration with a delegated administrator.

questions.content: A company is using AWS to develop and manage its production web application. The application includes an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that invokes an AWS Lambda function. The Lambda function processes and then stores data in a databas The company wants to implement user authorization for the web application in an integrated way. The company already uses a third-party identity provider that issues OAuth tokens for the company’s other applications.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Integrate the company’s third-party identity provider with API Gateway. Configure an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to validate tokens from the identity provider. Require the Lambda authorizer on all API routes. Update the web application to get tokens from the identity provider and include the tokens in the Authorization header when calling the API Gateway HTTP API.
answers.explanation: API Gateway supports integration with third-party identity providers for user authorization via Lambda authorizers. Using a Lambda authorizer to validate OAuth tokens issued by the existing third-party identity provider aligns with the requirement to use the existing identity system. This approach avoids storing credentials in code and leverages managed AWS services. Security best practices favor validating tokens securely and consistently, which Lambda authorizers enable for custom token validation.

answers.content: Integrate the company's third-party identity provider with AWS Directory ServicConfigure Directory Service as an API Gateway authorizer to validate tokens from the identity provider. Require the Directory Service authorizer on all API routes. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center as a SAML 2.0 identity Provider. Configure the web application as a custom SAML 2.0 application.
answers.explanation: AWS Directory Service cannot act as an authorizer for API Gateway HTTP APIs and is not designed for OAuth token validation.

answers.content: Integrate the company’s third-party identity provider with AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure API Gateway to use IAM Identity Center for zero-configuration authentication and authorization. Update the web application to retrieve AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) tokens from IAM Identity Center and include the tokens in the Authorization header when calling the API Gateway HTTP API.
answers.explanation: IAM Identity Center integration is not a zero-configuration solution for external OAuth tokens and requires user federation setup; STS tokens are not retrieved this way for API Gateway authorization.

answers.content: Integrate the company’s third-party identity provider with AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure IAM users with permissions to call the API Gateway HTTP API. Update the web application to extract request parameters from the IAM users and include the parameters in the Authorization header when calling the API Gateway HTTP API.
answers.explanation: Using IAM users for application users and extracting request parameters is not aligned with OAuth token-based user authorization and does not follow best security practices.

questions.content: A company needs to optimize the cost of an AWS environment that contains multiple accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company conducted cost optimization activities 3 years ago and purchased Amazon EC2 Standard Reserved Instances that recently expired.  The company needs EC2 instances for 3 more years. Additionally, the company has deployed a new serverless workload.  Which strategy will provide the company with the MOST cost savings?

answers.content: Purchase the same Reserved Instances for an additional 3-year term with All Upfront payment. Purchase a 3-year Compute Savings Plan with All Upfront payment in the management account to cover any additional compute costs
answers.explanation: Savings Plans are recommended over Reserved Instances for cost optimization. A 3-year term with All Upfront payment provides the greatest cost savings. Purchasing a Compute Savings Plan at the management account level covers additional compute costs across the organization, supporting multiple accounts and services including serverless workloads. Combining Reserved Instances for predictable EC2 workloads and Savings Plans for flexibility aligns with best cost optimization strategies.

answers.content: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan with No Upfront payment in each member account. Use the Savings Plans recommendations in the AWS Cost Management console to choose the Compute Savings Plan.
answers.explanation: 1-year term with No Upfront payment is less cost-effective and buying in each member account increases management overhead.

answers.content: Purchase a 3-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with No Upfront payment in the management account to cover EC2 costs in each AWS Region. Purchase a 3-year Compute Savings Plan with No Upfront payment in the management account to cover any additional compute costs.
answers.explanation: Using both EC2 Instance and Compute Savings Plans simultaneously may be redundant and No Upfront payment limits maximum savings.

answers.content: Purchase a 3-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with All Upfront payment in each member account. Use the Savings Plans recommendations in the AWS Cost Management console to choose the EC2 Instance Savings Plan.
answers.explanation: Purchasing EC2 Instance Savings Plans in each member account increases complexity; management account purchase is preferred for organization-wide benefits.

questions.content: A media company has a 30-T8 repository of digital news videos. These videos are stored on tape in an on-premises tape library and referenced by a Media Asset Management (MAM) system. The company wants to enrich the metadata for these videos in an automated fashion and put them into a searchable catalog by using a MAM featurThe company must be able to search based on information in the video, such as objects, scenery items, or people’s faces. A catalog is available that contains faces of people who have appeared in the videos that include an image of each person. The company would like to migrate these videos to AWS.  The company has a high-speed AWS Direct Connect connection with AWS and would like to move the MAM solution video content directly from its current file system.  How can these requirements be met by using the LEAST amount of ongoing management overhead and causing MINIMAL disruption to the existing system?

answers.content: Set up an AWS Storage Gateway, file gateway appliance on-premises. Use the MAM solution to extract the videos from the current archive and push them into the file gateway. Use the catalog of faces to build a collection in Amazon Rekognition. Build an AWS Lambda function that invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Rekognition pull the video from the Amazon S3 files backing the file gateway, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway allows seamless integration with on-premises applications, enabling the MAM solution to push videos directly into S3 with minimal disruption and low management overhead. Amazon Rekognition provides a managed service to build face collections and analyze videos for metadata extraction without requiring custom infrastructure management. Using AWS Lambda to invoke Rekognition for processing videos stored in S3 (via file gateway) follows AWS best practices by leveraging managed services and serverless computThis approach avoids manual processing or complex custom pipelines and does not require re-architecting the MAM solution drastically.

answers.content: Set up an AWS Storage Gateway, tape gateway appliance on-premises. Use the MAM solution to extract the videos from the current archive and push them into the tape gateway. Use the catalog of faces to build a collection in Amazon Rekognition. Build an AWS Lambda function that invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Amazon Rekognition process the video in the tape gateway, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution.
answers.explanation: Tape gateway is designed for tape backups, not for live or frequent data access and processing; Rekognition cannot process videos directly in the tape gateway.

answers.content: Configure a video ingestion stream by using Amazon Kinesis Video Streams. Use the catalog of faces to build a collection in Amazon Rekognition. Stream the videos from the MAM solution into Kinesis Video Streams. Configure Amazon Rekognition to process the streamed videos. Then, use a stream consumer to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution. Configure the stream to store the videos in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Kinesis Video Streams is designed for real-time streaming input but would require significant re-architecture of the existing MAM solution to stream videos instead of file-based access.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon EC2 instance that runs the OpenCV libraries. Copy the videos, images, and face catalog from the on-premises library into an Amazon EBS volume mounted on this EC2 instancProcess the videos to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution, while also copying the video files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Running OpenCV on EC2 requires heavy management, custom processing, and does not leverage AWS managed AI services, increasing operational overhead and security risk.

questions.content: A company hosts a data-processing application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application polls an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for newly uploaded files. When a new file is detected, the application extracts data from the file and runs logic to select a Docker container image to process the filThe application starts the appropriate container image and passes the file location as a parameter.  The data processing that the container performs can take up to 2 hours. When the processing is complete, the code that runs inside the container writes the file back to Amazon EFS and exits.  The company needs to refactor the application to eliminate the EC2 instances that are running the containers.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Configure the processing to run as AWS Fargate tasks. Extract the container selection logic to run as an Amazon EventBridge rule that starts the appropriate Fargate task. Configure the EventBridge rule to run when files are added to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS does not support native event notifications to trigger EventBridge rules, so triggering Fargate tasks this way is not feasible.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Configure the processing to run as AWS Fargate tasks. Update and containerize the container selection logic to run as a Fargate service that starts the appropriate Fargate task. Configure an EFS event notification to invoke the Fargate service when files are added to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: EFS event notifications are not supported, so invoking a Fargate service on EFS file addition is not possible.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Configure the processing to run as AWS Fargate tasks. Extract the container selection logic to run as an AWS Lambda function that starts the appropriate Fargate task. Migrate the storage of file uploads to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the processing code to use Amazon S3. Configure an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when objects are created.
answers.explanation: Migrating file storage to Amazon S3 aligns with AWS best practices for event notifications and triggering processing workflows. Using S3 event notifications to invoke a Lambda function that selects and starts Fargate tasks removes the need for EC2 instances and supports long-running processing by FargatAWS Lambda integrated with Amazon ECS Fargate provides a managed, serverless approach eliminating EC2 infrastructurThis solution follows the preference for managed AWS services, leveraging Amazon S3 for storage and event triggering, which is more practical than triggering directly on EFS, as EFS event notifications are not natively supported.

answers.content: Create AWS Lambda container images for the processing. Configure Lambda functions to use the container images. Extract the container selection logic to run as a decision Lambda function that invokes the appropriate Lambda processing function. Migrate the storage of file uploads to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the processing code to use Amazon S3. Configure an S3 event notification to invoke the decision Lambda function when objects are created.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda has a maximum execution time limit of 15 minutes, which is insufficient for 2-hour processing tasks.

questions.content: A company has deployed applications to thousands of Amazon EC2 instances in an AWS account. A security audit discovers that several unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes are attached to the EC2 instances. The company’s security policy requires the EBS volumes to be encrypted.  The company needs to implement an automated solution to encrypt the EBS volumes. The solution also must prevent development teams from creating unencrypted EBS volumes.  Which solution will meet these requirements?
