answers.content: Configure the AWS Config managed rule that identifies unencrypted EBS volumes. Configure an automatic remediation action. Associate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volumCreate an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. In the key policy, include a statement to deny the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
answers.explanation: The key policy cannot be relied upon to prevent creation of unencrypted EBS volumes; account settings provide a more reliable enforcement.

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager Fleet Manager to create a list of unencrypted EBS volumes, Create a Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volumCreate an SCP to deny the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
answers.explanation: Adds complexity by using Fleet Manager unnecessarily; also SCPs cannot prevent unencrypted volume creation as effectively as account-level encryption settings.

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager Fleet Manager to create a list of unencrypted EBS volumes. Create a Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volumModify the AWS account setting for EBS encryption to always encrypt new EBS volumes.
answers.explanation: Fleet Manager is unnecessary; does not include AWS Config for identifying existing unencrypted volumes and their automatic remediation.

answers.content: Configure the AWS Config managed rule that identifies unencrypted EBS volumes. Configure an automatic remediation action. Associate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volumModify the AWS account setting for EBS encryption to always encrypt new EBS volumes.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Config managed rules allows identification and automatic remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes, as required to fix existing instances. An automatic remediation action with an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook can automate creation of new encrypted volumes, meeting automation needs. Modifying the AWS account setting for EBS encryption to always encrypt new volumes prevents development teams from creating unencrypted EBS volumes, enforcing the policy proactively. This solution uses managed AWS services and follows security best practices by encrypting all EBS volumes and implementing automatic remediation.

questions.content: A company is migrating its data center to the AWS Cloud and needs to complete the migration as quickly as possiblThe company has many applications that are running on hundreds of VMware VMs in the data center. Each VM is configured with a shared Windows folder that contains common shared files. The file share is larger than 100 GB in siz The company’s compliance team requires a change request to be fled and approved for every software installation and modification to each VM. The company has an AWS Direct Connect connection with 10 GB of bandwidth between AWS and the data center.  Which set of steps should the company take to complete the migration in the LEAST amount of time?

answers.content: Use VM ImporvExport to create images of each VM. Use AWS Application Migration Service to manage and view the images. Copy the Windows file share data to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. After migration, remap the file share to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Using VM Import/Export and AWS Application Migration Service is the preferred managed service-based way to migrate hundreds of VMware VMs quickly. Copying the Windows file share data to Amazon EFS allows for scalable, shared storage that can replace the on-premises shared folder during migration. AWS Application Migration Service supports migrating VMs without requiring agent installation on each VM, aligning with minimizing changes for compliancAmazon EFS supports large shared file systems and can be remapped post-migration, fitting the requirement to maintain large shared files. Options involving agent installation on each VM or hypervisor or using Snowcone add complexity or delay, conflicting with the requirement to complete migration quickly.

answers.content: Deploy the AWS Application Discovery Service agentless appliance to VMware vCenter. Review the portfolio of discovered VMs in AWS Migration Hub.
answers.explanation: Only discovers VMs and reviews portfolio but does not address migration or file share handling.

answers.content: Deploy the AWS Application Migration Service agentless appliance to VMware vCenter. Copy the Windows file share data to a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. After migration, remap the file share on each VM to the FSx for Windows File Server file system. C. Create and review a portfolio in AWS Migration Hub. Order an AWS Snowcone devicDeploy AWS Application Migration Service to VMware vCenter and export all the VMs to the Snowcone devicCopy all Windows file share data to the Snowcone devicShip the Snowcone device to AWS. Use Application Migration Service to deploy all the migrated instances.
answers.explanation: Involves Snowcone which adds shipping delay and complexity, not the fastest method.

answers.content: Deploy the AWS Application Discovery Service Agent and the AWS Application Migration Service Agent onto each VMware hypervisor directly. Review the portfolio in AWS Migration Hub. Copy each VM’s file share data to a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. After migration, remap the file share on each VM to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
answers.explanation: Requires deploying agents on hypervisors which the compliance team restricts (software installation requires change requests), slowing migration.

questions.content: A company operates a static content distribution platform that serves customers globally. The customers consume content from their own AWS accounts.  The company serves its content from an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uploads the content from its on-premises environment to the S3 bucket by using an S3 File Gateway.  The company wants to improve the platform’s performance and reliability by serving content from the AWS Region that is geographically closest to customers. The company must route the on-premises data to Amazon S3 with minimal latency and without public internet exposur Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Implement S3 Multi-Region Access Points
answers.explanation: S3 Multi-Region Access Points (MRAPs) are designed to improve performance and reliability for multi-Region applications by dynamically routing requests to the nearest bucket via the AWS Global Accelerator network, reducing latency (Source 2). This directly addresses the requirement to serve content from the AWS Region geographically closest to customers with minimal operational overhead (Source 1).

answers.content: Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to copy content to different Regions
answers.explanation: Cross-Region Replication adds operational complexity and does not directly address minimal latency routing from on-premises to S3 or avoid public internet exposure.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function that tracks the routing of clients to Regions
answers.explanation: Creating a custom Lambda function for client routing increases operational overhead and is not a managed solution for performance and reliability.

answers.content: Use an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to connect to a Multi-Region Access Point.
answers.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not integrate directly with Multi-Region Access Points and may not provide minimal latency or avoid public internet exposure as effectively as PrivateLink and Direct Connect.

answers.content: Use AWS PrivateLink and AWS Direct Connect to connect to a Multi-Region Access Point.
answers.explanation:
The requirement is to route on-premises data (uploaded via S3 File Gateway) to Amazon S3 with minimal latency and without public internet exposure.
AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated, private network connection from the on-premises environment to AWS (Source 3, 4), satisfying the "without public internet exposure" and "minimal latency" requirements for the on-premises upload.
AWS PrivateLink facilitates private connectivity to AWS services, including Multi-Region Access Points, using private IP addresses within a VPC (Source 3). This ensures the traffic remains on the private AWS network after reaching the edge location via Direct Connect, maintaining the private connection path to the MRAP.

questions.content: A company wants to create a single Amazon S3 bucket for its data scientists to store work-related documents. The company uses AWS IAM Identity Center to authenticate all users. A group for the data scientists was created.  The company wants to give the data scientists access to only their own work. The company also wants to create monthly reports that show which documents each user accessed.  Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a custom IAM Identity Center permission set to grant the data scientists access to an S3 bucket prefix that matches their username tag. Use a policy to limit access to paths with the ${aws:PrincipalTag/userName}/* condition.
answers.explanation: Create a custom IAM Identity Center permission set to grant the data scientists access to an S3 bucket prefix that matches their username tag. Use a policy to limit access to paths with the ${aws:PrincipalTag/userName}/\* condition. This step addresses the requirement to "give the data scientists access to only their own work." When users authenticate via IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO), AWS can pass attributes (like their username) as principal tags. By creating a permission set with a policy that uses the ${aws:PrincipalTag/userName} condition key, you can enforce fine-grained access control (FGAC) to ensure a user can only access the S3 prefix path matching their specific username (e.g., s3://bucket-name/jane.doe/\*). Chose C: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 data events and deliver the logs to an S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run queries on the CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3 and generate reports. This step addresses the requirement to "create monthly reports that show which documents each user accessed." S3 data events (GetObject, PutObject, etc.) logged by CloudTrail capture user identity, time, and the resource accessed, making them ideal for auditing and reporting on document access. Amazon Athena is an excellent tool for querying large amounts of structured data directly in S3, such as CloudTrail logs, to generate the required monthly reports.

answers.content: Create an IAM Identity Center role for the data scientists group that has Amazon S3 read access and write access. Add an S3 bucket policy that allows access to the IAM Identity Center role.
answers.explanation: This option allows all members of the Data Scientists group to access the entire S3 bucket, violating the requirement to give data scientists access to *only their own work*. Using a single role for the group does not provide the fine-grained, user-specific access control required.

answers.content: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 data events and deliver the logs to an S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run queries on the CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3 and generate reports.
answers.explanation: This step addresses the requirement to "create monthly reports that show which documents each user accessed." S3 data events (GetObject, PutObject, etc.) logged by CloudTrail capture user identity, time, and the resource accessed, making them ideal for auditing and reporting on document access. Amazon Athena is an excellent tool for querying large amounts of structured data directly in S3, such as CloudTrail logs, to generate the required monthly reports.

answers.content: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 management events to CloudWatch. Use Amazon Athena’s CloudWatch connector to query the logs and generate reports.
answers.explanation: S3 management events track operations on the bucket itself (e.g., CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, modifying policies), not object-level data access (GetObject, PutObject). To report on which *documents* each user accessed, S3 *data events* must be logged. While CloudTrail can deliver logs to CloudWatch, querying large volumes of logs for reporting purposes is typically more efficient and cost-effective using Athena directly on logs stored in S3 (as described in option C).

answers.content: Enable S3 access logging to EMR File System (EMRFS). Use Amazon S3 Select to query logs and generate reports.
answers.explanation: S3 Access Logs are an alternative logging method to CloudTrail, but they are generally less reliable and lack the detailed identity information (like PrincipalTags) that CloudTrail data events provide, making detailed auditing potentially difficult. Furthermore, EMRFS is a component of Amazon EMR for interacting with S3, and enabling S3 access logging *to EMRFS* is not the standard or efficient solution for storing and querying access logs. S3 Select is designed for querying data within objects, not primarily for large-scale analytical reporting on log files. CloudTrail and Athena (Option C) provide the standard, scalable, and effective solution for this reporting requirement.

questions.content: A company is using a single AWS Region for its ecommerce websitThe website includes a web application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website also includes an Amazon DynamoDB tablA custom domain name in Amazon Route 53 is linked to the ALB. The company created an SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) and attached the certificate to the ALB. The company is not using a content delivery network as part of its design.  The company wants to replicate its entire application stack in a second Region to provide disaster recovery, plan for future growth, and provide improved access time to users. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that achieves these goals and minimizes administrative overhead.  Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create an AWS CloudFormation template for the current infrastructure design. Use parameters for important system values, including Region. Use the CloudFormation template to create the new infrastructure in the second Region.
answers.explanation: This step addresses the goal of minimizing administrative overhead and replicating the entire application stack. Using AWS CloudFormation (or StackSets for multi-Region deployment) allows for Infrastructure as Code (IaC), ensuring the infrastructure in the second Region is an exact, consistent replica of the first. This is a best practice for disaster recovery and expansion.

answers.content: Use the AWS Management Console to document the existing infrastructure design in the first Region and to create the new infrastructure in the second Region.
answers.explanation: Manually documenting and recreating infrastructure using the console increases administrative overhead and risks inconsistency; it does not minimize overhead as required.

answers.content: Update the Route 53 hosted zone record for the application to use weighted routing. Send 50% of the traffic to the ALB in each Region.
answers.explanation: Weighted routing splits traffic regardless of latency or user proximity, which may not improve access times and does not align with the goal of improved user experience.

answers.content: Update the Route 53 hosted zone record for the application to use latency-based routing. Send traffic to the ALB in each Region.
answers.explanation: Latency-based routing (LBR) in Amazon Route 53 is the best option to achieve "improved access time to users." LBR directs users to the AWS Region that provides the lowest latency (fastest response time) from their geographical location. This is crucial for performance optimization in a multi-Region setup. (Reference: Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53 - AWS Documentation)

answers.content: Update the configuration of the existing DynamoDB table by enabling DynamoDB Streams. Add the second Region to create a global table.
answers.explanation: To replicate the DynamoDB table and data across Regions for disaster recovery and improved access time, the DynamoDB Global Tables feature is the appropriate solution. Global tables use DynamoDB Streams for multi-Region, multi-active replication, ensuring the data is highly available and close to users, meeting both the disaster recovery and improved access time goals. (Reference: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables - AWS)

questions.content: A company has an application that uses Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The quality assurance (QA) department needs to launch a large number of short-lived environments to test the application. The application environments are currently launched by the manager of the department using an AWS CloudFormation templatTo launch the stack, the manager uses a role with permission to use CloudFormation, EC2, and Auto Scaling APIs. The manager wants to allow testers to launch their own environments, but does not want to grant broad permissions to each user.  Which set up would achieve these goals?

answers.content: Upload the AWS CloudFormation template to Amazon S3. Give users in the QA department permission to assume the manager’s role and add a policy that restricts the permissions to the template and the resources it creates. Train users to launch the template from the CloudFormation console.
answers.explanation: Granting users the ability to assume the manager’s role is overly broad and less secure than using Service Catalog launch constraints.

answers.content: Create an AWS Service Catalog product from the environment templatAdd a launch constraint to the product with the existing rolGive users in the QA department permission to use AWS Service Catalog APIs only. Train users to launch the template from the AWS Service Catalog console.
answers.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows creation of products from CloudFormation templates with launch constraints that use an existing role, providing controlled permissions. Giving testers AWS Service Catalog API permissions limits their access scope securely, avoiding broad permissions. This approach aligns with security best practices by restricting user permissions and using managed services for environment provisioning.

answers.content: Upload the AWS CloudFormation template to Amazon S3. Give users in the QA department permission to use CloudFormation and S3 APIs, with conditions that restrict the permissions to the template and the resources it creates. Train users to launch the template from the CloudFormation console.
answers.explanation: Giving direct CloudFormation and S3 permissions increases risk due to broader access and less control compared to using Service Catalog.

answers.content: Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application from the environment templatGive users in the QA department permission to use Elastic Beanstalk permissions only. Train users to launch Elastic Beanstalk environments with the Elastic Beanstalk CLI, passing the existing role to the environment as a service role.
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is not designed for launching arbitrary CloudFormation templates and may not support the existing environment setup.

questions.content: An entertainment company hosts a ticketing service on a fleet of Linux Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The ticketing service uses a pricing filThe pricing file is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has S3 Standard storagA central pricing solution that is hosted by a third party updates the pricing fil The pricing file is updated every 1-15 minutes and has several thousand line items. The pricing file is downloaded to each EC2 instance when the instance launches.  The EC2 instances occasionally use outdated pricing information that can result in incorrect charges for customers.  Which solution will resolve this problem MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function to update an Amazon DynamoDB table with new prices each time the pricing file is updated. Update the ticketing service to use DynramoDB to look up pricing
answers.explanation: Using AWS Lambda to update an Amazon DynamoDB table with new pricing data ensures that the pricing information is centralized and updated frequently and consistently. The ticketing service can query DynamoDB in real-time, preventing the use of outdated pricing data without needing to rely on local file copies. DynamoDB is a managed, scalable database service that can cost-effectively handle thousands of pricing line items with low latency. This approach eliminates complexity and synchronization issues associated with sharing files across instances and ensures that all instances use the latest pricing.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function to update an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file share with the pricing file each time the file is updated. Update the ticketing service to use Amazon EFS to access the pricing file.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is more expensive and complex compared to DynamoDB and may introduce latency; it is not the most cost-effective or simplest solution.

answers.content: Load Mountpoint for Amazon S3 onto the AMI of the EC2 instances. Configure Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to mount the S3 bucket that contains the pricing filUpdate the ticketing service to point to the mount point and path to access the $3 object,
answers.explanation: Mounting S3 as a file system is not an AWS-managed service and can cause latency and consistency problems; it is not a best practice for frequent updates.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumUse EBS Multi-Attach to attach the volume to every EC2 instancWhen a new EC2 instance launches, configure the new instance to update the pricing file on the EBS volumUpdate the ticketing service to point to the new local source.
answers.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach has limitations and is not designed for sharing frequently updated files across multiple instances, making it unreliable and complex.

questions.content: A company creates an Amazon API Gateway API and shares the API with an external development team. The API uses AWS Lambda functions and is deployed to a stage that is named Production.  The external development team is the sole consumer of the API. The API experiences sudden increases of usage at specific times, leading to concerns about increased costs. The company needs to limit cost and usage without reworking the Lambda functions.  Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Configure the API to send requests to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues instead of directly to the Lambda functions. Update the Lambda functions to consume messages from the queues and to process the requests. Set up the queues to invoke the Lambda functions when new messages arrive.
answers.explanation: Requires changing Lambda functions to consume from SQS, violating the 'without reworking Lambda functions' requirement.

answers.content: Configure provisioned concurrency for each Lambda function. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to register the Lambda functions as targets. Set up scaling schedules to increase and decrease capacity to match changes in API usage.
answers.explanation: Provisioned concurrency and Application Auto Scaling increase costs and complexity without directly limiting usage or costs.

answers.content: Create an API Gateway API key and an AWS WAF Regional web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the Production stagAdd a rate-based rule to the web ACL. In the rule, specify the rate limit and a custom request aggregation that uses the X-API-Key header. Share the API key with the external development team.
answers.explanation: Using AWS WAF rate-based rules with custom aggregation based on X-API-Key is less straightforward and less directly integrated for cost and usage control compared to usage plans.

answers.content: Create an API Gateway API Key and usage plan. Define throttling limits and quotas in the usage plan. Associate the usage plan with the Production stage and the API key. Share the API key with the external development team.
answers.explanation: API Gateway usage plans with API keys allow defining throttling limits and quotas directly, which control usage and costs effectively without changing Lambda functions. This method does not require reworking Lambda functions or deploying additional services, making it cost-effective and aligned with best practices. Using API Gateway's built-in usage plans and API keys is a managed AWS service feature designed for controlling API usagOther options either involve reworking Lambda functions, managing more complex scaling setups, or less direct cost control mechanisms.

questions.content: A company is migrating its on-premises IoT platform to AWS. The platform consists of the following components:  • A MongoDB cluster as a data store for all collected and processed IoT data. • An application that uses Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to connect to IoT devices every 5 minutes to collect data. • An application that runs jobs periodically to generate reports from the IoT data. The jobs take 120-600 seconds to finish running. • A web application that runs on a web server. End users use the web application to generate reports that are accessible to the general public.  The company needs to migrate the platform to AWS to reduce operational overhead while maintaining performanc Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create AWS Step Functions state machines with AWS Lambda tasks to prepare the reports and to write the reports to Amazon S3. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has an S3 origin to serve the reports
answers.explanation: Rationale: The application runs jobs periodically to generate reports, and these jobs take 120-600 seconds to finish. This duration exceeds the current maximum timeout for standard AWS Lambda functions (15 minutes or 900 seconds), but using Step Functions to orchestrate Lambda functions is a common pattern for managing long-running, multi-step workflows. This solution provides a serverless approach for the reporting process, reducing operational overhead compared to managing EC2 instances. Serving the final reports through CloudFront with an S3 origin is a highly scalable, low-overhead way to make reports publicly accessible (static website hosting via S3 and content delivery network via CloudFront).

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to connect to the IoT devices. process the data, and write the data to the data storConfigure a Lambda layer to temporarily store messages for processing.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because directly programming Lambda to connect to IoT devices disregards AWS managed IoT Core, increasing complexity and overhead.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with Amazon EC2 instances to prepare the reports. Create an ingress controller on the EKS cluster to serve the reports.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EKS and EC2 increases operational overhead and management complexity, contrary to requirements.

answers.content: Connect the IoT devices to AWS IoT Core to publish messages. Create an AWS IoT rule that runs when a message is received. Configure the rule to call an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to parse, transform, and store device message data to the data store.
answers.explanation: Rationale: The existing application uses MQTT to connect to IoT devices every 5 minutes to collect data. AWS IoT Core is the managed service designed for connecting IoT devices using protocols like MQTT, offering the lowest operational overhead for device connectivity and message ingestion. AWS IoT rules can then easily trigger a Lambda function to handle the processing and storage of the data, migrating the on-premises MQTT application to a fully managed, serverless architecture.

answers.content: Migrate the MongoDB cluster to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility).
answers.explanation: Rationale: The platform uses a MongoDB cluster as a data store. Amazon DocumentDB is AWS's fully managed, scalable, and highly durable document database service compatible with MongoDB. Migrating to DocumentDB significantly reduces the operational overhead associated with managing the MongoDB cluster (such as patching, backups, and scaling) while maintaining application compatibility.

questions.content: A company plans to migrate a legacy on-premises application to AWS. The application is a Java web application that runs on Apache Tomcat with a PostgreSQL databas The company does not have access to the source code but can deploy the application Java Archive (JAR) files. The application has increased traffic at the end of each month.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Deploy Tomcat and PostgreSQL to all the instances by using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) mount points. Use AWS Step Functions to deploy additional EC2 instances to scale for increased traffic.
answers.explanation: Requires manual deployment of Tomcat and PostgreSQL on EC2 and EFS, increasing operational overhead and complexity.

answers.content: Provision Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AWS Regions. Deploy Tomcat and PostgreSQL in the container images. Use a Network Load Balancer to scale for increased traffic.
answers.explanation: Provisioning Amazon EKS across multiple Regions and managing containers for both application and database increases complexity and operational overhead without source code access benefit.

answers.content: Refactor the Java application into Python-based containers. Use AWS Lambda functions for the application logic. Store application data in Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Use AWS Storage Gateway and Lambda concurrency to scale for increased traffic.
answers.explanation: Refactoring application to Python Lambda functions is not possible without source code access and involves a major rewrite, which is not feasible.

answers.content: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the Tomcat servers with auto scaling in multiple Availability Zones. Store application data in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databasDeploy Amazon CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer to scale for increased traffic.
answers.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a managed service that reduces operational overhead by handling deployment, capacity provisioning, load balancing, and auto scaling. Elastic Beanstalk supports deploying Java web applications with Apache Tomcat, matching the application's environment without needing source code changes. Using Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL provides a managed, highly available database service, reducing overhead compared to managing PostgreSQL on EC2 instances. Deploying in multiple Availability Zones with Elastic Beanstalk and RDS ensures high availability and scalable handling of increased traffic. This approach aligns with AWS best practices to use managed services and minimize operational overhead, especially when source code is unavailable for refactoring.

questions.content: A company runs a web application on a single Amazon EC2 instancEnd users experience slow application performance during times of peak usage, when CPU utilization is consistently more than 95%.  A user data script installs required custom packages on the EC2 instancThe process of launching the instance takes several minutes.  The company is creating an Auto Scaling group that has mixed instance groups, varied CPUs, and a maximum capacity limit. The Auto Scaling group will use a launch template for various configuration options. The company needs to decrease application latency when new instances are launched during auto scaling.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use a predictive scaling policy. Use an instance maintenance policy to run the user data script. Set the default instance warmup time to 0 seconds.
answers.explanation: Setting warmup time to 0 seconds disregards the initialization delay; no use of warm pools to reduce latency.

answers.content: Use a dynamic scaling policy. Use lifecycle hooks to run the user data script. Set the default instance warmup time to 0 seconds.
answers.explanation: Setting warmup time to 0 seconds is not best practice; lifecycle hooks are used but no warm pools to pre-launch instances.

answers.content: Use a predictive scaling policy. Enable warm pools for the Auto Scaling group. Use an instance maintenance policy to run the user data script.
answers.explanation: Predictive scaling is less suitable than dynamic scaling for immediate CPU spikes; instance maintenance policy is deprecated compared to lifecycle hooks.

answers.content: Use a dynamic scaling policy. Enable warm pools for the Auto Scaling group. Use lifecycle hooks to run the user data script.
answers.explanation: Dynamic scaling policies are recommended for real-time responsiveness to CPU utilization changes. Lifecycle hooks allow running initialization scripts such as user data in a controlled manner during instance launch. Enabling warm pools helps reduce latency when new instances are launched by pre-provisioning instances. Setting instance warmup time to 0 seconds is not recommended since it ignores the initialization period; warm pools address warmup more effectively.

questions.content: Accompany runs an application on Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda. The application stores temporary data in Amazon S3. The S3 objects are deleted after 24 hours.  The company deploys new versions of the application by launching AWS CloudFormation stacks. The stacks create the required resources. After validating a new version, the company deletes the old stack. The deletion of an old development stack recently failed. A solutions architect needs to resolve this issue without major architecture changes.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a Lambda function to delete objects from an S3 bucket. Add the Lambda function as a custom resource in the CloudFormation stack with a DependsOn attribute that points to the S3 bucket resource.
answers.explanation: Deleting objects from the S3 bucket before deleting the CloudFormation stack prevents deletion failures caused by non-empty buckets. Using a Lambda-backed custom resource in the CloudFormation stack to clean up S3 objects automates this process as part of stack deletion. This approach resolves the deletion failure without major architecture changes, aligning with the requirement. Options involving DeletionPolicy attributes do not address deletion failures due to objects in the bucket. Switching to Amazon EFS introduces major architectural changes and is not necessary.

answers.content: Modify the CloudFormation stack to attach a DeletionPolicy attribute with a value of Delete to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: The Delete DeletionPolicy does not remove existing objects causing deletion failure in S3 buckets.

answers.content: Update the CloudFormation stack to add a DeletionPolicy attribute with a value of Snapshot for the S3 bucket resource
answers.explanation: The Snapshot DeletionPolicy is not applicable to S3 buckets and does not resolve deletion failures.

answers.content: Update the CloudFormation template to create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store temporary files instead of Amazon S3. Configure the Lambda functions to run in the same VPC as the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Switching to Amazon EFS is a major architecture change, which the question prohibits.

questions.content: A company stores and manages documents in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The file system is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. The file system is mounted to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs proprietary softwar The company has enabled automatic backups for the file system. The automatic backups use the AWS Backup default backup plan.  A solutions architect must ensure that deleted documents can be recovered within an RPO of 100 minutes.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new IAM rolCreate a new backup plan. Use the new IAM role to create backups. Update the KMS key policy to allow the new IAM role to use the key. Implement an hourly backup schedule for the file system.
answers.explanation: Creating a new IAM role and backup plan adds unnecessary complexity and the hourly backup schedule is too infrequent for the 100-minute RPO.

answers.content: Create a new backup plan. Update the KMS key policy to allow the AWSServiceRoleForBackup IAM role to use the key. Implement a custom cron expression to run a backup of the file system every 30 minutes.
answers.explanation: To meet an RPO of 100 minutes, backups must occur at least every 30 minutes, which requires a custom backup schedule more frequent than the default plan. Updating the KMS key policy to allow the AWSServiceRoleForBackup IAM role ensures the backup service can access encrypted backups. Using the AWSServiceRoleForBackup aligns with managed AWS service best practices and leverages AWS Backup capabilities. Creating a custom cron expression for backup frequency fits the requirement to reduce data loss impact.

answers.content: Create a new IAM rolUse the existing backup plan. Update the KMS key policy to allow the new IAM role to use the key. Enable continuous backups for point-in-time recovery.
answers.explanation: Enabling continuous backups is not applicable to EFS backups and creating a new IAM role is unnecessary when the AWSServiceRoleForBackup role can be used.

answers.content: Use the existing backup plan. Update the KMS key policy to allow the AWSServiceRoleForBackup IAM role to use the key. Enable Cross-Region Replication for the file system.
answers.explanation: Cross-Region Replication does not address the RPO of 100 minutes or backup frequency and may not be supported for EFS backups.

questions.content: A company needs to modernize an application and migrate the application to AWS. The application stores user profile data as text in a single table in an on-premises MySQL databas After the modernization, users will use the application to upload video files that are up to 4 GB in sizOther users must be able to download the video files from the application. The company needs a video storage solution that provides rapid scaling. The solution must not affect application performanc Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Store the videos as base64-encoded strings in a TEXT column in the database.
answers.explanation: Storing large videos as base64-encoded strings in an Amazon Aurora database is inefficient, costly, and impacts performance.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Store the videos as objects in Amazon S3. Store the S3 key in the corresponding DynamoDB item.
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database service suitable for storing application metadata with rapid scaling. Storing large video files (up to 4 GB) directly in the database as base64-encoded strings is not efficient and would impact performancAmazon S3 is designed for scalable object storage, ideal for large files like videos, without affecting database or application performancStoring the S3 key in DynamoDB allows efficient retrieval of metadata while keeping large objects in S3. AWS Database Migration Service and AWS Schema Conversion Tool facilitate migration and modernization to DynamoDB.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Store the videos as objects in Amazon S3. Store the S3 object identifier in the corresponding Amazon Keyspaces entry.
answers.explanation: Amazon Keyspaces is less common and adds complexity without clear advantage compared to DynamoDB; DynamoDB is preferred for rapid scaling and seamless integration.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Store the videos as base64-encoded strings in the corresponding DynamoDB item.
answers.explanation: Storing large videos as base64-encoded strings in DynamoDB is inefficient and can degrade performance; S3 is the preferred storage for large files.

questions.content: A company needs to migrate 60 on-premises legacy applications to AWS. The applications are based on the NET Framework and run on Windows.  The company needs a solution that minimizes migration time and requires no application code changes. The company also does not want to manage the infrastructur Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Refactor the applications and containerize them by using AWS Toolkit for NET Refactoring. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch type to host the containerized applications.
answers.explanation: Refactoring and containerization is time-consuming and contradicts the requirement of no code changes.

answers.content: Use the Windows Web Application Migration Assistant to migrate the applications to AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Use Elastic Beanstalk to deploy and manage the applications.
answers.explanation: Refactoring involves modernizing the application and is not recommended for large migrations, so options A and D are not suitablUsing EC2 instances requires managing infrastructure, which does not meet the requirement of no infrastructure management (eliminates option C). AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a managed service that supports Windows and .NET applications and minimizes migration time with no code changes, matching the requirements well. The Windows Web Application Migration Assistant helps migrate applications to Elastic Beanstalk, fulfilling the requirement to avoid code changes and infrastructure management.

answers.content: Use the Windows Web Application Migration Assistant to migrate the applications to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the EC2 instances to deploy and manage the applications.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances requires managing the infrastructure, which is against the requirement.

answers.content: Refactor the applications and containerize them by using AWS Toolkit for NET Refactoring. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with the Fargate launch type to host the containerized applications.
answers.explanation: Refactoring and containerizing with EKS involves code changes and infrastructure management, which is not preferred.

questions.content: A company is designing an AWS environment for a manufacturing application. The application has been successful with customers, and the application's user base has increased. The company has connected the AWS environment to the company's on-premises data center through a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company has configured BGP for the connection.  The company must update the existing network connectivity solution to ensure that the solution is highly available, fault tolerant, and secur Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Add a dynamic private IP AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a secondary path to secure data in transit and provide resilience for the Direct Connect connection. Configure MACsec to encrypt traffic inside the Direct Connect connection.
answers.explanation: Adding a dynamic private IP AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a secondary path provides resilience and secure data in transit. AWS Site-to-Site VPN automatically encrypts data, ensuring security without requiring additional encryption like MACsec. Using a VPN as a backup to Direct Connect is a cost-effective way to ensure high availability and fault tolerancConfiguring MACsec on Direct Connect is not commonly available or recommended as the primary encryption method; VPN provides encryption by default.

answers.content: Provision another Direct Connect connection between the company's on-premises data center and AWS to increase the transfer speed and provide resiliencConfigure MACsec to encrypt traffic inside the Direct Connect connection.
answers.explanation: Provisioning a second Direct Connect connection is more expensive and less cost-effective.

answers.content: Configure multiple private VIFs. Load balance data across the VIFs between the on-premises data center and AWS to provide resilience.
answers.explanation: Configuring multiple private VIFs does not inherently provide resilience or encryption and lacks load balancing capabilities over VIFs.

answers.content: Add a static AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a secondary path to secure data in transit and to provide resilience for the Direct Connect connection.
answers.explanation: A static VPN does not offer the dynamic routing benefits of a dynamic VPN and is less robust for failover.

questions.content: A company that has multiple business units is using AWS Organizations with all features enabled. The company has implemented an account structure in which each business unit has its own AWS account. Administrators in each AWS account need to view detailed cost and utilization data for their account by using Amazon Athena.  Each business unit can have access to only its own cost and utilization data. The IAM policies that govern the ability to set up AWS Cost and Usage Reports are in placA central Cost and Usage Report that contains all data for the organization is already available in an Amazon S3 bucket.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational complexity?

answers.content: In the organization's management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Cost and Usage Report data with each member account.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM does not support sharing S3 bucket data like Cost and Usage Reports, so this would not work.

answers.content: In the organization's management account, configure an S3 event to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a new file arrives in the S3 bucket that contains the central Cost and Usage Report. Configure the Lambda function to extract each member account’s data and to place the data in Amazon S3 under a separate prefix. Modify the S3 bucket policy to allow each member account to access its own prefix.
answers.explanation: Custom Lambda processing for data segregation adds significant operational complexity, which is against the requirement.

answers.content: In each member account, access AWS Cost Explorer. Create a new report that contains relevant cost information for the account. Save the report in Cost Explorer. Provide instructions that the account administrators can use to access the saved report.
answers.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer allows each member account to generate and view cost and utilization reports specific to their account. This method does not require complex data processing or sharing permissions across accounts and uses existing AWS services designed for cost reporting. Given that IAM policies to set up Cost and Usage Reports are in place, each account can generate their own reports conveniently. This approach aligns with least operational complexity by leveraging native AWS reporting tools without custom data extraction or cross-account sharing.

answers.content: In each member account, create a new S3 bucket to store Cost and Usage Report data. Set up a Cost and Usage Report to deliver the data to the new S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Setting up separate Cost and Usage Reports per account duplicates work and is unnecessary since centralized reporting exists, increasing complexity.

questions.content: A company needs to gather data from an experiment in a remote location that does not have internet connectivity. During the experiment, sensors that are connected to a local network will generate 6 TB of data in a proprietary format over the course of 1 week. The sensors can be configured to upload their data files to an FTP server periodically, but the sensors do not have their own FTP server. The sensors also do not support other protocols. The company needs to collect the data centrally and move the data to object storage in the AWS Cloud as soon as possible after the experiment.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devicConnect the device to the local network. Configure AWS DataSync with a target bucket name, and unload the data over NFS to the devicAfter the experiment, return the device to AWS so that the data can be loaded into Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync cannot unload data over NFS without an FTP server; sensors only support FTP, so this option is incompatible.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowcone device, including an Amazon Linux 2 AMI. Connect the device to the local network. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance on the devicCreate a shell script that periodically downloads data from each sensor. After the experiment, return the device to AWS so that the data can be loaded as an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume.
answers.explanation: Creating a custom shell script to download data is complex and not aligned with security best practices; also returning data as EBS volume is nonstandard for Snowcone.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowcone device, including an Amazon Linux 2 AMI. Connect the device to the local network. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance on the devicInstall and configure an FTP server on the EC2 instancConfigure the sensors to upload data to the EC2 instancAfter the experiment, return the device to AWS so that the data can be loaded into Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: The sensors only support uploading data via FTP and do not have their own FTP server, so a solution must include an FTP server. Using an AWS Snowcone device with Amazon Linux 2 AMI allows launching an EC2 instance to install and configure an FTP server, enabling sensors to upload data locally. Returning the Snowcone device after the experiment allows secure transfer of the accumulated data into Amazon S3. This approach uses a managed data transfer device (Snowcone) and managed instances (EC2 on Snowcone) without relying on unsupported protocols or unsecured manual copying. Other options either do not provide FTP server capability or suggest transferring data over unsupported protocols or configurations.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowcone devicConnect the device to the local network. Configure the device to use Amazon FSx. Configure the sensors to upload data to the devicConfigure AWS DataSync on the device to synchronize the uploaded data with an Amazon S3 bucket. Return the device to AWS so that the data can be loaded as an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx is not designed for FTP uploads, and configuring DataSync on the device to synchronize with S3 while handling FTP uploads is not feasible.

questions.content: A company is deploying a new web-based application and needs a storage solution for the Linux application servers. The company wants to create a single location for updates to application data for all instances. The active dataset will be up to 100 GB in sizA solutions architect has determined that peak operations will occur for 3 hours daily and will require a total of 225 MiBps of read throughput.  The solutions architect must design a Multi-AZ solution that makes a copy of the data available in another AWS Region for disaster recovery (DR). The DR copy has an RPO of less than 1 hour.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Deploy a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Multi-AZ file system. Configure the file system for 75 MiBps of provisioned throughput. Implement replication to a file system in the DR Region.
answers.explanation: EFS throughput provisioning of 75 MiBps is insufficient for the required 225 MiBps, and EFS does not natively support cross-Region replication.

answers.content: Deploy a new Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure Bursting Throughput mode for the file system. Use AWS Backup to back up the file system to the DR Region.
answers.explanation: FSx for Lustre in Bursting mode cannot guarantee the sustained throughput required, and AWS Backup typically does not provide RPO under 1 hour for DR.

answers.content: Deploy a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with 225 MiBps of throughput. Enable Multi-Attach for the EBS volumUse AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the EBS volume to the DR Region.
answers.explanation: Amazon EBS Multi-Attach supports Multi-AZ within a Region, not cross-Region; Elastic Disaster Recovery is recommended for SAP application layers but replication of the EBS volume cross-Region is not straightforward here.

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system in both the production Region and the DR Region. Create an AWS DataSync scheduled task to replicate the data from the production file system to the DR file system every 10 minutes.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS supports replicating data between Regions, suitable for multi-AZ and DR scenarios. Using AWS DataSync scheduled tasks to replicate every 10 minutes meets the RPO of less than 1 hour. Provisioned throughput must support the required read throughput of 225 MiBps; FSx for OpenZFS is designed for high throughput workloads and allows replication. This solution provides Multi-AZ availability and a DR copy in another Region without relying on backups that would not meet the RPO.

questions.content: A company used AWS CloudFormation to create all new infrastructure in its AWS member accounts. The resources rarely change and are properly sized for the expected load. The monthly AWS bill is consistent.  Occasionally, a developer creates a new resource for testing and forgets to remove the resource when the test is completMost of these tests last a few days before the resources are no longer needed.  The company wants to automate the process of finding unused resources. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that determines whether the cost in the AWS bill is increasing. The solution must help identify resources that cause an increase in cost and must automatically notify the company's operations team.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Turn on billing alerts. Use AWS Cost Explorer to determine the costs for the past month. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for total estimated charges. Specify a cost threshold that is higher than the costs that Cost Explorer determined. Add a notification to alert the operations team if the alarm threshold is breached.
answers.explanation: Uses billing alerts and a single month average which may not account for normal fluctuations or multi-account costs and lacks automated identification of specific resources causing cost increases.

answers.content: Turn on billing alerts. Use AWS Cost Explorer to determine the average monthly costs for the past 3 months. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for total estimated charges. Specify a cost threshold that is higher than the costs that Cost Explorer determined. Add a notification to alert the operations team if the alarm threshold is breached.
answers.explanation: Similar to A but uses 3 months average; still relies on billing alerts and threshold alarms without automated anomaly detection or per-resource insight.

answers.content: Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create a cost monitor that has a monitor type of Linked account. Create a subscription to send daily AWS cost summaries to the operations team. Specify a threshold for cost variance.
answers.explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection is designed to identify unusual cost patterns, helping to automatically detect increases in cost and the underlying resources causing them. Creating a cost monitor with 'Linked account' type allows tracking costs across member accounts in an AWS organization, matching the scenario of multiple member accounts. Sending daily cost summaries and setting thresholds for cost variance meets the requirement for automated notifications to the operations team when cost increases occur. This approach is more precise and automated than simple billing alerts and cost threshold alarms, providing actionable insights. Security best practices and managed AWS services are prioritized, and Cost Anomaly Detection is a managed AWS service for this purpose.

answers.content: Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create a cost monitor that has a monitor type of AWS services. Create a subscription to send daily AWS cost summaries to the operations team. Specify a threshold for cost variance.
answers.explanation: Monitor type 'AWS services' tracks anomalies by service but does not focus on linked accounts and may not pinpoint anomalies across member accounts as effectively as the 'Linked account' monitor type.

questions.content: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage its development environment. Each development team at the company has its own AWS account. Each account has a single VPC and CIDR blocks that do not overlap.  The company has an Amazon Aurora DB cluster in a shared services account. All the development teams need to work with live data from the DB cluster.  Which solution will provide the required connectivity to the DB cluster with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) resource share for the DB cluster. Share the DB cluster with all the development accounts.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM does not support sharing an Aurora DB cluster itself, so this option is invalid.

answers.content: Create a transit gateway in the shared services account. Create an AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) resource share for the transit gateway. Share the transit gateway with all the development accounts. Instruct the developers to accept the resource sharConfigure networking.
answers.explanation: Transit Gateway allows centralized, scalable, and manageable network connectivity between multiple VPCs across accounts within an AWS Organization, reducing operational complexity. Sharing the Transit Gateway with other accounts via AWS RAM is a managed AWS service approach, avoiding complex manual networking or VPN setups. Each development account can connect to the shared services account's VPC where the Aurora cluster resides without overlapping CIDRs causing complications. Options involving VPN or resource sharing mechanisms other than Transit Gateway lead to higher operational overhead or are not appropriate for network connectivity to Aurora.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that points to the IP address of the DB cluster. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the ALB. Add permissions to allow each development account to connect to the endpoint service.
answers.explanation: Creating an ALB and PrivateLink for a database endpoint is not a standard or supported method to connect to Aurora DB clusters and adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection in the shared services account. Configure networking. Use AWS Marketplace VPN software in each development account to connect to the Site-to-Site VPN connection.
answers.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN connections across multiple accounts increase operational overhead and complexity; not the least overhead.

questions.content: A company has an on-premises data center and is using Kubernetes to develop a new solution on AWS. The company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters for its development and test environments.  The EKS control plane and data plane for production workloads must reside on premises. The company needs an AWS managed solution for Kubernetes management.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Install an AWS Outposts server in the on-premises data center. Deploy Amazon EKS by using a local cluster configuration on the Outposts server for the production workloads.
answers.explanation: Deploying Amazon EKS using local cluster configuration on Outposts is not the standard managed on-premises approach and may increase operational overhead.

answers.content: Install Amazon EKS Anywhere on the company's hardware in the on-premises data center. Deploy the production workloads on an EKS Anywhere cluster.
answers.explanation: Amazon EKS Anywhere is an AWS managed solution for running Kubernetes clusters on-premises with minimal operational overhead. EKS Anywhere supports deployment on the company’s existing hardware without requiring AWS Outposts. This matches the requirement to have the EKS control plane and data plane on premises for production workloads. It is specifically designed to reduce operational overhead compared to manually managing Kubernetes clusters.

answers.content: Install an AWS Outposts server in the on-premises data center. Deploy Amazon EKS by using an extended cluster configuration on the Outposts server for the production workloads.
answers.explanation: Extended cluster configuration on Outposts is more complex and incurs more overhead than EKS Anywhere.

answers.content: Install an AWS Outposts server in the on-premises data center. Install Amazon EKS Anywhere on the Outposts server. Deploy the production workloads on an EKS Anywhere cluster.
answers.explanation: Installing EKS Anywhere on Outposts server adds unnecessary complexity compared to direct deployment on existing hardware with EKS Anywhere.

questions.content: A public retail web application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of Amazon EC2 instances running across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) in a Region backed by an Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ deployment. Target group health checks are configured to use HTTP and pointed at the product catalog pagAuto Scaling is configured to maintain the web fleet size based on the ALB health check.  Recently, the application experienced an outagAuto Scaling continuously replaced the instances during the outagA subsequent investigation determined that the web server metrics were within the normal range, but the database tier was experiencing high load, resulting in severely elevated query response times.  Which of the following changes together would remediate these issues while improving monitoring capabilities for the availability and functionality of the entire application stack for future growth? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Configure read replicas for Amazon RDS MySQL and use the single reader endpoint in the web application to reduce the load on the backend database tier.
answers.explanation: Using only the single reader endpoint with read replicas does not address write load issues or monitoring improvements directly.

answers.content: Configure the target group health check to point at a simple HTML page instead of a product catalog page and the Amazon Route 53 health check against the product page to evaluate full application functionality. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify administrators when the site fails.
answers.explanation: The Application Load Balancer (ALB) health check currently uses the product catalog page. This page relies on the database. When the database is overloaded, the health check fails, causing Auto Scaling to replace perfectly healthy web servers (as the web server metrics were normal). This is an example of a "shallow" health check causing cascading failures. Changing the target group health check to a simple HTML page makes the load balancer's decision about the EC2 instance health independent of the database load. This stops the continuous replacement of instances during a database outage. Additionally, configuring an Amazon Route 53 health check against the product page provides a "deep" health check that evaluates the full application functionality (including database connectivity) and can be used to notify administrators via Amazon CloudWatch alarms, improving monitoring capabilities for the entire stack's availability.Reference: (https://aws.github.io/aws-elb-best-practices/reliability/failure_management/) (Deep health checks Best Practice)

answers.content: Configure the target group health check to use a TCP check of the Amazon EC2 web server and the Amazon Route 53 health check against the product page to evaluate full application functionality. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify administrators when the site fails.
answers.explanation: TCP health checks do not validate full application functionality, reducing monitoring insight accuracy compared to HTTP checks on specific pages.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for Amazon RDS with an action to recover a high-load, impaired RDS instance in the database tier.
answers.explanation: Recovering an impaired RDS instance does not solve the root cause of high load and elevated query response times and does not improve future monitoring sufficiently.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon ElastiCache cluster and place it between the web application and RDS MySQL instances to reduce the load on the backend database tier.
answers.explanation: The root cause of the outage was a high load on the database tier leading to elevated query response times. Amazon ElastiCache (e.g., Redis or Memcached) is a highly effective solution for caching frequently accessed data, which significantly reduces the load on the backend Amazon RDS database. Placing an ElastiCache cluster between the web application and RDS MySQL instances addresses the performance issue and prevents future overloads, complementing the change in the health check mechanism.

questions.content: A flood monitoring agency has deployed more than 10,000 water-level monitoring sensors. Sensors send continuous data updates, and each update is less than 1 MB in sizThe agency has a fleet of on-premises application servers. These servers receive updates from the sensors, convert the raw data into a human readable format, and write the results to an on-premises relational database server. Data analysts then use simple SQL queries to monitor the data.  The agency wants to increase overall application availability and reduce the effort that is required to perform maintenance tasks. These maintenance tasks, which include updates and patches to the application servers, cause downtimWhile an application server is down, data is lost from sensors because the remaining servers cannot handle the entire workload.  The agency wants a solution that optimizes operational overhead and costs. A solutions architect recommends the use of AWS IoT Core to collect the sensor data.  What else should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Send the sensor data to Amazon Kinesis Data FirehosUse an AWS Lambda function to read the Kinesis Data Firehose data, convert it to .csv format, and insert it into an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instancInstruct the data analysts to query the data directly from the DB instance.
answers.explanation: Directly inserting into Aurora MySQL increases operational overhead and risk of downtime; using Firehose with Lambda is less optimal than managed Flink for transformation at scale.

answers.content: Send the sensor data to Amazon Kinesis Data FirehosUse an AWS Lambda function to read the Kinesis Data Firehose data, convert it to Apache Parquet format, and save it to an Amazon S3 bucket. Instruct the data analysts to query the data by using Amazon Athena.
answers.explanation: Lambda has limitations for continuous processing and scalability compared to Apache Flink; Firehose to S3 with Parquet and Athena is supported, but transformation with Flink is more robust.

answers.content: Send the sensor data to an Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) application to convert the data to .csv format and store it in an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the data into an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instancInstruct the data analysts to query the data directly from the DB instance.
answers.explanation: Importing transformed data into Aurora adds maintenance and availability risks of managing an RDS instance; querying directly from S3 with Athena is more operationally efficient.

answers.content: Send the sensor data to an Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) application to convert the data to Apache Parquet format and store it in an Amazon S3 bucket. Instruct the data analysts to query the data by using Amazon Athena.
answers.explanation: Using AWS IoT Core with an Apache Flink application allows scalable and reliable data processing and transformation in a managed service, reducing operational overhead and maintenance downtimStoring data in Apache Parquet format in Amazon S3 optimizes cost and performance for querying with Amazon Athena, a serverless query service, addressing the need for simple SQL queries by data analysts. This solution improves availability by decoupling ingestion and processing from on-premises infrastructure, eliminating downtime and data loss issues. Querying data using Athena on S3 is more cost-efficient and easier to maintain than managing an Aurora MySQL instance at scale.

questions.content: A company in the United States (US) has acquired a company in EuropBoth companies use the AWS Cloud. The US company has built a new application with a microservices architecturThe US company is hosting the application across five VPCs in the us-east-2 Region. The application must be able to access resources in one VPC in the eu-west-1 Region. However, the application must not be able to access any other VPCs.  The VPCs in both Regions have no overlapping CIDR ranges. All accounts are already consolidated in one organization in AWS Organizations.  Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Create one transit gateway in eu-west-1. Attach the VPCs in us-east-2 and the VPC in eu-west-1 to the transit gateway. Create the necessary route entries in each VPC so that the traffic is routed through the transit gateway.
answers.explanation: A transit gateway in eu-west-1 cannot attach VPCs in us-east-2; transit gateways cannot span regions.

answers.content: Create one transit gateway in each Region. Attach the involved subnets to the regional transit gateway. Create the necessary route entries in the associated route tables for each subnet so that the traffic is routed through the regional transit gateway. Peer the two transit gateways.
answers.explanation: While peering transit gateways is possible, this is more costly and complex than required for limited connections.

answers.content: Create a full mesh VPC peering connection configuration between all the VPCs. Create the necessary route entries in each VPC so that the traffic is routed through the VPC peering connection.
answers.explanation: A full mesh peering between all VPCs is unnecessarily complex and allows broader connectivity than required.

answers.content: Create one VPC peering connection for each VPC in us-east-2 to the VPC in eu-west-1. Create the necessary route entries in each VPC so that the traffic is routed through the VPC peering connection.
answers.explanation: VPC peering requires a direct peering connection between each pair of VPCs that must communicatThe application must access only one VPC in eu-west-1 from five VPCs in us-east-2 with no overlap in CIDRs. Creating one VPC peering connection from each us-east-2 VPC to the single eu-west-1 VPC meets the communication requirement without enabling access to other VPCs. Transit gateway solutions would be more expensive and enable broader connectivity, failing the requirement to restrict access only to the single eu-west-1 VPC. A full mesh peering would be excessively complex and unnecessary when only one destination VPC is needed.

questions.content: A company has several AWS Lambda functions written in Python. The functions are deployed with the .zip package deployment typThe functions use a Lambda layer that contains common libraries and packages in a .zip filThe Lambda .zip packages and Lambda layer .zip file are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket.  The company must implement automatic scanning of the Lambda functions and the Lambda layer to identify CVEs. A subset of the Lambda functions must receive automated code scans to detect potential data leaks and other vulnerabilities. The code scans must occur only for selected Lambda functions, not all the Lambda functions.  Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Activate Amazon Inspector. Start automated CVE scans.
answers.explanation: This is necessary because Amazon Inspector is the service used to perform automated vulnerability scans, including scanning for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in Lambda functions and layers. Activating it is the first step to enable this capability.

answers.content: Activate Lambda standard scanning and Lambda code scanning in Amazon Inspector.
answers.explanation:
The requirement is to identify CVEs and perform automated code scans for data leaks. Amazon Inspector provides two scan types for Lambda: Lambda standard scanning for application dependencies and layers (to find package vulnerabilities/CVEs), and Lambda code scanning for custom application code (to detect vulnerabilities and potential data leaks). Activating both scan types is required to meet the full set of requirements.
Reference: Automate security assessments for Lambda with Amazon Inspector - AWS Documentation

answers.content: Enable Amazon GuardDuty. Enable the Lambda Protection feature in GuardDuty.
answers.explanation: GuardDuty and its Lambda Protection feature focus on threat detection but do not perform automated CVE or code scanning.

answers.content: Enable scanning in the Monitor settings of the Lambda functions that need code scans.
answers.explanation: Correctly proposes selectively enabling scanning on individual Lambda functions to meet requirement of scanning only selected functions.

answers.content: Tag Lambda functions that do not need code scans. In the tag, include a key of InspectorCodeExclusion and a value of LambdaCodeScanning.
answers.explanation: The requirement specifies that "A subset of the Lambda functions must receive automated code scans," meaning some should be excluded. Amazon Inspector allows you to use tags to manage scanning exclusion. By tagging the functions that DO NOT need code scans with the key InspectorCodeExclusion and value LambdaCodeScanning, you exclude them from the code scanning process while still allowing other eligible functions to be scanned.

questions.content: A company is running a large containerized workload in the AWS Cloud. The workload consists of approximately 100 different services. The company uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to orchestrate the workload.  Recently the company’s development team started using AWS Fargate instead of Amazon EC2 instances in the ECS cluster. In the past, the workload has come close to running the maximum number of EC2 instances that are available in the account.  The company is worried that the workload could reach the maximum number of ECS tasks that are allowed. A solutions architect must implement a solution that will notify the development team when Fargate reaches 80% of the maximum number of tasks.  What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

answers.content: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the Sample Count statistic for each service in the ECS cluster. Set an alarm for when the math expression sample count/SERVICE_QUOTA(service)*100 is greater than 80. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: Monitoring Sample Count per service is not the correct metric for tracking Fargate task usage or service quotas.

answers.content: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor service quotas that are published under the AWS/Usage metric namespacSet an alarm for when the math expression metric/SERVICE_QUOTA(metric)*100 is greater than 80. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch provides service quota metrics under the AWS/Usage namespace, which allows monitoring of usage against service quotas. Setting a CloudWatch alarm on a math expression comparing the current metric to the service quota enables proactive notification before reaching the limit. Amazon SNS is the recommended service to notify the development team due to its integration with CloudWatch alarms and support for multiple notification protocols. This approach uses managed AWS monitoring and notification services to ensure secure and reliable tracking of resource limits.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function to poll detailed metrics from the ECS cluster. When the number of running Fargate tasks is greater than 80, invoke Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the development team.
answers.explanation: Polling metrics via a Lambda function and using SES adds unnecessary complexity and is less reliable than CloudWatch alarms and SNS for notifications.

answers.content: Create an AWS Config rule to evaluate whether the Fargate SERVICE_QUOTA is greater than 80. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the development team when the AWS Config rule is not compliant.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules are not designed to monitor or react to service quota usage or ECS task counts and using SES manually is not best practice.

questions.content: A company is changing the way that it handles patching of Amazon EC2 instances in its application account. The company currently patches instances over the internet by using a NAT gateway in a VPC in the application account.  The company has EC2 instances set up as a patch source repository in a dedicated private VPC in a core account. The company wants to use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager and the patch source repository in the core account to patch the EC2 instances in the application account. The company must prevent all EC2 instances in the application account from accessing the internet.  The EC2 instances in the application account need to access Amazon S3, where the application data is stored. These EC2 instances need connectivity to Systems Manager and to the patch source repository in the private VPC in the core account.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a network ACL that blocks outbound traffic on port 80. Associate the network ACL with all subnets in the application account.
