answers.content: Store a random string in AWS Systems Manager Parameter StorConfigure Parameter Store automatic rotation for the string. Configure CloudFront to inject the random string as a custom HTTP header for the origin request. Inspect the value of the custom HTTP header, and block access in the ALB.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store is less preferred than Secrets Manager for secret rotation and management; also, blocking in ALB requires custom logic not natively supported.

answers.content: Configure AWS Shield Advanced Create a security group policy to allow connections from CloudFront service IP address ranges. Add the policy to AWS Shield Advanced, and attach the policy to the ALB.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced does not manage security group policies and IP address whitelisting for CloudFront; security groups cannot reference AWS Shield policies.

questions.content: A global company has a mobile app that displays ticket barcodes. Customers use the tickets on the mobile app to attend live events. Event scanners read the ticket barcodes and call a backend API to validate the barcode data against data in a databasAfter the barcode is scanned, the backend logic writes to the database's single table to mark the barcode as used.  The company needs to deploy the app on AWS with a DNS name of api.example.com. The company will host the database in three AWS Regions around the world.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST latency?

answers.content: Host the database on Amazon Aurora global database clusters. Host the backend on three Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters that are in the same Regions as the databasCreate an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator to route requests to the nearest ECS cluster. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the accelerator endpoint
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora global database clusters are designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full MySQL and PostgreSQL compatibility, fitting the relational database requirement. Hosting the backend on Amazon ECS clusters in the same Regions as the Aurora global database clusters minimizes latency by keeping compute close to the data. AWS Global Accelerator routes requests to the nearest ECS cluster, providing low latency and high availability across Regions. Using Route 53 to map api.example.com to the Global Accelerator endpoint enables global DNS management with low latency. Options using CloudFront with backend logic in Lambda@Edge or CloudFront functions do not align with relational database usage or backend API architecture and may add latency. Using DynamoDB global tables does not fit the relational database requirement; Aurora is preferred for this use case.

answers.content: Host the database on Amazon Aurora global database clusters. Host the backend on three Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters that are in the same Regions as the databasCreate an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the three clusters as origins. Route requests to the nearest EKS cluster. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EKS is more complex and does not provide significant latency benefits compared to ECS with Global Accelerator; CloudFront is not ideal for routing backend API traffic.

answers.content: Host the database on Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Associate the CloudFront distribution with a CloudFront function that contains the backend logic to validate the barcodes. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB global tables do not meet the relational database requirement; embedding backend logic into CloudFront functions is not suitable for write operations to a database.

answers.content: Host the database on Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Associate the CloudFront distribution with a Lambda@Edge function that contains the backend logic to validate the barcodes. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: Similar to C, DynamoDB global tables do not fit relational workloads, and using Lambda@Edge for backend logic complicates stateful database writes and validation logic.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate an application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The company will begin the migration by moving the application’s underlying data storage to AWS. The application data is stored on a shared file system on premises, and the application servers connect to the shared file system through SMB.  A solutions architect must implement a solution that uses an Amazon S3 bucket for shared storagUntil the application is fully migrated and code is rewritten to use native Amazon S3 APIs, the application must continue to have access to the data through SMB. The solutions architect must migrate the application data to AWS to its new location while still allowing the on-premises application to access the data.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Configure AWS DataSync with one location for the on-premises file share and one location for the new Amazon FSx file system. Create a new DataSync task to copy the data from the on-premises file share location to the Amazon FSx file system.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx is not using Amazon S3 as required; it stores data in its own file system, not in S3.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket for the application. Copy the data from the on-premises storage to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Directly copying data to S3 does not provide SMB access; the application cannot access S3 through SMB without an intermediary.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) VM to the on-premises environment. Use AWS SMS to migrate the file storage server from on premises to an Amazon EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Migrating the file server to an EC2 instance is a custom solution and does not leverage managed services to provide SMB over S3.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket for the application. Deploy a new AWS Storage Gateway file gateway on an on-premises VM. Create a new file share that stores data in the S3 bucket and is associated with the file gateway. Copy the data from the on-premises storage to the new file gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway supports SMB access and stores data in Amazon S3, providing a seamless SMB interface for applications while using S3 as backend storagThis solution allows the application to continue accessing data via SMB without code changes during migration. Data is migrated to S3 through the file gateway which acts as a bridge, meeting the requirement of using S3 for storage but retaining SMB access. It leverages a managed AWS service designed for this purpose, following best practices of using managed services and ensuring secure and efficient migration.

questions.content: A company runs a software-as-a-service (SaaS) application on AWS. The application consists of AWS Lambda functions and an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ databasDuring market events, the application has a much higher workload than normal. Users notice slow response times during the peak periods because of many database connections. The company needs to improve the scalable performance and availability of the databas Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm action that triggers a Lambda function to add an Amazon RDS for MySQL read replica when resource utilization hits a threshold.
answers.explanation: Adding read replicas manually via Lambda on CloudWatch alarm is a reactive and custom solution, not managed and adds complexity.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora, and add a read replica. Add a database connection pool outside of the Lambda handler function.
answers.explanation: While migrating to Aurora and adding a read replica is good, adding a connection pool outside the Lambda handler is less effective and not the best practice compared to RDS Proxy.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora, and add a read replica. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted records.
answers.explanation: Using Route 53 weighted records does not address database connection pooling or performance issues directly and is an inappropriate solution for scaling database connections.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora, and add an Aurora Replica. Configure Amazon RDS Proxy to manage database connection pools.
answers.explanation: Migrating to Amazon Aurora improves scalability and availability compared to standard RDS for MySQL. Aurora Replicas provide better read scalability and failover support. Using Amazon RDS Proxy manages and pools database connections efficiently, reducing connection overhead and improving Lambda function scalability. This solution aligns with AWS best practices for managing database connections and improving performance during high workload periods.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The company currently hosts the data center on Linux-based VMware VMs. A solutions architect must collect information about network dependencies between the VMs. The information must be in the form of a diagram that details host IP addresses, hostnames, and network connection information.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Application Discovery ServicSelect an AWS Migration Hub home AWS Region. Install the AWS Application Discovery Agent on the on-premises servers for data collection. Grant permissions to Application Discovery Service to use the Migration Hub network diagrams.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service is designed to collect detailed information about on-premises servers, including network dependencies, host IP addresses, and hostnames. Installing the Application Discovery Agent on on-premises servers is the recommended method for comprehensive data collection. Selecting an AWS Migration Hub home region enables the centralization of data collection and visualization, including network diagrams. Using Application Discovery Service with Migration Hub supports the generation of network diagrams that meet the requirements.

answers.content: Use the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector for server data collection. Export the network diagrams from the AWS Migration Hub in .png format.
answers.explanation: Agentless Collector does not provide as detailed network connection information or network diagrams as the agent-based method.

answers.content: Install the AWS Application Migration Service agent on the on-premises servers for data collection. Use AWS Migration Hub data in Workload Discovery on AWS to generate network diagrams.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service is for migration, not for collecting detailed dependency or network diagram data.

answers.content: Install the AWS Application Migration Service agent on the on-premises servers for data collection. Export data from AWS Migration Hub in .csv format into an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard to generate network diagrams.
answers.explanation: Exporting data to CSV and using CloudWatch dashboards is complex and not a managed or standard method to generate network dependency diagrams, lacking security and ease.

questions.content: A company has an application that has a web frontend. The application runs in the company's on-premises data center and requires access to file storage for critical data. The application runs on three Linux VMs for redundancy. The architecture includes a load balancer with HTTP request-based routing.  The company needs to migrate the application to AWS as quickly as possiblThe architecture on AWS must be highly availabl Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the architecture?

answers.content: Migrate the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) containers that use the Fargate launch type in three Availability Zones. Use Amazon S3 to provide file storage for all three containers. Use a Network Load Balancer to direct traffic to the containers.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is object storage, not file storage, and Network Load Balancer does not support HTTP request-based routing.

answers.content: Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in three Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file storagMount the file storage on all three EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to direct traffic to the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Migrating to EC2 instances in three Availability Zones provides a highly available architecture consistent with the original three Linux VMs setup. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is designed to provide scalable and shared file storage accessible from multiple EC2 instances, preserving the shared file storage requirement. An Application Load Balancer supports HTTP request-based routing, which matches the existing architecture's requirement. This solution involves the fewest changes because it retains the VM-based architecture and HTTP routing type.

answers.content: Migrate the application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) containers that use the Fargate launch type in three Availability Zones. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre to provide file storage for all three containers. Use a Network Load Balancer to direct traffic to the containers.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for high-performance compute workloads, not general shared file storage, and Network Load Balancer does not support HTTP routing.

answers.content: Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in three AWS Regions. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for file storagEnable Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for all three EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to direct traffic to the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances across three Regions and Amazon EBS (which cannot be shared across instances) complicates the architecture and Cross-Region Replication is not applicable to EBS volumes; also, an Application Load Balancer must be regional, not multi-region.

questions.content: A company has a web application that uses Amazon API Gateway. AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. A recent marketing campaign has increased demand. Monitoring software reports that many requests have significantly longer response times than before the marketing campaign.  A solutions architect enabled Amazon CloudWatch Logs for API Gateway and noticed that errors are occurring on 20% of the requests. In CloudWatch, the Lambda function Throttles metric represents 1% of the requests and the Errors metric represents 10% of the requests. Application logs indicate that, when errors occur, there is a call to DynamoDB.  What change should the solutions architect make to improve the current response times as the web application becomes more popular?

answers.content: Increase the concurrency limit of the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Lambda throttling is low (1%), so increasing concurrency limit will not significantly improve response times.

answers.content: Implement DynamoDB auto scaling on the table.
answers.explanation: The errors and increased response times are linked to calls to DynamoDB during errors, indicating DynamoDB is a bottleneck. DynamoDB auto scaling improves throughput capacity automatically in response to demand increases, helping to reduce throttling and errors. Lambda throttling is only 1%, so increasing Lambda concurrency limit is less impactful than addressing DynamoDB throughput. API Gateway throttle limits are not indicated as a problem since most errors occur during DynamoDB calls. Re-creating the DynamoDB table is a more drastic, less operationally convenient solution compared to enabling auto scaling.

answers.content: Increase the API Gateway throttle limit.
answers.explanation: API Gateway throttle limits are not causing errors; errors are associated with DynamoDB calls.

answers.content: Re-create the DynamoDB table with a better-partitioned primary index.
answers.explanation: Re-creating the DynamoDB table is complex and unnecessary before trying DynamoDB auto scaling.

questions.content: A company's compliance audit reveals that some Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that were created in an AWS account were not encrypted. A solutions architect must implement a solution to encrypt all new EBS volumes at rest.  Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST effort?

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to delete noncompliant volumes.
answers.explanation: Deleting noncompliant volumes after creation is reactive and could disrupt operations; it does not prevent unencrypted volumes from being created.

answers.content: Use AWS Audit Manager with data encryption.
answers.explanation: AWS Audit Manager is for compliance auditing and reporting, not for enforcing or implementing encryption directly.

answers.content: Create an AWS Config rule to detect the creation of a new EBS volumEncrypt the volume by using AWS Systems Manager Automation.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Config rules and Systems Manager Automation to encrypt volumes is reactive and involves manual or automated remediation rather than prevention, increasing effort.

answers.content: Turn on EBS encryption by default in all AWS Regions.
answers.explanation: Turning on EBS encryption by default in all AWS Regions is a preventive control that ensures all new EBS volumes are encrypted without manual intervention. This method requires the least operational effort and aligns with AWS best practices for automated encryption enforcement. Other options involve detection and remediation steps after unencrypted volumes are created, increasing complexity and operational overhead.

questions.content: A company’s solutions architect needs to provide secure Remote Desktop connectivity to users for Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are hosted in a VPC. The solution must integrate centralized user management with the company's on-premises Active Directory. Connectivity to the VPC is through the internet. The company has hardware that can be used to establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection.  Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory. Deploy an EC2 instance as a bastion host in the VPC. Ensure that the EC2 instance is joined to the domain. Use the bastion host to access the target instances through RDP.
answers.explanation: Deploying a bastion host EC2 instance adds cost and operational overhead compared to leveraging the VPN connection directly.

answers.content: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to integrate with the on-premises Active Directory by using the AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory AD Connector. Configure permission sets against user groups for access to AWS Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Fleet Manager to access the target instances through RDP.
answers.explanation: Configuring AWS IAM Identity Center and Systems Manager Fleet Manager adds complexity and may not be as cost-effective as using VPN.

answers.content: Implement a VPN between the on-premises environment and the target VPEnsure that the target instances are joined to the on-premises Active Directory domain over the VPN connection. Configure RDP access through the VPN. Connect from the company’s network to the target instances.
answers.explanation: Using the existing hardware to establish a Site-to-Site VPN aligns with the given facts and ensures secure connectivity to the VPC over the internet. Joining EC2 instances to the on-premises Active Directory via the VPN provides centralized user management as required. Configuring RDP access through the VPN is secure and cost-effective compared to deploying additional managed services or bastion hosts. This solution avoids unnecessary deployment of additional AWS managed directories or bastion hosts, reducing cost while meeting security best practices.

answers.content: Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory. Deploy a Remote Desktop Gateway on AWS by using an AWS Quick Start. Ensure that the Remote Desktop Gateway is joined to the domain. Use the Remote Desktop Gateway to access the target instances through RDP.
answers.explanation: Deploying a Remote Desktop Gateway adds additional infrastructure and cost compared to using the VPN for secure connectivity.

questions.content: A company is deploying a new API to AWS. The API uses Amazon API Gateway with a Regional API endpoint and an AWS Lambda function for hosting. The API retrieves data from an external vendor API, stores data in an Amazon DynamoDB global table, and retrieves data from the DynamoDB global table The API key for the vendor's API is stored in AWS Secrets Manager and is encrypted with a customer managed key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The company has deployed its own API into a single AWS Region.  A solutions architect needs to change the API components of the company’s API to ensure that the components can run across multiple Regions in an active-active configuration.  Which combination of changes will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Deploy the API to multiple Regions. Configure Amazon Route 53 with custom domain names that route traffic to each Regional API endpoint. Implement a Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
answers.explanation: Deploying the API to multiple Regions and using Amazon Route 53 routing to direct traffic to Regional API Gateway endpoints enables an active-active, multi-Region API architecture with minimal changes.

answers.content: Create a new KMS multi-Region customer managed key. Create a new KMS customer managed replica key in each in-scope Region.
answers.explanation: Using a KMS multi-Region customer managed key allows encryption keys to be consistently available across Regions, reducing key management complexity.

answers.content: Replicate the existing Secrets Manager secret to other Regions. For each in-scope Region's replicated secret, select the appropriate KMS key.
answers.explanation: Replicating the Secrets Manager secret across Regions keeps the vendor API key synchronized and encrypted with the appropriate regional KMS keys, minimizing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create a new AWS managed KMS key in each in-scope Region. Convert an existing key to a multiRegion key. Use the multi-Region key in other Regions.
answers.explanation: AWS managed KMS keys cannot be converted to multi-Region keys and do not support the required replication model.

answers.content: Create a new Secrets Manager secret in each in-scope Region. Copy the secret value from the existing Region to the new secret in each in-scope Region.
answers.explanation: Manually creating and copying secrets in each Region increases operational overhead and risk of configuration drift.

answers.content: Modify the deployment process for the Lambda function to repeat the deployment across in-scope Regions. Turn on the multi-Region option for the existing API. Select the Lambda function that is deployed in each Region as the backend for the multi-Region API.
answers.explanation: API Gateway does not support a “multi-Region option” toggle; active-active behavior must be implemented through separate Regional deployments and routing.

questions.content: A software company needs to create short-lived test environments to test pull requests as part of its development process. Each test environment consists of a single Amazon EC2 instance that is in an Auto Scaling group.  The test environments must be able to communicate with a central server to report test results. The central server is located in an on-premises data center. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the company can create and delete test environments without any manual intervention. The company has created a transit gateway with a VPN attachment to the on-premises network.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an AWS CloudFormation template that contains a transit gateway attachment and related routing configurations. Create a CloudFormation stack set that includes this templatUse CloudFormation StackSets to deploy a new stack for each VPC in the account. Deploy a new VPC for each test environment.
answers.explanation: Deploying a new VPC for each test environment via StackSets creates more operational overhead than using a single VPC.

answers.content: Create a single VPC for the test environments. Include a transit gateway attachment and related routing configurations. Use AWS CloudFormation to deploy all test environments into the VPC.
answers.explanation: Using a single VPC for all test environments with a transit gateway attachment and the necessary routing configurations minimizes operational overhead by avoiding management of multiple VPCs, accounts, or complex network attachments. AWS best practices favor managed services and simpler architecture to reduce complexity and manual intervention. Options involving multiple accounts or multiple VPCs increase management complexity and operational overhead. Deploying Kubernetes (EKS) adds unnecessary complexity not required by the question. The provided key facts do not support the need for more complex network segregation or account management in this scenario.

answers.content: Create a new OU in AWS Organizations for testing. Create an AWS CioudFormation template that contains a VPC, necessary networking resources, a transit gateway attachment, and related routing configurations. Create a CloudFormation stack set that includes this templatUse CloudFormation StackSets for deployments into each account under the testing OU. Create a new account for each test environment.
answers.explanation: Creating new AWS accounts for each test environment adds significant management complexity and overhead.

answers.content: Convert the test environment EC2 instances into Docker images. Use AWS CloudFormation to configure an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster in a new VPC, create a transit gateway attachment, and create related routing configurations. Use Kubernetes to manage the deployment and lifecycle of the test environments.
answers.explanation: Using EKS to run test environments is unnecessarily complex for single EC2 instances and increases operational overhead.

questions.content: A company runs its sales reporting application in an AWS Region in the United States. The application uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional API and AWS Lambda functions to generate on-demand reports from data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL databasThe frontend of the application is hosted on Amazon S3 and is accessed by users through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company is using Amazon Route 53 as the DNS service for the domain. Route 53 is configured with a simple routing policy to route traffic to the API Gateway API.  In the next 6 months, the company plans to expand operations to EuropMore than 90% of the database traffic is read-only traffic. The company has already deployed an API Gateway API and Lambda functions in the new Region.  A solutions architect must design a solution that minimizes latency for users who download reports.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) task with full load to replicate the primary database in the original Region to the database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to latency-based routing to connect to the API Gateway API.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS full load replication alone does not keep data continuously synchronized, causing stale reads and higher latency; latency-based routing alone is insufficient without continuous replication.

answers.content: Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) task with full load plus change data capture (CDC) to replicate the primary database in the original Region to the database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to geolocation routing to connect to the API Gateway API.
answers.explanation: Geolocation routing may cause suboptimal routing and does not ensure lowest latency; DMS with CDC is more complex and less managed than RDS cross-Region read replicas.

answers.content: Configure a cross-Region read replica for the RDS database in the new Region Change the Route 53 record to latency-based routing to connect to the API Gateway API.
answers.explanation: Configuring a cross-Region read replica for the RDS database in the new Region ensures that more than 90% read-only database traffic is served locally with low latency, improving performance for European users. Changing the Route 53 record to latency-based routing routes users to the Region with the lowest latency, optimizing user experience on both continents. This solution uses a managed AWS service feature (RDS cross-Region read replica) preferred over manual or custom replication solutions. CloudFront caching reduces backend requests, but since reports require up-to-date data, serving read traffic from a cross-Region read replica is appropriate and secure.

answers.content: Configure a cross-Region read replica for the RDS database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to geolocation routing to connect to the API Gateway API.
answers.explanation: Geolocation routing is less optimal than latency-based routing for minimizing latency, which is the requirement.

questions.content: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage a multi-account structurThe company has hundreds of AWS accounts and expects the number of accounts to increasThe company is building a new application that uses Docker images. The company will push the Docker images to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Only accounts that are within the company’s organization should have access to the images.  The company has a CI/CD process that runs frequently. The company wants to retain all the tagged images. However, the company wants to retain only the five most recent untagged images.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create a private repository in Amazon ECR. Create a permissions policy for the repository that allows only required ECR operations. Include a condition to allow the ECR operations if the value of the aws:PrincipalOrglD condition key is equal to the ID of the company’s organization. Add a lifecycle rule to the ECR repository that deletes all untagged images over the count of five
answers.explanation: A private repository in Amazon ECR ensures images are not publicly accessible, aligning with the requirement that only accounts within the company’s organization have access. Using a permissions policy with aws:PrincipalOrgID condition enforces access restriction to only organizational accounts, meeting security best practices. ECR lifecycle policies natively support automatic deletion of untagged images over a configured count, requiring minimal operational overhead. This solution leverages managed features of Amazon ECR for both security and image lifecycle management, avoiding custom Lambda functions or manual operations.

answers.content: Create a public repository in Amazon ECR. Create an IAM role in the ECR account. Set permissions so that any account can assume the role if the value of the aws:PrincipalOrglD condition key is equal to the ID of the company’s organization. Add a lifecycle rule to the ECR repository that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.
answers.explanation: Public repositories expose images to anyone; relying on an IAM role does not prevent public access, conflicting with security best practices.

answers.content: Create a private repository in Amazon ECR. Create a permissions policy for the repository that includes only required ECR operations. Include a condition to allow the ECR operations for all account IDs in the organization Schedule a daily Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function and EventBridge to delete images adds unnecessary operational overhead when native ECR lifecycle policies already exist.

answers.content: Create a public repository in Amazon ECR. Configure Amazon ECR to use an interface VPC endpoint with an endpoint policy that includes the required permissions for images that the company needs to pull. Include a condition to allow the ECR operations for all account IDs in the company’s organization. Schedule a daily Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.
answers.explanation: Public repositories contradict the requirement to restrict access to organizational accounts and introducing VPC endpoints and Lambda functions increases complexity unnecessarily.

questions.content: A research center is migrating to the AWS Cloud and has moved its on-premises 1 PB object storage to an Amazon S3 bucket. One hundred scientists are using this object storage to store their work-related documents. Each scientist has a personal folder on the object storAll the scientists are members of a single IAM user group.  The research center's compliance officer is worried that scientists will be able to access each other's work. The research center has a strict obligation to report on which scientist accesses which documents. The team that is responsible for these reports has little AWS experience and wants a ready-to-use solution that minimizes operational overhead.  Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an identity policy that grants the user read and write access. Add a condition that specifies that the S3 paths must be prefixed with $(aws:username). Apply the policy on the scientists’ IAM user group.
answers.explanation: Correct because it restricts access to personal folders, ensuring no cross-access among scientists.

answers.content: Configure a trail with AWS CloudTrail to capture all object-level events in the S3 bucket. Store the trail output in another S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs and generate reports.
answers.explanation: Correct as CloudTrail provides detailed object-level logging, suitable for compliance and reporting using Athena.

answers.content: Enable S3 server access logging. Configure another S3 bucket as the target for log delivery. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs and generate reports.
answers.explanation: S3 server access logging captures limited access data and is less detailed for auditing and reporting compared to CloudTrail.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket policy that grants read and write access to users in the scientists’ IAM user group.
answers.explanation: A bucket policy granting read/write to the entire group does not limit scientists to their folders, violating access segregation.

answers.content: Configure a trail with AWS CloudTrail to capture all object-level events in the S3 bucket and write the events to Amazon CloudWatch. Use the Amazon Athena CloudWatch connector to query the logs and generate reports.
answers.explanation: Using CloudWatch with Athena introduces additional complexity and operational overhead, which is not ideal for less-experienced teams.

questions.content: A company is migrating mobile banking applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. Backend service applications run in an on-premises data center. The data center has an AWS Direct Connect connection into AWS. The applications that run in the VPC need to resolve DNS requests to an on-premises Active Directory domain that runs in the data center.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

answers.content: Provision a set of EC2 instances across two Availability Zones in the VPC as caching DNS servers to resolve DNS queries from the application servers within the VPC.
answers.explanation: Requires manual provisioning and management of EC2 caching DNS servers, increasing administrative overhead.

answers.content: Provision an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zonConfigure NS records that point to on-premises DNS servers.
answers.explanation: Route 53 private hosted zones do not natively support forwarding to on-premises DNS servers, leading to complex manual configuration.

answers.content: Create DNS endpoints by using Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Add conditional forwarding rules to resolve DNS namespaces between the on-premises data center and the VPC.
answers.explanation: Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS endpoints with conditional forwarding rules securely and automatically resolve DNS queries between the VPC and on-premises Active Directory domain. This approach uses a managed AWS service designed for integrating DNS namespaces with minimal administrative overhead. Provisioning EC2 instances as caching DNS servers requires manual setup and management, increasing overhead compared to Route 53 Resolver. Route 53 private hosted zones do not natively support forwarding to on-premises DNS servers, requiring additional manual configuration. Provisioning a new Active Directory domain controller with trust relationships involves complex setup and higher administrative overhead than DNS resolver endpoints.

answers.content: Provision a new Active Directory domain controller in the VPC with a bidirectional trust between this new domain and the on-premises Active Directory domain.
answers.explanation: Setting up a new AD domain controller with trust relationships has significantly higher administrative overhead and complexity.

questions.content: A company is deploying a third-party firewall appliance solution from AWS Marketplace to monitor and protect traffic that leaves the company's AWS environments. The company wants to deploy this appliance into a shared services VPC and route all outbound internet-bound traffic through the appliances.  A solutions architect needs to recommend a deployment method that prioritizes reliability and minimizes failover time between firewall appliances within a single AWS Region. The company has set up routing from the shared services VPC to other VPCs.  Which steps should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Deploy two firewall appliances into the shared services VPC, each in a separate Availability Zone.
answers.explanation: Deploying firewall appliances in separate Availability Zones ensures high availability and fault tolerance, minimizing failover time.

answers.content: Create a new Network Load Balancer in the shared services VPC. Create a new target group, and attach it to the new Network Load Balancer. Add each of the firewall appliance instances to the target group.
answers.explanation: A Network Load Balancer is not designed for inline traffic inspection and does not support the transparent traffic flow required for firewall appliances.

answers.content: Create a new Gateway Load Balancer in the shared services VPC. Create a new target group, and attach it to the new Gateway Load Balancer. Add each of the firewall appliance instances to the target group.
answers.explanation: A Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) is specifically designed for third-party network appliances and provides fast, transparent failover with minimal operational overhead.

answers.content: Create a VPC interface endpoint. Add a route to the route table in the shared services VPC. Designate the new endpoint as the next hop for traffic that enters the shared services VPC from other VPCs.
answers.explanation: Interface VPC endpoints are used for private access to AWS services, not for routing traffic through security appliances.

answers.content: Deploy two firewall appliances into the shared services VPC, each in the same Availability Zone.
answers.explanation: Deploying both appliances in the same Availability Zone creates a single point of failure and reduces reliability.

answers.content: Create a VPC Gateway Load Balancer endpoint. Add a route to the route table in the shared services VPC. Designate the new endpoint as the next hop for traffic that enters the shared services VPC from other VPCs.
answers.explanation: A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (GWLBe) allows traffic from other VPCs to be routed through the firewall appliances seamlessly using route tables.

questions.content: A company is launching a new online game on Amazon EC2 instances. The game must be available globally. The company plans to run the game in three AWS Regions us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1. The game's leaderboards, player inventory and event status must be available across Regions.  A solutions architect must design a solution that will give any Region the ability to scale to handle the load of all Regions. Additionally, users must automatically connect to the Region that provides the least latency.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an EC2 Spot Fleet. Attach the Spot Fleet to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator IP address that points to the NLB. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing entry for the Global Accelerator IP address. Save the game metadata to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in each Region. Set up a read replica in the other Regions.
answers.explanation: Using an RDS MySQL primary and read replicas across Regions increases operational complexity and does not provide true multi-master global writes as needed for global availability and scaling.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances Attach the Auto Scaling group to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each Region. For each Region, create an Amazon Route 53 entry that uses geoproximity routing and points to the NLB in that Region. Save the game metadata to MySQL databases on EC2 instances in each Region. Set up replication between the database EC2 instances in each Region.
answers.explanation: Hosting MySQL databases on EC2 with custom replication increases operational overhead and complexity, and geoproximity routing does not necessarily route based on lowest latency.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Attach the Auto Scaling group to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each Region. For each Region, create an Amazon Route 53 entry that uses latency-based routing and points to the NLB in that Region. Save the game metadata to an Amazon DynamoDB global table.
answers.explanation: Creating an Auto Scaling group and attaching it to an NLB in each Region leverages managed AWS services for scaling and load balancing, minimizing operational overhead. Using Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing ensures users automatically connect to the Region with the least latency, fulfilling the requirement efficiently. Amazon DynamoDB global tables provide a managed, multi-Region, fully replicated NoSQL database solution suitable for game metadata like leaderboards, player inventory, and event status, enabling global scalability with minimal operational burden. This approach aligns with AWS best practices by using managed services for scalability, global data replication, and routing based on latency.

answers.content: Use EC2 Global View. Deploy the EC2 instances to each Region. Attach the instances to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy a DNS server on an EC2 instance in each Region. Set up custom logic on each DNS server to redirect the user to the Region that provides the lowest latency. Save the game metadata to an Amazon Aurora global database.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 Global View and custom DNS servers adds unnecessary management complexity and operational overhead instead of leveraging managed AWS routing and database services.

questions.content: A company runs its application on Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions. The EC2 instances experience a continuous and stable load. The Lambda functions experience a varied and unpredictable load. The application includes a caching layer that uses an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster.  A solutions architect must recommend a solution to minimize the company's overall monthly costs.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Purchase an EC2 instance Savings Plan to cover the EC2 instances. Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Lambda to cover the minimum expected consumption of the Lambda functions. Purchase reserved nodes to cover the MemoryDB cache nodes.
answers.explanation: EC2 instance Savings Plans specifically provide cost savings for EC2 instances with steady usagCompute Savings Plans cover Lambda function usage based on compute consumption, allowing flexibility with varied and unpredictable loads. MemoryDB supports reserved nodes to reduce cost for stable, continuous cache usagThis approach aligns with best practice of matching Savings Plans or reserved nodes to workload characteristics and service support.

answers.content: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan to cover the EC2 instances. Purchase Lambda reserved concurrency to cover the expected Lambda usagPurchase reserved nodes to cover the MemoryDB cache nodes.
answers.explanation: Compute Savings Plans do not optimally cover EC2 instances; EC2 instance Savings Plans provide better pricing for EC2. Lambda reserved concurrency is not a cost-saving mechanism but a concurrency control feature.

answers.content: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan to cover the entire expected cost of the EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and MemoryDB cache nodes.
answers.explanation: Compute Savings Plans cannot cover MemoryDB reserved nodes; MemoryDB requires reserved nodes for cost savings, so this option misses MemoryDB discounting.

answers.content: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan to cover the EC2 instances and the MemoryDB cache nodes. Purchase Lambda reserved concurrency to cover the expected Lambda usage.
answers.explanation: Compute Savings Plans do not apply to MemoryDB cache nodes, so this option incorrectly attempts to cover MemoryDB with Compute Savings Plans.

questions.content: A company wants to use Amazon S3 to back up its on-premises file storage solution. The company’s on-premises file storage solution supports NFS, and the company wants its new solution to support NFS. The company wants to archive the backup files after 5 days. If the company needs archived files for disaster recovery, the company is willing to wait a few days for the retrieval of those files.  Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the file gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 5 days.
answers.explanation: Transitions to S3 Standard-IA instead of Glacier Deep Archive, which is less cost-effective for long-term archival.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the volume gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 days.
answers.explanation: Volume gateway does not support NFS, which is required by the company.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the tape gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 5 days.
answers.explanation: Tape gateway emulates tape backups and is less appropriate for file storage with NFS support, plus it transitions to Standard-IA, not Glacier Deep Archive.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the file gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 days.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway supports NFS, meeting the requirement for NFS support. Using an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 days aligns with the cost-effective archiving of infrequently accessed files with acceptable retrieval latency for disaster recovery. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the most cost-effective storage class for archival where retrieval can take days, fitting the company's willingness to wait for disaster recovery. The solution uses managed AWS services designed for file storage and lifecycle management, aligning with best practices.

questions.content: A company is using AWS Organizations with a multi-account architecturThe company's current security configuration for the account architecture includes SCPs, resource-based policies, identity-based policies, trust policies, and session policies.  A solutions architect needs to allow an IAM user in Account A to assume a role in Account B.  Which combination of steps must the solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Configure the SCP for Account A to allow the action.
answers.explanation: When using AWS Organizations, a Service Control Policy (SCP) applies permissions at the Organization Unit (OU) or account level. For a cross-account action like AssumeRole to succeed, the SCP attached to Account A (the source account) must explicitly allow the `sts:AssumeRole` action. If the SCP denies this action, no identity-based or resource-based policy can override the denial.

answers.content: Configure the resource-based policies to allow the action.
answers.explanation: Resource-based policies are not used for IAM roles but for resources like S3 buckets; assuming a role requires trust policy configuration.

answers.content: Configure the identity-based policy on the user in Account A to allow the action.
answers.explanation: The IAM user in Account A (the source account) needs an identity-based policy that grants them permission to perform the `sts:AssumeRole` action on the target role's ARN in Account B. This policy defines what the *user* is allowed to do.

answers.content: Configure the identity-based policy on the user in Account B to allow the action.
answers.explanation: Identity-based policies on users in Account B do not affect the ability of an external user to assume a role in Account B; the trust policy governs this.

answers.content: Configure the trust policy on the target role in Account B to allow the action.
answers.explanation: An IAM role requires a trust policy, which is a resource-based policy, that specifies which principals are allowed to assume the role. To allow the IAM user from Account A to assume the role in Account B, the trust policy on the role in Account B must list the principal (either the specific user's ARN or the entire Account A ARN) and grant the `sts:AssumeRole` permission. (Reference: <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-use-trust-policies-with-iam-roles/> and <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_aws-accounts.html>)

answers.content: Configure the session policy to allow the action and to be passed programmatically by the GetSessionToken API operation.
answers.explanation: Session policies cannot grant new permissions or enable cross-account access; they only further restrict permissions that are already allowed. Additionally, GetSessionToken is not used for cross-account role assumption, which requires sts:AssumeRole with proper identity and trust policies, so this option is incorrect.

questions.content: A solutions architect is reviewing a company's process for taking snapshots of Amazon RDS DB instances. The company takes automatic snapshots every day and retains the snapshots for 7 days.  The solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that takes snapshots every 6 hours and retains the snapshots for 30 days. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage all of its AWS accounts. The company needs a consolidated view of the health of the RDS snapshots.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Turn on the cross-account management feature in AWS Backup. Create a backup plan that specifies the frequency and retention requirements. Add a tag to the DB instances. Apply the backup plan by using tags. Use AWS Backup to monitor the status of the backups.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup supports cross-account management, enabling centralized backup plans and monitoring with minimal operational overhead. Using AWS Backup to create a backup plan with tags allows automated snapshot frequency and retention configuration. AWS Backup provides a consolidated view of backup health across accounts using AWS Organizations, meeting the requirement for a consolidated status view. This approach leverages a managed AWS service designed for backup automation and monitoring, aligning with AWS best practices for security and operational efficiency.

answers.content: Turn on the cross-account management feature in Amazon RDS. Create a snapshot global policy that specifies the frequency and retention requirements. Use the RDS console in the management account to monitor the status of the backups.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS does not have a cross-account management feature for snapshot scheduling and consolidated monitoring.

answers.content: Turn on the cross-account management feature in AWS CloudFormation. From the management account, deploy a CloudFormation stack set that contains a backup plan from AWS Backup that specifies the frequency and retention requirements. Create an AWS Lambda function in the management account to monitor the status of the backups. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule in each account to run the Lambda function on a schedule.
answers.explanation: CloudFormation and Lambda require high operational overhead compared to native AWS Backup cross-account features.

answers.content: Configure AWS Backup in each account. Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager lifecycle policy that specifies the frequency and retention requirements. Specify the DB instances as the target resource Use the Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager console in each member account to monitor the status of the backups.
answers.explanation: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager does not support RDS snapshots and requires separate configuration in each account, increasing overhead.

questions.content: A data analytics company has an Amazon Redshift cluster that consists of several reserved nodes. The cluster is experiencing unexpected bursts of usage because a team of employees is compiling a deep audit analysis report. The queries to generate the report are complex read queries and are CPU intensiv Business requirements dictate that the cluster must be able to service read and write queries at all times. A solutions architect must devise a solution that accommodates the bursts of usag Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Provision an Amazon EMR cluster Offload the complex data processing tasks.
answers.explanation: Provisioning an Amazon EMR cluster adds unnecessary complexity and cost instead of leveraging native Redshift features.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Lambda function to add capacity to the Amazon Redshift cluster by using a classic resize operation when the cluster’s CPU metrics in Amazon CloudWatch reach 80%.
answers.explanation: Classic resize operations are inefficient and time-consuming, leading to potential downtime and do not support real-time burst scaling.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Lambda function to add capacity to the Amazon Redshift cluster by using an elastic resize operation when the cluster’s CPU metrics in Amazon CloudWatch reach 80%.
answers.explanation: Although elastic resize is faster than classic resize, using a Lambda to trigger resizing still involves operational overhead and potential downtime, unlike Concurrency Scaling.

answers.content: Turn on the Concurrency Scaling feature for the Amazon Redshift cluster.
answers.explanation: Concurrency Scaling is a managed Amazon Redshift feature designed to handle bursts of complex read queries without impacting the availability of the cluster for read and write operations. Concurrency Scaling automatically adds transient cluster capacity during peak usage, which meets the requirement of servicing read and write queries at all times. It is more cost-effective than permanently resizing the cluster as it scales capacity only when needed. Using Concurrency Scaling aligns with AWS best practices by leveraging managed services rather than manual or custom scaling solutions.

questions.content: An online survey company runs its application in the AWS Cloud. The application is distributed and consists of microservices that run in an automatically scaled Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The ECS cluster is a target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is a custom origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution.  The company has a survey that contains sensitive data. The sensitive data must be encrypted when it moves through the application. The application's data-handling microservice is the only microservice that should be able to decrypt the data  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a symmetric AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is dedicated to the data-handling microservicCreate a field-level encryption profile and a configuration. Associate the KMS key and the configuration with the CloudFront cache behavior.
answers.explanation: AWS KMS keys cannot be associated directly with CloudFront field-level encryption; CloudFront uses RSA keys for this purpose.

answers.content: Create an RSA key pair that is dedicated to the data-handing microservicUpload the public key to the CloudFront distribution. Create a field-level encryption profile and a configuration. Add the configuration to the CloudFront cache behavior.
answers.explanation: CloudFront supports field-level encryption using RSA public keys where the public key is stored with CloudFront and the private key remains with the consuming service, ensuring only the intended microservice can decrypt the data. The data-handling microservice can securely decrypt sensitive data with its corresponding private RSA key while encrypting at the field level in CloudFront protects confidentiality during transit. AWS KMS keys are used for data volume encryption within ECS but are not directly integrated for field-level encryption in CloudFront. Using RSA key pairs for CloudFront field-level encryption aligns with best practices for data confidentiality and controlled decryption access.

answers.content: Create a symmetric AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is dedicated to the data-handling microservicCreate a Lambda@Edge function. Program the function to use the KMS key to encrypt the sensitive data.
answers.explanation: Lambda@Edge cannot directly use AWS KMS keys for encrypting sensitive data; this is not a managed or standard CloudFront field-level encryption solution.

answers.content: Create an RSA key pair that is dedicated to the data-handling microservicCreate a Lambda@Edge function. Program the function to use the private key of the RSA key pair to encrypt the sensitive data.
answers.explanation: Using the private RSA key in Lambda@Edge for encryption is insecure and contradicts best practices, as encryption should use public keys and decryption private keys remain secure within the microservice.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate its on-premises VMware cluster of 120 VMs to AWS. The VMs have many different operating systems and many custom software packages installed. The company also has an on-premises NFS server that is 10 TB in sizThe company has set up a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to AWS for the migration.  Which solution will complete the migration to AWS in the LEAST amount of time?

answers.content: Export the on-premises VMs and copy them to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use VM Import/Export to create AMIs from the VM images that are stored in Amazon S3. Order an AWS Snowball Edge devicCopy the NFS server data to the devicRestore the NFS server data to an Amazon EC2 instance that has NFS configured.
answers.explanation: Using VM Import/Export is slower and more manual, and ordering Snowball Edge adds physical shipping delays, increasing total migration time.

answers.content: Configure AWS Application Migration Service with a connection to the VMware cluster. Create a replication job for the VMS. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure AWS DataSync to copy the NFS server data to the EFS file system over the Direct Connect connection.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service is designed to replicate on-premises VMs to AWS with minimal downtime and effort, supporting diverse operating systems and software configurations. AWS DataSync can efficiently transfer large amounts of NFS data over a high-speed Direct Connect connection to Amazon EFS, a managed scalable file storage service that supports NFS. This solution leverages managed AWS services that minimize manual intervention and maximize data transfer speed, aligning with best practices to prioritize operational efficiency and security.

answers.content: Recreate the VMs on AWS as Amazon EC2 instances. Install all the required software packages. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure AWS DataSync to copy the NFS server data to the FSx for Lustre file system over the Direct Connect connection.
answers.explanation: Recreating VMs manually is time-consuming, and Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for high-performance workloads, not standard NFS workloads; also, it adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Order two AWS Snowball Edge devices. Copy the VMs and the NFS server data to the devices. Run VM Import/Export after the data from the devices is loaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Copy the NFS server data from Amazon S3 to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Ordering two Snowball Edge devices and using VM Import/Export increases physical transfer delays, making it slower than direct network-based replication.

questions.content: A company is building an application that will run on an AWS Lambda function. Hundreds of customers will use the application. The company wants to give each customer a quota of requests for a specific time period. The quotas must match customer usage patterns. Some customers must receive a higher quota for a shorter time period.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API with a proxy integration to invoke the Lambda function. For each customer, configure an API Gateway usage plan that includes an appropriate request quota. Create an API key from the usage plan for each user that the customer needs.
answers.explanation: API Gateway REST API supports usage plans that allow configuring request quotas tailored to each customer. API Gateway usage plans and API keys enable control over request quotas per customer securely and at scalThis aligns with AWS best practices for quota and throttling management for APIs invoking Lambda functions. Option A uses managed AWS services designed for request quota management rather than custom or manual solutions.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with a proxy integration to invoke the Lambda function. For each customer configure an API Gateway usage plan that includes an appropriate request quota Configure route-level throttling for each usage plan. Create an API Key from the usage plan for each user that the customer needs.
answers.explanation: Amazon API Gateway HTTP API does not currently support usage plans and API key quotas.

answers.content: Create a Lambda function alias for each customer. Include a concurrency limit with an appropriate request quota. Create a Lambda function URL for each function alias. Share the Lambda function URL for each alias with the relevant customer.
answers.explanation: Lambda function aliases and concurrency limits do not provide customer-specific request quotas matching usage patterns.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC. Configure the Lambda function as a target for the ALB. Configure an AWS WAF web ACL for the ALB. For each customer configure a rale-based rule that includes an appropriate request quota.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF rules on ALB cannot granularly manage request quotas per customer as effectively as API Gateway usage plans.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate several applications to AWS. The company does not have a good understanding of its entire application estatThe estate consists of a mixture of physical machines and VMs.  One application that the company will migrate has many dependencies that are sensitive to latency. The company is unsure what all the dependencies arHowever the company knows that the low-latency communications use a custom IP-based protocol that runs on port 1000. The company wants to migrate the application and these dependencies together to move all the low-latency interfaces to AWS at the same tim The company has installed the AWS Application Discovery Agent and has been collecting data for several months.  What should the company do to identify the dependencies that need to be migrated in the same phase as the application?

answers.content: Use AWS Migration Hub and select the servers that host the application. Visualize the network graph to find servers that interact with the application. Turn on data exploration in Amazon Athena. Query the data that is transferred between the servers to identify the servers that communicate on port 1000. Return to Migration Hub. Create a move group that is based on the findings from the Athena queries.
answers.explanation: AWS Migration Hub is designed to visualize network dependencies, which directly helps identify servers interacting with the application. Using Amazon Athena to query collected discovery data against specific traffic characteristics, such as communication on port 1000, aligns with secure, managed AWS service usagCreating a move group in Migration Hub based on discovered network communications enables grouping servers that need to be migrated together, following AWS best practices.

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration Service and select the servers that host the application. Visualize the network graph to find servers that interact with the application. Configure Application Migration Service to launch test instances for all the servers that interact with the application. Perform acceptance tests on the test instances. If no issues are identified, create a move group that is based on the tested servers.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service is used for migration, not specifically for initial dependency visualization and identification based on network traffic.

answers.content: Use AWS Migration Hub and select the servers that host the application. Turn on data exploration in Network Access Analyzer. Use the Network Access Analyzer console to select the servers that host the application. Select a Network Access Scope of port 1000 and note the matching servers. Return to Migration Hub. Create a move group that is based on the findings from Network Access Analyzer.
answers.explanation: No key facts mention Network Access Analyzer as part of this discovery or dependency mapping process, making it unsupported by the provided info.

answers.content: Use AWS Migration Hub and select the servers that host the application. Push the Amazon CloudWalch agent to the identified servers by using the AWS Application Discovery Agent. Export the CloudWatch logs that the agents collect to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs to find servers that communicate on port 1000. Return to Migration Hub Create a move group that is based on the findings from the Athena queries.
answers.explanation: Pushing CloudWatch agent via AWS Application Discovery Agent and querying logs in Athena is an unnecessary manual step; Migration Hub directly supports network visualization, which is preferred.

questions.content: A company's solutions architect is evaluating an AWS workload that was deployed several years ago. The application tier is stateless and runs on a single large Amazon EC2 instance that was launched from an AMI. The application stores data in a MySQL database that runs on a single EC2 instanc The CPU utilization on the application server EC2 instance often reaches 100% and causes the application to stop responding. The company manually installs patches on the instances. Patching has caused downtime in the past. The company needs to make the application highly availabl Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development me?

answers.content: Move the application tier to AWS Lambda functions in the existing VPC. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic across the Lambda functions. Use Amazon GuardDuty to scan the Lambda functions. Migrate the database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility.
answers.explanation: Migrating to Lambda and DocumentDB would require significant redevelopment and is not compatible with the existing MySQL database.

answers.content: Change the EC2 instance type to a smaller Graviton powered instance typUse the existing AMI to create a launch template for an Auto Scaling group. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic across the instances in the Auto Scaling group. Set the Auto Scaling group to scale based on CPU utilization. Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Changing to smaller instances contradicts the need to handle high CPU usage; migrating to DynamoDB requires application changes and does not align with the existing relational model.

answers.content: Move the application tier to containers by using Docker. Run the containers on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with EC2 instances. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic across the ECS cluster. Configure the ECS cluster to scale based on CPU utilization. Migrate the database to Amazon Neptune.
answers.explanation: Migrating to containers and Amazon Neptune requires more development effort and Neptune is not a MySQL-compatible database.

answers.content: Create a now AMI that is configured with AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent). Use the new AMI to create a launch template for an Auto Scaling group. Use smaller instances in the Auto Scaling group. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic across the instances in the Auto Scaling group. Set the Auto Scaling group to scale based on CPU utilization. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL.
answers.explanation: Using an Auto Scaling group with a launch template and an Application Load Balancer addresses the high CPU utilization by distributing load and providing redundancy, eliminating a single point of failure as recommended for high availability. Using smaller instances improves scalability and resource management. Including the AWS Systems Manager Agent enables easier automated patching, avoiding downtime caused by manual patch operations. Migrating the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL provides a highly available, managed relational database service compatible with MySQL, improving database availability and fault tolerancThis solution requires the least development effort as it builds directly on the existing AMI and application architecture without requiring refactoring to containers, Lambda, or different database types.

questions.content: A North American company with headquarters on the East Coast is deploying a new web application running on Amazon EC2 in the us-east-1 Region. The application should dynamically scale to meet user demand and maintain resiliency. Additionally, the application must have disaster recovery capabilities in an active-passive configuration with the us-west-1 Region.  Which steps should a solutions architect take after creating a VPC in the us-east-1 Region?

answers.content: Create a VPC in the us-west-1 Region. Use inter-Region VPC peering to connect both VPCs. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) spanning multiple Availability Zones (AZs) to the VPC in the us-east-1 Region. Deploy EC2 instances across multiple AZs in each Region as part of an Auto Scaling group spanning both VPCs and served by the ALB.
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling groups cannot span multiple VPCs and ALBs do not span multiple Regions; inter-Region VPC peering does not enable this configuration.

answers.content: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) spanning multiple Availability Zones (AZs) to the VPC in the us-east-1 Region. Deploy EC2 instances across multiple AZs as part of an Auto Scaling group served by the ALDeploy the same solution to the us-west-1 Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 record set with a failover routing policy and health checks enabled to provide high availability across both Regions.
answers.explanation: Deploying an ALB spanning multiple AZs in the us-east-1 Region with EC2 instances across multiple AZs in an Auto Scaling group ensures dynamic scaling and resiliency within the primary Region. Deploying the same setup in the us-west-1 Region creates an active-passive disaster recovery configuration consistent with best practices for disaster recovery across Regions. Using Amazon Route 53 with a failover routing policy and health checks provides automatic failover between Regions, maintaining high availability and disaster recovery readiness. The approach does not rely on unsupported configurations such as ALBs spanning Regions or Auto Scaling groups spanning multiple Regions, adhering to AWS service capabilities.

answers.content: Create a VPC in the us-west-1 Region. Use inter-Region VPC peering to connect both VPCs. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that spans both VPCs. Deploy EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones as part of an Auto Scaling group in each VPC served by the ALB. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that points to the ALB.
answers.explanation: ALBs cannot span both VPCs or Regions, so this architecture is not supported and would not provide the required active-passive disaster recovery.

answers.content: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) spanning multiple Availability Zones (AZs) to the VPC in the us-east-1 Region. Deploy EC2 instances across multiple AZs as part of an Auto Scaling group served by the ALB. Deploy the same solution to the us-west-1 Region. Create separate Amazon Route 53 records in each Region that point to the ALB in the Region. Use Route 53 health checks to provide high availability across both Regions.
answers.explanation: Creating separate Route 53 records per Region is less effective than using a failover routing policy with health checks; this approach is less aligned with disaster recovery best practices.

questions.content: An online gaming company needs to optimize the cost of its workloads on AWS. The company uses a dedicated account to host the production environment for its online gaming application and an analytics application.  Amazon EC2 instances host the gaming application and must always be availablThe EC2 instances run all year. The analytics application uses data that is stored in Amazon S3. The analytics application can be interrupted and resumed without issu Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the online gaming application instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the analytics application.
answers.explanation: Using On-Demand Instances for the analytics application is more expensive and does not take advantage of the application's tolerance for interruption.

answers.content: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the online gaming application instances. Use Spot Instances for the analytics application.
answers.explanation: The gaming application requires EC2 instances that must always be available and run all year, making a purchase of EC2 Instance Savings Plan the most cost-effective and reliable option for consistent workloads. The analytics application can be interrupted and resumed, which aligns well with using Spot Instances that are lower cost but can be interrupted. Using Spot Instances for analytics reduces costs significantly without impacting availability since interruptions can be handled. Savings Plans optimize cost for steady state usage such as the gaming application as compared to On-Demand pricing. AWS Service Catalog is not necessary for this use case and does not directly affect cost optimization for these workloads.

answers.content: Use Spot Instances for the online gaming application and the analytics application. Set up a catalog in AWS Service Catalog to provision services at a discount.
answers.explanation: Using Spot Instances for the gaming application risks downtime since it must always be available, violating availability requirements.

answers.content: Use On-Demand Instances for the online gaming application. Use Spot Instances for the analytics application. Set up a catalog in AWS Service Catalog to provision services at a discount.
answers.explanation: Using On-Demand Instances for gaming is not cost-optimized when Savings Plans are available for steady workloads, and the AWS Service Catalog is unrelated to cost savings here.

questions.content: An online magazine will launch its latest edition this month. This edition will be the first to be distributed globally. The magazine's dynamic website currently uses an Application Load Balancer in front of the web tier, a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances for web and application servers, and Amazon Aurora MySQL. Portions of the website include static content and almost all traffic is read-only.  The magazine is expecting a significant spike in internet traffic when the new edition is launched. Optimal performance is a top priority for the week following the launch.  Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to reduce system response times for a global audience? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use logical cross-Region replication to replicate the Aurora MySQL database to a secondary Region. Replace the web servers with Amazon S3. Deploy S3 buckets in cross-Region replication mode.
