answers.explanation: Logical replication is slower and more complex than Aurora Global Database, and replacing web servers entirely with S3 is not suitable for dynamic application logic.

answers.content: Ensure the web and application tiers are each in Auto Scaling groups. Introduce an AWS Direct Connect connection. Deploy the web and application tiers in Regions across the world.
answers.explanation: AWS Direct Connect does not help with global user traffic optimization and is unnecessary for public-facing applications.

answers.content: Migrate the database from Amazon Aurora to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Ensure all three of the application tiers – web, application, and database – are in private subnets.
answers.explanation: Migrating from Aurora to standard RDS reduces scalability and does not support global, low-latency access.

answers.content: Use an Aurora global database for physical cross-Region replication. Use Amazon S3 with cross-Region replication for static content and resources. Deploy the web and application tiers in Regions across the world.
answers.explanation: Aurora Global Database provides fast, physical cross-Region replication with low latency, and S3 cross-Region replication ensures static content is available globally, enabling a true multi-Region architecture.

answers.content: Introduce Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing and Amazon CloudFront distributions. Ensure the web and application tiers are each in Auto Scaling groups.
answers.explanation: Route 53 latency-based routing combined with CloudFront and Auto Scaling web and application tiers directs users to the closest healthy Region and scales automatically, improving performance and availability.

questions.content: A company needs to optimize the cost of its application on AWS. The application uses AWS Lambda functions and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) containers that run on AWS FargatThe application is write-heavy and stores data in an Amazon Aurora MySQL databas The load on the application is not consistent. The application experiences long periods of no usage, followed by sudden and significant increases and decreases in traffic. The database runs on a memory optimized DB instance that cannot handle the load.  A solutions architect must design a solution that can scale to handle the changes in traffic.  Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Add additional read replicas to the databasPurchase Instance Savings Plans and RDS Reserved Instances.
answers.explanation: Adding read replicas and purchasing Reserved Instances doesn't address sudden drops in usage, leading to unnecessary costs during idle periods.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Aurora DB cluster that has multiple writer instances. Purchase Instance Savings Plans.
answers.explanation: Multiple writer instances increase availability but do not scale down during no usage, reducing cost effectiveness.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Aurora global databasPurchase Compute Savings Plans and RDS Reserved instances.
answers.explanation: Aurora global database supports global read scaling but does not address inconsistent local load or cost optimization during low usage.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Aurora Serverless v1. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.
answers.explanation: Aurora Serverless v1 provides on-demand, auto-scaling database capacity which is ideal for variable and unpredictable workloads, enabling cost optimization during periods of no usagCompute Savings Plans offer cost savings for compute usage that fits well with serverless or variable load environments. The application experiences fluctuating traffic, so a solution that scales automatically without prepaid capacity (like Reserved Instances) is more cost-effectivManaged services such as Aurora Serverless reduce operational overhead associated with manual scaling or adding read replicas.

questions.content: A company operates a fleet of servers on premises and operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in its organization in AWS Organizations. The company's AWS accounts contain hundreds of VPCs. The company wants to connect its AWS accounts to its on-premises network. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections are already established to a single AWS account. The company wants to control which VPCs can communicate with other VPCs.  Which combination of steps will achieve this level of control with the LEAST operational effort? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a transit gateway in an AWS account. Share the transit gateway across accounts by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
answers.explanation: A Transit Gateway acts as a central hub (cloud router) for connecting VPCs and on-premises networks \[7\]. Since the company has hundreds of VPCs across multiple AWS accounts in an organization, creating a single TGW and sharing it across accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) is the most operationally efficient way to enable connectivity and centralize network management

answers.content: Configure attachments to all VPCs and VPNs.
answers.explanation: Once the TGW is created and shared, all VPCs and the existing VPN connection must be attached to the Transit Gateway. Attachments are necessary for resources (VPCs, VPNs) to communicate through the TGW

answers.content: Setup transit gateway route tables. Associate the VPCs and VPNs with the route tables.
answers.explanation: Transit Gateway route tables control how network traffic is routed between attachments (VPCs and VPNs) \[4\]. By creating custom route tables and associating specific VPC or VPN attachments with those tables, you can implement the required granular control over which VPCs can communicate with other VPCs or the on-premises network \[1\], \[2\]. This achieves the requirement of controlling communication with the least operational effort, as opposed to managing routing rules in hundreds of individual VPCs or using VPC peering.

answers.content: Configure VPC peering between the VPCs.
answers.explanation: VPC peering does not scale well with hundreds of VPCs and offers less centralized control.

answers.content: Configure attachments between the VPCs and VPNs.
answers.explanation: Redundant with B; 'Configure attachments' was already covered, and separating VPC and VPN attachments does not add value compared to centralized attachments managed in B.

answers.content: Setup route tables on the VPCs and VPNs.
answers.explanation: Setting up route tables on individual VPCs and VPNs requires manual configuration and ongoing management across hundreds of VPCs, which creates high operational overhead. It also does not provide centralized, scalable control over inter-VPC communication, making it unsuitable for the “least operational effort” requirement.

questions.content: A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application consists of a single application server and a Microsoft SQL Server database server. Each server is deployed on a VMware VM that consumes 500 TB of data across multiple attached volumes.  The company has established a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection from the closest AWS Region to its on-premises data center. The Direct Connect connection is not currently in use by other services.  Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to migrate the application with the LEAST amount of downtime? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the database server VM to AWS.
answers.explanation: AWS SMS is less suitable for large database server migrations compared to AWS DMS for SQL Server databases.

answers.content: Use VM Import/Export to import the application server VM.
answers.explanation: VM Import/Export is not ideal for minimizing downtime since it requires VM export and import operations that can be time-consuming.

answers.content: Export the VM images to an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device.
answers.explanation: Using Snowball Edge for 500 TB data requires manual handling and does not minimize downtime as effectively as online services like SMS and DMS.

answers.content: Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the application server VM to AWS.
answers.explanation: Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the application server VM to AWS.AWS SMS automates the incremental replication of live server volumes to AWS, significantly reducing server downtime at cutover for the application server. This is crucial for a large 500 TB VM migration where the initial transfer is substantial. AWS SMS continuously replicates changes, minimizing the final cutover time.Source: <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/apn/aws-server-migration-service-server-migration-to-the-cloud-made-easy/>

answers.content: Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to migrate the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance.
answers.explanation: Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to migrate the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance.AWS DMS is specifically designed to migrate databases with minimal downtime. It uses Change Data Capture (CDC) to continuously replicate ongoing changes from the source Microsoft SQL Server database to the target Amazon RDS DB instance (SQL Server or compatible engine) while the migration is in progress. This enables a near zero-downtime cutover for the database component.Source: <https://teleglobals.com/blog/migrating-databases-to-aws-with-minimal-downtime>

questions.content: A company needs to aggregate Amazon CloudWatch logs from its AWS accounts into one central logging account. The collected logs must remain in the AWS Region of creation. The central logging account will then process the logs, normalize the logs into standard output format, and stream the output logs to a security tool for more processing.  A solutions architect must design a solution that can handle a large volume of logging data that needs to be ingested. Less logging will occur outside normal business hours than during normal business hours. The logging solution must scale with the anticipated load. The solutions architect has decided to use an AWS Control Tower design to handle the multi-account logging process.  Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet the requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a destination Amazon Kinesis data stream in the central logging account.
answers.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams can ingest very large, variable volumes of log data and scale automatically. It is regional, so logs stay in the Region where they are created.

answers.content: Create a destination Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue in the central logging account.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch Logs cannot directly stream logs to SQS using subscription filters. SQS is not a supported destination for CloudWatch Logs subscriptions.

answers.content: Create an IAM role that grants Amazon CloudWatch Logs the permission to add data to the Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create a trust policy. Specify the trust policy in the IAM rolIn each member account, create a subscription filter for each log group to send data to the Kinesis data stream.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch Logs supports cross-account subscription filters to Kinesis Data Streams using an IAM role with a trust policy. Each log group needs its own subscription filter, which matches how CloudWatch Logs works.

answers.content: Create an IAM role that grants Amazon CloudWatch Logs the permission to add data to the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a trust policy. Specify the trust policy in the IAM role. In each member account, create a single subscription filter for all log groups to send data to the SQS queue.
answers.explanation: This option is invalid because CloudWatch Logs does not support SQS as a subscription destination, and you also cannot create one subscription filter for all log groups.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to normalize the logs in the member accounts and to write the logs to the security tool.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda is a serverless, scalable compute service that is ideal for processing records from a Kinesis Data Stream, performing the necessary log normalization, and then writing the processed logs to the final destination (the security tool). Since the logging load is anticipated to vary, Lambda's automatic scaling is beneficial.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to normalize the logs in the central logging account and to write the logs to the security tool.
answers.explanation: Processing logs in each member account breaks the requirement for centralized logging and processing. It also increases operational overhead and does not align with the Control Tower centralized logging model.

questions.content: A company runs applications in hundreds of production AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and has a centralized backup operation that uses AWS Backup.  The company is concerned about ransomware attacks. To address this concern, the company has created a new policy that all backups must be resilient to breaches of privileged-user credentials in any production account.  Which combination of steps will meet this new requirement? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Implement cross-account backup with AWS Backup vaults in designated non-production accounts.
answers.explanation: Storing backups in a separate account protects them from compromise if privileged credentials in a production account are breached, which is a core ransomware-resilience best practice.

answers.content: Add an SCP that restricts the modification of AWS Backup vaults.
answers.explanation: An SCP prevents even highly privileged users in production accounts from deleting or altering backups or vault settings, enforcing centralized, organization-wide protection.

answers.content: Implement AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode.
answers.explanation: Vault Lock in compliance mode makes backups immutable for the retention period, ensuring attackers cannot delete or shorten retention even with admin credentials.

answers.content: Implement least privilege access for the IAM service role that is assigned to AWS Backup.
answers.explanation: Good security hygiene, but does not guarantee immutability or cross-account protection against compromised credentials.

answers.content: Configure the backup frequency, lifecycle, and retention period to ensure that at least one backup always exists in the cold tier.
answers.explanation: it does not prevent a malicious actor from deleting or modifying backups, so it does not protect against credential compromise.

answers.content: Configure AWS Backup to write all backups to an Amazon S3 bucket in a designated non-production account. Ensure that the S3 bucket has S3 Object Lock enabled.
answers.explanation: invalid because AWS Backup does not store backups directly in customer-managed S3 buckets, making this option technically incorrect.

questions.content: A company is migrating its infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. The company must comply with a variety of regulatory standards for different projects. The company needs a multi-account environment.  A solutions architect needs to prepare the baseline infrastructurThe solution must provide a consistent baseline of management and security, but it must allow flexibility for different compliance requirements within various AWS accounts. The solution also needs to integrate with the existing on-premises Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) server.  Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Create a single SCP for least privilege access across all accounts. Create a single OU for all accounts. Configure an IAM identity provider for federation with the on-premises AD FS server. Configure a central logging account with a defined process for log generating services to send log events to the central account. Enable AWS Config in the central account with conformance packs for all accounts.
answers.explanation: Manually creating SCP and OU structure with a single central logging account leads to more operational overhead and less flexibility than AWS Control Tower.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Enable AWS Control Tower on the organization. Review included controls (guardrails) for SCPs. Check AWS Config for areas that require additions. Add OUs as necessary. Connect AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to the on-premises AD FS server.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower provides a managed baseline for multi-account environments including security guardrails via SCPs, reducing operational overhead. AWS Control Tower supports OU management and flexible compliance through customization of guardrails and AWS Config, fitting the requirement for varied compliance across accounts. Connecting AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to on-premises AD FS provides a secure, managed, and scalable federated identity solution, which aligns with best practices. This solution uses managed AWS services to ensure security and management with minimal operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Create SCPs for least privilege access. Create an OU structure, and use it to group AWS accounts. Connect AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to the on-premises AD FS server. Configure a central logging account with a defined process for log generating services to send log events to the central account. Enable AWS Config in the central account with aggregators and conformance packs.
answers.explanation: While comprehensive, it involves more manual setup and does not use AWS Control Tower, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Enable AWS Control Tower on the organization. Review included controls (guardrails) for SCPs. Check AWS Config for areas that require additions. Configure an IAM identity provider for federation with the on-premises AD FS server.
answers.explanation: Does not include using AWS IAM Identity Center for federated access, which is preferred over directly configuring an IAM identity provider for AD FS.

questions.content: A company recently migrated a web application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The web application infrastructure consists of an Amazon CloudFront distribution that routes to an Application Load Balancer (ALB), with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to process requests. A recent security audit revealed that the web application is accessible by using both CloudFront and ALB endpoints. However, the company requires that the web application must be accessible only by using the CloudFront endpoint.  Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?

answers.content: Create a new security group and attach it to the CloudFront distribution. Update the ALB security group ingress to allow access only from the CloudFront security group.
answers.explanation: Cannot attach a security group directly to a CloudFront distribution; this is not supported.

answers.content: Update ALB security group ingress to allow access only from the com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing CloudFront managed prefix list.
answers.explanation: Updating the ALB security group ingress to allow access only from the CloudFront managed prefix list provides a secure, maintenance-free way to restrict access to the ALB only through CloudFront. Using the CloudFront managed prefix list is a managed AWS service solution, which is preferred over manual IP management. It enforces the requirement that the web application is accessible only via CloudFront, aligning with security best practices by blocking direct ALB access.

answers.content: Create a com.amazonaws.region.elasticloadbalancing VPC interface endpoint for Elastic Load Balancing. Update the ALB scheme from internet-facing to internal.
answers.explanation: Changing the ALB scheme to internal and creating a VPC endpoint requires more effort and architectural changes, not the least effort.

answers.content: Extract CloudFront IPs from the AWS provided ip-ranges.json document. Update ALB security group ingress to allow access only from CloudFront IPs.
answers.explanation: Manually updating ALB security group with IP addresses from ip-ranges.json is error-prone and requires constant updates; less preferable than managed prefix lists.

questions.content: A company is migrating an application to the AWS Cloud. The application runs in an on-premises data center and writes thousands of images into a mounted NFS file system each night. After the company migrates the application, the company will host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance with a mounted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.  The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection to AWS. Before the migration cutover, a solutions architect must build a process that will replicate the newly created on-premises images to the EFS file system.  What is the MOST operationally efficient way to replicate the images?

answers.content: Configure a periodic process to run the aws s3 sync command from the on-premises file system to Amazon S3. Configure an AWS Lambda function to process event notifications from Amazon S3 and copy the images from Amazon S3 to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Involves multiple steps and uses Lambda unnecessarily, reducing operational efficiency.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway with an NFS mount point. Mount the file gateway file system on the on-premises server. Configure a process to periodically copy the images to the mount point.
answers.explanation: Storage Gateway file gateway requires manual copying rather than automated sync; less operationally efficient.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent to an on-premises server that has access to the NFS file system. Send data over the Direct Connect connection to an S3 bucket by using a public VIF. Configure an AWS Lambda function to process event notifications from Amazon S3 and copy the images from Amazon S3 to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Uses a public VIF and an intermediate S3 bucket with Lambda processing, adding complexity and security risks.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent to an on-premises server that has access to the NFS file system. Send data over the Direct Connect connection to an AWS PrivateLink interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EFS by using a private VIF. Configure a DataSync scheduled task to send the images to the EFS file system every 24 hours.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is a managed service designed specifically for automating and efficiently replicating large amounts of data. DataSync supports direct transfer to Amazon EFS, eliminating the need for intermediate storage such as Amazon S3. Using a private VIF and AWS PrivateLink for Amazon EFS ensures secure, private network communication over Direct Connect, aligning with security best practices. Scheduling DataSync to run every 24 hours provides an operationally efficient and automated replication process.

questions.content: A company has developed a mobile gamThe backend for the game runs on several virtual machines located in an on-premises data center. The business logic is exposed using a REST API with multiple functions. Player session data is stored in central file storagBackend services use different API keys for throttling and to distinguish between live and test traffic.  The load on the game backend varies throughout the day. During peak hours, the server capacity is not sufficient. There are also latency issues when fetching player session data. Management has asked a solutions architect to present a cloud architecture that can handle the game’s varying load and provide low-latency data access. The API model should not be changed.  Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Implement the REST API using a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Run the business logic on an Amazon EC2 instance behind the NLB. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.
answers.explanation: Network Load Balancer does not provide advanced REST API features like path-based routing; Aurora Serverless may not provide as low latency as DynamoDB for session data.

answers.content: Implement the REST API using an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
answers.explanation: Using an Application Load Balancer (ALB) is appropriate for REST APIs, aligning with the requirement to keep the API model unchanged. Running business logic in AWS Lambda allows automatic scaling to handle varying loads without managing servers, addressing peak load issues. Storing player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity provides low-latency access and automatic scaling, improving performance over central file storagThis solution uses fully managed AWS services optimized for scalability and low latency, following AWS best practices.

answers.content: Implement the REST API using Amazon API Gateway. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
answers.explanation: API Gateway differs from the existing REST API model, which management requested to keep unchanged.

answers.content: Implement the REST API using AWS AppSync. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.
answers.explanation: AWS AppSync uses GraphQL, which changes the API model; Aurora Serverless's latency is not optimal for session data compared to DynamoDB.

questions.content: A financial services company runs a complex, multi-tier application on Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions. The application stores temporary data in Amazon S3. The S3 objects are valid for only 45 minutes and are deleted after 24 hours.  The company deploys each version of the application by launching an AWS CloudFormation stack. The stack creates all resources that are required to run the application. When the company deploys and validates a new application version, the company deletes the CloudFormation stack of the old version.  The company recently tried to delete the CloudFormation stack of an old application version, but the operation failed. An analysis shows that CloudFormation failed to delete an existing S3 bucket. A solutions architect needs to resolve this issue without making major changes to the application's architectur Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Implement a Lambda function that deletes all files from a given S3 bucket. Integrate this Lambda function as a custom resource into the CloudFormation stack. Ensure that the custom resource has a DependsOn attribute that points to the S3 bucket's resource.
answers.explanation: CloudFormation cannot delete an S3 bucket if it contains objects, causing the stack deletion to fail. Implementing a Lambda function as a custom resource that deletes all objects in the bucket ensures the bucket is emptied before deletion. Using the DependsOn attribute makes sure the Lambda function runs in the correct order relative to the bucket resource, enabling successful deletion. This approach avoids major architectural changes and aligns with AWS best practices for managing S3 bucket deletion in CloudFormation.

answers.content: Modify the CloudFormation template to provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store the temporary files there instead of in Amazon S3. Configure the Lambda functions to run in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system to the EC2 instances and Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Replacing S3 with Amazon EFS is a major architectural change, violating the 'no major changes' requirement.

answers.content: Modify the CloudF ormation stack to create an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires all objects 45 minutes after creation. Add a DependsOn attribute that points to the S3 bucket’s resource.
answers.explanation: S3 Lifecycle rules do not delete the bucket itself and may not align timings precisely to enable stack deletion; does not directly resolve bucket deletion failure.

answers.content: Modify the CloudFormation stack to attach a DeletionPolicy attribute with a value of Delete to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: DeletionPolicy 'Delete' is the default and does not empty the bucket; it does not solve the failure caused by non-empty buckets.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The database for the application stores structured product data and temporary user session data. The company needs to decouple the product data from the user session data. The company also needs to implement replication in another AWS Region for disaster recovery.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the HIGHEST performance?

answers.content: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with separate schemas to host the product data and the user session data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region.
answers.explanation: Using separate schemas in a single RDS instance does not decouple data at the service level; read replicas aid disaster recovery but performance for session data may lag.

answers.content: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create a global datastore in Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to host the user session data.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Memcached does not offer a global datastore or cross-Region replication, failing the replication requirement for session data.

answers.content: Create two Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Use one global table to host the product data. Use the other global table to host the user session data. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for caching.
answers.explanation: Using two separate Amazon DynamoDB global tables natively decouples product data and user session data, meeting the requirement to separate them. DynamoDB global tables provide multi-Region replication inherently, supporting disaster recovery. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) offers high performance caching, addressing the need for the highest performancManaged services like DynamoDB and DAX align with AWS best practices for operational efficiency and security.

answers.content: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create an Amazon DynamoDB global table to host the user session data.
answers.explanation: Mixing RDS and DynamoDB can work but does not optimize performance for sessions as well as two DynamoDB global tables with DAX; additional operational complexity is introduced.

questions.content: A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application uses MongoDB as a key-value databasAccording to the company's technical guidelines, all Amazon EC2 instances must be hosted in a private subnet without an internet connection. In addition, all connectivity between applications and databases must be encrypted. The database must be able to scale based on demand.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) tables for the application with Provisioned IOPS volumes. Use the instance endpoint to connect to Amazon DocumentDB.
answers.explanation: Using the instance endpoint does not support failover and scaling as effectively as the cluster endpoint.

answers.content: Create new Amazon DynamoDB tables for the application with on-demand capacity. Use a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB to connect to the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is not MongoDB compatible and does not meet the requirement for MongoDB compatibility.

answers.content: Create new Amazon DynamoDB tables for the application with on-demand capacity. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB to connect to the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is not MongoDB compatible and using an interface VPC endpoint is less optimal than a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB, plus it won't meet MongoDB compatibility.

answers.content: Create new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) tables for the application with Provisioned IOPS volumes. Use the cluster endpoint to connect to Amazon DocumentDB.
answers.explanation: Amazon DocumentDB supports MongoDB compatibility, meeting the requirement to use MongoDB as a key-value databasUsing the cluster endpoint ensures proper connection to Amazon DocumentDB and supports scaling based on demand. Provisioned IOPS volumes ensure performance and stability required by the application. Hosting EC2 instances in private subnets without internet connection is compatible with accessing the cluster endpoint within the VPC securely. Connectivity to Amazon DocumentDB can be encrypted natively, meeting the encryption requirement.

questions.content: A company processes environmental data. The company has set up sensors to provide a continuous stream of data from different areas in a city. The data is available in JSON format.  The company wants to use an AWS solution to send the data to a database that does not require fixed schemas for storagThe data must be sent in real tim Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to send the data to Amazon Redshift.
answers.explanation: Amazon Redshift requires a fixed schema and is not optimized for flexible JSON data without schema.

answers.content: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to send the data to Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams alone cannot directly send data to DynamoDB; also DynamoDB is a key-value/NoSQL store but the integration is less direct and managed than Firehose to Keyspaces.

answers.content: Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to send the data to Amazon Aurora.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora is a relational database requiring fixed schemas, which conflicts with the requirement for flexible schema storage.

answers.content: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to send the data to Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra).
answers.explanation: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is a NoSQL database that supports flexible schemas, suitable for JSON data without fixed schemas. Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose can deliver streaming data in near real-time to managed data stores like Amazon Keyspaces. The solution uses managed AWS services that support real-time data ingestion and flexible schema storagThis meets the requirement of processing continuous streams of JSON data with a database that does not require fixed schemas.

questions.content: A solutions architect needs to migrate an on-premises legacy application to AWS. The application runs on two servers behind a load balancer. The application requires a license file that is associated with the MAC address of the server's network adapter It takes the software vendor 12 hours to send new license files. The application also uses configuration files with a static IP address to access a database server, host names are not supported.  Given these requirements, which combination of steps should be taken to implement highly available architecture for the application servers in AWS? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a pool of ENIs. Request license files from the vendor for the pool, and store the license files in Amazon S3. Create a bootstrap automation script to download a license file and attach the corresponding ENI to an Amazon EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: The application license is tied to the server's MAC address, and obtaining a new license takes 12 hours. To achieve high availability and rapid replacement of failed instances without waiting 12 hours, you must ensure the replacement instance uses a licensed MAC address. In AWS, the MAC address is associated with an Elastic Network Interface (ENI). By creating a pool of ENIs, requesting licenses for those ENIs, and storing the licenses and ENIs for use, a new EC2 instance can be launched quickly and have a pre-licensed ENI (with its static MAC address) attached via a bootstrap script. The license file can be stored in Amazon S3 for easy access during the instance bootstrap process.Reference: Elastic Network Interfaces documentation confirms that an ENI has a persistent MAC address.

answers.content: Create a pool of ENIs. Request license files from the vendor for the pool, store the license files on an Amazon EC2 instancCreate an AMI from the instance and use this AMI for all future EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Storing license files on an EC2 instance and using that instance to create AMIs is not scalable or as manageable as using a pool of ENIs and S3, and it does not ensure the correct MAC addresses persist accurately.

answers.content: Create a bootstrap automation script to request a new license file from the vendor .When the response is received, apply the license file to an Amazon EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Automating license file requests from the vendor is not practical given the vendor takes 12 hours to respond; proactive license management with a pool of ENIs is required.

answers.content: Edit the bootstrap automation script to read the database server IP address from the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and inject the value into the local configuration files.
answers.explanation: The application uses configuration files with a static IP address to access a database server, and hostnames are not supported. This requirement means the application configuration must be updated upon launch if the database IP address ever changes (e.g., in a failover or disaster recovery scenario) or if the application needs to scale in different environments. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store is a highly available and secure way to store configuration data, like the static database IP address. A bootstrap script can read the current IP address from the Parameter Store and inject it into the application's local configuration files during startup, ensuring the new instance always connects to the correct database endpoint. This decouples the configuration from the AMI and allows for centralized management and high availability.Reference: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store documentation highlights its use for configuration data and secrets management.

answers.content: Edit an Amazon EC2 instance to include the database server IP address in the configuration files and re-create the AMI to use for all future EC2 stances.
answers.explanation: Embedding static database IPs into an AMI requires AMI rebuilding for changes, reducing flexibility and increasing operational overhead; Parameter Store is preferred.

questions.content: A solutions architect is determining the DNS strategy for an existing VPC. The VPC is provisioned to use the 10.24.34.0/24 CIDR block. The VPC also uses Amazon Route 53 Resolver for DNS. New requirements mandate that DNS queries must use private hosted zones. Additionally instances that have public IP addresses must receive corresponding public hostnames  Which solution will meet these requirements to ensure that the domain names are correctly resolved within the VPC?

answers.content: Create a private hosted zonActivate the enableDnsSupport attribute and the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPC. Update the VPC DHCP options set to include domain-name-servers=10.24.34.2.
answers.explanation: Setting domain-name-servers to 10.24.34.2 points to a custom DNS server rather than AWS-provided DNS, which is not recommended.

answers.content: Create a private hosted zone Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC. Activate the enableDnsSupport attribute and the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPC. Create a new VPC DHCP options set, and configure domain-name-servers=AmazonProvidedDNS. Associate the new DHCP options set with the VPC.
answers.explanation: Creating a private hosted zone and associating it with the VPC ensures DNS queries use private hosted zones as required. Activating enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames allows instances to resolve DNS and get hostnames, including public hostnames for instances with public IPs. Using the AmazonProvidedDNS for the DHCP options set ensures the VPC DNS resolver is used correctly, complying with AWS best practices for DNS resolution in VPCs.

answers.content: Deactivate the enableDnsSupport attribute for the VPActivate the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPCreate a new VPC DHCP options set, and configure doman-name-servers=10.24.34.2. Associate the new DHCP options set with the VPC.
answers.explanation: Deactivating enableDnsSupport disables DNS resolution in the VPC, which is contrary to the requirement for DNS queries to use private hosted zones.

answers.content: Create a private hosted zonAssociate the private hosted zone with the VPC. Activate the enableDnsSupport attribute for the VPC. Deactivate the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPC. Update the VPC DHCP options set to include domain-name-servers=AmazonProvidedDNS.
answers.explanation: Deactivating enableDnsHostnames prevents instances from receiving hostnames, which conflicts with the requirement that instances with public IPs must receive public hostnames.

questions.content: An online retail company hosts its stateful web-based application and MySQL database in an on-premises data center on a single server. The company wants to increase its customer base by conducting more marketing campaigns and promotions. In preparation, the company wants to migrate its application and database to AWS to increase the reliability of its architectur Which solution should provide the HIGHEST level of reliability?

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instancDeploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in Amazon Neptune
answers.explanation: Amazon Neptune is not designed for session storage; it is a graph database, so it is not optimal for session management.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication group.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora MySQL provides higher availability and reliability compared to standard RDS MySQL or MariaDB due to its distributed, fault-tolerant, self-healing storage system. Deploying the application in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer is a best practice for high reliability and scalability. Storing sessions in Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication group ensures session data durability and high availability. The combination in option B aligns with AWS managed services that improve operational reliability and availability.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility). Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer Store sessions in Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
answers.explanation: Amazon DocumentDB is a different database engine (MongoDB-compatible) not compatible with the given MySQL database, and using Kinesis Data Firehose for session storage is inappropriate.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS MariaDB Multi-AZ DB instancDeploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS MariaDB is less reliable than Aurora MySQL for high availability, and Memcached does not provide replication or persistence, reducing session reliability.

questions.content: A research company is running daily simulations in the AWS Cloud to meet high demand. The simulations run on several hundred Amazon EC2 instances that are based on Amazon Linux 2. Occasionally, a simulation gets stuck and requires a cloud operations engineer to solve the problem by connecting to an EC2 instance through SSH.  Company policy states that no EC2 instance can use the same SSH key and that all connections must be logged in AWS CloudTrail.  How can a solutions architect meet these requirements?

answers.content: Launch new EC2 instances, and generate an individual SSH key for each instancStore the SSH key in AWS Secrets Manager. Create a new IAM policy, and attach it to the engineers’ IAM role with an Allow statement for the GetSecretValue action. Instruct the engineers to fetch the SSH key from Secrets Manager when they connect through any SSH client.
answers.explanation: Storing SSH private keys in Secrets Manager increases risk and operational complexity; AWS best practices favor temporary credentials and managed services over manual key distribution.

answers.content: Create an AWS Systems Manager document to run commands on EC2 instances to set a new unique SSH key. Create a new IAM policy, and attach it to the engineers’ IAM role with an Allow statement to run Systems Manager documents. Instruct the engineers to run the document to set an SSH key and to connect through any SSH client.
answers.explanation: Manually running Systems Manager documents to set SSH keys does not ensure unique keys per instance automatically, and does not inherently provide connection logging and temporary credential management.

answers.content: Launch new EC2 instances without setting up any SSH key for the instances. Set up EC2 Instance Connect on each instancCreate a new IAM policy, and attach it to the engineers’ IAM role with an Allow statement for the SendSSHPublicKey action. Instruct the engineers to connect to the instance by using a browser-based SSH client from the EC2 console.
answers.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect enables unique, per-user, per-instance SSH key handling without storing long-term SSH keys on instances, meeting the requirement that no EC2 instance uses the same SSH key. Using EC2 Instance Connect integrates with IAM permissions, allowing control over who can SSH into instances via the SendSSHPublicKey action, thus aligning with AWS best practices favoring temporary security credentials. Connections through the browser-based SSH client are logged in AWS CloudTrail, fulfilling the requirement that all connections must be logged. This solution avoids managing and rotating SSH keys manually or via Secrets Manager, which is less secure and more operationally complex.

answers.content: Set up AWS Secrets Manager to store the EC2 SSH key. Create a new AWS Lambda function to create a new SSH key and to call AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to set the SSH key on the EC2 instancConfigure Secrets Manager to use the Lambda function for automatic rotation once daily. Instruct the engineers to fetch the SSH key from Secrets Manager when they connect through any SSH client.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda to rotate SSH keys daily and storing them in Secrets Manager introduces unnecessary complexity and risk; temporary, IAM-based access via EC2 Instance Connect is preferred.

questions.content: A company has application services that have been containerized and deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances with public IPs. An Apache Kafka cluster has been deployed to the EC2 instances. A PostgreSQL database has been migrated to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company expects a significant increase of orders on its platform when a new version of its flagship product is released.  What changes to the current architecture will reduce operational overhead and support the product release?

answers.content: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create additional read replicas for the DB instancCreate Amazon Kinesis data streams and configure the application services to use the data streams. Store and serve static content directly from Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances directly does not reduce operational overhead as well as managed container services and lacks Multi-AZ DB deployment.

answers.content: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Deploy the DB instance in Multi-AZ mode and enable storage auto scaling. Create Amazon Kinesis data streams and configure the application services to use the data streams. Store and serve static content directly from Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Using Kinesis data streams instead of managed Kafka does not address operational overhead; Kafka operations remain manual.

answers.content: Deploy the application on a Kubernetes cluster created on the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Deploy the DB instance in Multi-AZ mode and enable storage auto scaling. Create an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster and configure the application services to use the cluster. Store static content in Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: Running Kubernetes on EC2 instances increases operational overhead compared to managed EKS with Fargate; also, no DB read replicas for scaling reads.

answers.content: Deploy the application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate and enable auto scaling behind an Application Load Balancer. Create additional read replicas for the DB instancCreate an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster and configure the application services to use the cluster. Store static content in Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EKS with AWS Fargate reduces operational overhead by removing the need to manage EC2 instances directly for the containerized application. Enabling auto scaling behind an Application Load Balancer supports the expected increase in orders by automatically adjusting capacity. Creating additional read replicas for the RDS PostgreSQL instance improves read scalability relevant for increased demand. Migrating Kafka to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) removes the operational burden of managing Kafka on EC2 instances. Serving static content from Amazon S3 behind Amazon CloudFront provides scalable, low-latency content delivery.

questions.content: A large payroll company recently merged with a small staffing company. The unified company now has multiple business units, each with its own existing AWS account.  A solutions architect must ensure that the company can centrally manage the billing and access policies for all the AWS accounts. The solutions architect configures AWS Organizations by sending an invitation to all member accounts of the company from a centralized management account.  What should the solutions architect do next to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create the OrganizationAccountAccess IAM group in each member account. Include the necessary IAM roles for each administrator.
answers.explanation: IAM groups do not provide cross-account access and are not the recommended method for centralized account management.

answers.content: Create the OrganizationAccountAccessPolicy IAM policy in each member account. Connect the member accounts to the management account by using cross-account access.
answers.explanation: An IAM policy alone does not enable cross-account access; an IAM role with trust policy is required to delegate access.

answers.content: Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in each member account. Grant permission to the management account to assume the IAM role.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations uses a management account (formerly master account) to centrally manage member accounts. To allow the management account to assume roles in member accounts, a commonly recommended best practice is to create an IAM role named OrganizationAccountAccessRole in each member account. This role has permissions that allow the management account to assume it and perform administrative tasks, enabling centralized billing and policy management. Creating the OrganizationAccountAccessRole and granting permission to the management account aligns with AWS best practices and simplifies secure cross-account management.

answers.content: Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the management account. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM rolAssign the IAM role to the administrators in each member account.
answers.explanation: Creating the role in the management account, rather than member accounts, does not grant required access to manage those member accounts.

questions.content: A company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy a private REST API that will provide access to sensitive data. The API must be accessible only from an application that is deployed in a VPC. The company deploys the API successfully. However, the API is not accessible from an Amazon EC2 instance that is deployed in the VPC.  Which solution will provide connectivity between the EC2 instance and the API?

answers.content: Create an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. Attach an endpoint policy that allows apigateway:* actions. Disable private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint. Configure an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC. Use the VPC endpoint's DNS name to access the API.
answers.explanation: Disabling private DNS naming is incorrect; private DNS naming should be enabled for seamless access via standard API Gateway DNS names.

answers.content: Create an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. Attach an endpoint policy that allows the execute-api:Invoke action. Enable private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint. Configure an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC endpoint. Use the API endpoint’s DNS names to access the API.
answers.explanation: Creating an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway enables private connectivity from the VPC to the private API. The endpoint policy must allow the execute-api:Invoke action to permit invoking the API. Enabling private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint ensures the default API Gateway DNS names resolve correctly within the VPC, simplifying access. Configuring an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC endpoint ensures the requests are allowed on the API Gateway sidUsing the API endpoint's DNS names is best practice when private DNS naming is enabled.

answers.content: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and a VPC link. Configure private integration between API Gateway and the NLB. Use the API endpoint’s DNS names to access the API.
answers.explanation: Using a Network Load Balancer and VPC link is for private integrations inside API Gateway, not for accessing private APIs from EC2 inside the same VPC.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a VPC Link. Configure private integration between API Gateway and the ALB. Use the ALB endpoint’s DNS name to access the API.
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancer and VPC link configurations are for backend integrations, not for accessing private REST APIs from EC2 within the VPC.

questions.content: A company is running a workload that consists of thousands of Amazon EC2 instances. The workload is running in a VPC that contains several public subnets and private subnets. The public subnets have a route for 0.0.0.0/0 to an existing internet gateway. The private subnets have a route for 0.0.0.0/0 to an existing NAT gateway.  A solutions architect needs to migrate the entire fleet of EC2 instances to use IPv6. The EC2 instances that are in private subnets must not be accessible from the public internet.  What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Update the existing VPC, and associate a custom IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Update all the VPC route tables, and add a route for ::/0 to the internet gateway.
answers.explanation: Routing ::/0 to an internet gateway from private subnets exposes instances to inbound internet access, violating security requirements.

answers.content: Update the existing VPC, and associate an Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Update the VPC route tables for all private subnets, and add a route for ::/0 to the NAT gateway.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway does not support IPv6 traffic; routing IPv6 (::/0) traffic to a NAT gateway is invalid.

answers.content: Update the existing VPC, and associate an Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Create an egress-only internet gateway. Update the VPC route tables for all private subnets, and add a route for ::/0 to the egress-only internet gateway.
answers.explanation: For workloads on private subnets using IPv6, to prevent public internet access while still allowing outbound traffic, AWS best practice is to use an egress-only internet gateway. An egress-only internet gateway allows outbound IPv6 traffic from instances in a VPC to the internet but prevents inbound traffic initiated from the internet, maintaining security for private subnets. Associating an Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block is standard and preferred over custom blocks. Routing ::/0 to the egress-only internet gateway on private subnets ensures compliance with the requirement that private instances are not publicly accessible.

answers.content: Update the existing VPC, and associate a custom IPV6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Create a new NAT gateway, and enable IPV6 support. Update the VPC route tables for all private subnets, and add a route for ::/0 to the IPv6-enabled NAT gateway.
answers.explanation: NAT gateways do not support IPv6, so enabling IPv6 on a NAT gateway and routing ::/0 traffic there is not feasible.

questions.content: A company is managing many AWS accounts by using an organization in AWS Organizations. Different business units in the company run applications on Amazon EC2 instances. All the EC2 instances must have a BusinessUnit tag so that the company can track the cost for each business unit.  A recent audit revealed that some instances were missing this tag. The company manually added the missing tag to the instances.  What should a solutions architect do to enforce the tagging requirement in the future?

answers.content: Enable tag policies in the organization. Create a tag policy for the BusinessUnit tag. Ensure that compliance with tag key capitalization is turned off. Implement the tag policy for the ec2:instance resource typAttach the tag policy to the root of the organization.
answers.explanation: Enabling tag policies within AWS Organizations enforces tag compliance across all accounts and resources. Creating a tag policy for the BusinessUnit tag and attaching it to the root of the organization ensures centralized enforcement for all EC2 instances. Ensuring compliance with tag key capitalization is turned off avoids unnecessary failures due to case sensitivity. Tag policies are the managed AWS feature designed for enforcing tagging standards, which aligns with best practices prioritizing security and manageability.

answers.content: Enable tag policies in the organization. Create a tag policy for the BusinessUnit tag. Ensure that compliance with tag key capitalization is turned on. Implement the tag policy for the ec2:instance resource typAttach the tag policy to the organization's management account.
answers.explanation: Attaching the tag policy only to the management account does not enforce it across all accounts in the organization.

answers.content: Create an SCP and attach the SCP to the root of the organization. Include the following statement in the SCP: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02/image8.png]
answers.explanation: Using SCP for tag enforcement is not advisable over tag policies; SCPs do not directly enforce tag presence on resource creation.

answers.content: Create an SCP and attach the SCP to the organization’s management account. Include the following statement in the SCP: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02/image9.png]
answers.explanation: Attaching SCP to the management account limits scope and SCPs are not designed for detailed tag enforcement, unlike tag policies.

questions.content: A company’s CISO has asked a solutions architect to re-engineer the company's current CI/CD practices to make sure patch deployments to its application can happen as quickly as possible with minimal downtime if vulnerabilities are discovered. The company must also be able to quickly roll back a change in case of errors.  The web application is deployed in a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company is currently using GitHub to host the application source code, and has configured an AWS CodeBuild project to build the application. The company also intends to use AWS CodePipeline to trigger builds from GitHub commits using the existing CodeBuild project.  What CI/CD configuration meets all of the requirements?

answers.content: Configure CodePipeline with a deploy stage using AWS CodeDeploy configured for in-place deployment. Monitor the newly deployed code, and, if there are any issues, push another code update
answers.explanation: In-place deployments do not minimize downtime or allow easy rollback compared to blue/green.

answers.content: Configure CodePipeline with a deploy stage using AWS CodeDeploy configured for blue/green deployments. Monitor the newly deployed code, and, if there are any issues, trigger a manual rollback using CodeDeploy.
answers.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployments enable minimal downtime and quick rollback by shifting traffic between two environments. Blue/green deployments reduce risk by running the new version alongside the old version before cutover. Manual rollbacks in CodeDeploy allow quick restoration to the last known good deployment in case of issues. Using managed AWS services like CodeDeploy aligns with best practices for CI/CD deployment and rollback handling.

answers.content: Configure CodePipeline with a deploy stage using AWS CloudFormation to create a pipeline for test and production stacks. Monitor the newly deployed code, and, if there are any issues, push another code update.
answers.explanation: CloudFormation stacks are not designed specifically for zero-downtime deployments and quick rollbacks in a CI/CD pipeline.

answers.content: Configure the CodePipeline with a deploy stage using AWS OpsWorks and in-place deployments. Monitor the newly deployed code, and, if there are any issues, push another code update.
answers.explanation: OpsWorks is less suited for this use case than CodeDeploy and also uses in-place deployments, which risk downtime.

questions.content: A company needs to monitor a growing number of Amazon S3 buckets across two AWS Regions. The company also needs to track the percentage of objects that are encrypted in Amazon S3. The company needs a dashboard to display this information for internal compliance teams.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create a new 3 Storage Lens dashboard in each Region to track bucket and encryption metrics. Aggregate data from both Region dashboards into a single dashboard in Amazon QuickSight for the compliance teams.
answers.explanation: Using S3 Storage Lens is the managed AWS service designed for monitoring S3 bucket and encryption metrics at scale across multiple Regions. Creating Storage Lens dashboards in each Region and then aggregating the data with Amazon QuickSight provides a low operational overhead solution. This approach avoids custom coding or complex event-driven architectures, aligning with best practices of using managed services for monitoring. Direct access to Storage Lens dashboards (option C) does not consolidate cross-Region data into a single view, which is a requirement. Lambda and Athena or DynamoDB-based custom solutions (options B and D) increase operational overhead and complexity compared to Storage Lens.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Lambda function in each Region to list the number of buckets and the encryption status of objects. Store this data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena queries to display the data on a custom dashboard in Amazon QuickSight for the compliance teams.
answers.explanation: Custom Lambda and Athena solution increases operational overhead and complexity compared to managed Storage Lens solution.

answers.content: Use the S3 Storage Lens default dashboard to track bucket and encryption metrics. Give the compliance teams access to the dashboard directly in the S3 console.
answers.explanation: Default Storage Lens dashboard does not meet requirement to aggregate data across two Regions in a single dashboard.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect AWS CloudTrail events for S3 object creation. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to record encryption metrics in Amazon DynamoDB. Use Amazon QuickSight to display the metrics in a dashboard for the compliance teams.
answers.explanation: Event-driven Lambda and DynamoDB solution is more complex and operationally intensive than using Storage Lens.

questions.content: A software as a service (SaaS) company uses AWS to host a service that is powered by AWS PrivateLink. The service consists of proprietary software that runs on three Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The instances are in private subnets in multiple Availability Zones in the eu-west-2 Region. All the company's customers are in eu-west-2.  However, the company now acquires a new customer in the us-east-1 Region. The company creates a new VPC and new subnets in us-east-1. The company establishes inter-Region VPC peering between the VPCs in the two Regions.  The company wants to give the new customer access to the SaaS service, but the company does not want to immediately deploy new EC2 resources in us-east-1.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service in us-east-1 to use the existing NLB that is in eu-west-2. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.
answers.explanation: PrivateLink endpoint services cannot use an NLB from a different region directly, so configuring a PrivateLink endpoint service in us-east-1 with an NLB in eu-west-2 is not valid.

answers.content: Create an NLB in us-east-1. Create an IP target group that uses the IP addresses of the company's instances in eu-west-2 that host the SaaS servicConfigure a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the NLB that is in us-east-1. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.
answers.explanation: Option B uses an NLB in us-east-1 with an IP target group referencing the IPs of the existing EC2 instances in eu-west-2, allowing access without deploying new EC2 instances in us-east-1. PrivateLink endpoint service with the NLB in us-east-1 enables secure access while respecting the customer's new region and existing peering setup. This approach aligns with AWS best practices to use managed services (NLB with IP target groups) and avoids complex or unsupported configurations. Other options either incorrectly propose cross-region NLB usage, unsupported sharing mechanisms, or involve ALB to NLB associations that are not supported.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances in eu-west-2. Create an NLB in us-east-1. Associate the NLB that is in us-east-1 with an ALB target group that uses the ALB that is in eu-west-2. Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the NLB that is in us-east-1. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.
answers.explanation: ALB target groups cannot reference another ALB as a target, and associating an NLB in us-east-1 with an ALB target group in eu-west-2 is not supported.

answers.content: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the EC2 instances that are in eu-west-2. In us-east-1, create an NLB and an instance target group that includes the shared EC2 instances from eu-west-2. Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the NLB that is in us-east-1. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM cannot share EC2 instances across regions, so creating an NLB in us-east-1 with an instance target group that includes shared EC2 instances from eu-west-2 is not possible.

questions.content: A financial services company has an asset management product that thousands of customers use around the world. The customers provide feedback about the product through surveys. The company is building a new analytical solution that runs on Amazon EMR to analyze the data from these surveys. The following user personas need to access the analytical solution to perform different actions:  • Administrator: Provisions the EMR cluster for the analytics team based on the team’s requirements • Data engineer: Runs ETL scripts to process, transform, and enrich the datasets • Data analyst: Runs SQL and Hive queries on the data  A solutions architect must ensure that all the user personas have least privilege access to only the resources that they need. The user personas must be able to launch only applications that are approved and authorized. The solution also must ensure tagging for all resources that the user personas creat Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create IAM roles for each user persona. Attach identity-based policies to define which actions the user who assumes the role can perform. Create an AWS Config rule to check for noncompliant resources. Configure the rule to notify the administrator to remediate the noncompliant resources.
answers.explanation: IAM roles alone do not control approved applications or enforce tagging policies, and require manual remediation for noncompliance.

answers.content: Setup Kerberos-based authentication for EMR clusters upon launch. Specify a Kerberos security configuration along with cluster-specific Kerberos options.
answers.explanation: Kerberos authentication secures access but does not restrict cluster launch configurations, user permissions by persona, or enforce tagging.

answers.content: Use AWS Service Catalog to control the Amazon EMR versions available for deployment, the cluster configuration, and the permissions for each user persona.
answers.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows precise control of approved and authorized EMR versions and cluster configurations. It enables setting permissions per user persona ensuring least privilege access. Service Catalog also enforces tagging policies on created resources. This managed service aligns with best practice of controlling user access and resource provisioning in a secure and compliant manner.

answers.content: Launch the EMR cluster by using AWS CloudFormation, Attach resource-based policies to the EMR cluster during cluster creation. Create an AWS. Config rule to check for noncompliant clusters and noncompliant Amazon S3 buckets. Configure the rule to notify the administrator to remediate the noncompliant resources.
answers.explanation: Resource-based policies cannot be attached to EMR clusters and CloudFormation does not enforce least privilege per user persona or approved app launches.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company hosts many applications on Windows servers and Linux servers. Some of the servers are physical, and some of the servers are virtual. The company uses several types of databases in its on-premises environment. The company does not have an accurate inventory of its on-premises servers and applications.  The company wants to rightsize its resources during migration. A solutions architect needs to obtain information about the network connections and the application relationships. The solutions architect must assess the company’s current environment and develop a migration plan.  Which solution will provide the solutions architect with the required information to develop the migration plan?

answers.content: Use Migration Evaluator to request an evaluation of the environment from AWS. Use the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector to import the details into a Migration Evaluator Quick Insights report.
answers.explanation: Migration Evaluator is used with the agentless collector only and does not involve Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations, which limits comprehensive migration planning.

answers.content: Use AWS Migration Hub and install the AWS Application Discovery Agent on the servers. Deploy the Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations application data collector. Generate a report by using Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations.
answers.explanation: AWS Migration Hub with the AWS Application Discovery Agent provides detailed information about on-premises servers and their application relationships, which is essential for right-sizing and migration planning. Installing the Application Discovery Agent allows collecting network connections and application dependency details, which an agentless collector may not fully capturMigration Hub Strategy Recommendations can generate comprehensive reports based on collected data, aiding in migration assessment and planning.

answers.content: Use AWS Migration Hub and run the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector on the servers. Group the servers and databases by using AWS Application Migration ServicGenerate a report by using Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service is for migration execution, not for collecting discovery data or generating strategy recommendations, and agentless collector may miss detailed application relationships.

answers.content: Use the AWS Migration Hub import tool to load the details of the company’s on-premises environment. Generate a report by using Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations.
answers.explanation: Migration Hub import tool requires manual inventory data which the company does not have, making it unsuitable for discovery and planning.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate its on-premises transaction-processing application to AWS. The application runs inside Docker containers that are hosted on VMs in the company's data center. The Docker containers have shared storage where the application records transaction data.  The transactions are time sensitivThe volume of transactions inside the application is unpredictablThe company must implement a low-latency storage solution that will automatically scale throughput to meet increased demand. The company cannot develop the application further and cannot continue to administer the Docker hosting environment.  How should the company migrate the application to AWS to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate the containers that run the application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon S3 to store the transaction data that the containers share.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is not suitable for low-latency shared storage required by the application.

answers.content: Migrate the containers that run the application to AWS Fargate for Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Create a Fargate task definition. Add a volume to the task definition to point to the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: AWS Fargate removes the need to administer the underlying Docker hosting environment, meeting the requirement to avoid managing the Docker hosting environment. Amazon EFS provides shared storage that supports low-latency access and automatically scales throughput based on demand, which fits the application's need for scalable shared storage for transaction data. Using a Fargate task definition with an EFS volume enables containerized applications to share data persistently and with low latency, aligning with AWS best practices for containerized application migration. Amazon EBS volumes cannot be attached to multiple tasks simultaneously, making them unsuitable for shared storagAmazon S3 is object storage and is not suitable for low-latency shared storage required by the application.

answers.content: Migrate the containers that run the application to AWS Fargate for Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumCreate a Fargate task definition. Attach the EBS volume to each running task.
answers.explanation: Amazon EBS volumes cannot be shared across multiple containers simultaneously, so they cannot provide shared storage.

answers.content: Launch Amazon EC2 instances. Install Docker on the EC2 instances. Migrate the containers to the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Add a mount point to the EC2 instances for the EFS file system.
answers.explanation: Managing Amazon EC2 instances and installing Docker contradicts the requirement to avoid administering the Docker hosting environment.

questions.content: A solutions architect is reviewing an application's resilience before launch. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that is deployed in a private subnet of a VPC. The EC2 instance is provisioned by an Auto Scaling group that has a minimum capacity of 1 and a maximum capacity of 1. The application stores data on an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instancThe VPC has subnets configured in three Availability Zones and is configured with a single NAT gateway.  The solutions architect needs to recommend a solution to ensure that the application will operate across multiple Availability Zones.  Which solution will meet this requirement?

answers.content: Deploy an additional NAT gateway in the other Availability Zones. Update the route tables with appropriate routes. Modify the RDS for MySQL DB instance to a Multi-AZ configuration. Configure the Auto Scaling group to launch the instances across Availability Zones. Set the minimum capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 3.
answers.explanation: Deploying additional NAT gateways in other Availability Zones improves high availability and fault tolerance of network connectivity. Modifying the RDS for MySQL DB instance to a Multi-AZ configuration ensures database availability across multiple Availability Zones for better resiliencConfiguring the Auto Scaling group to launch instances across Availability Zones and increasing capacity to 3 provides instance-level resilience and fault tolerance.

answers.content: Replace the NAT gateway with a virtual private gateway. Replace the RDS for MySQL DB instance with an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. Configure the Auto Scaling group to launch instances across all subnets in the VPC. Set the minimum capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 3.
answers.explanation: Replacing the NAT gateway with a virtual private gateway is unrelated to the requirement, and Amazon Aurora is not specified as necessary; setting min and max capacity to 3 is correct but the rest is not.
