answers.content: Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instancMigrate the RDS for MySQL DB instance to an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instancLaunch a new EC2 instance in the other Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: Replacing NAT gateway with a NAT instance is less resilient and managed compared to NAT gateway; migrating RDS to PostgreSQL is not relevant; launching a single additional instance does not meet resilience across multiple AZs.

answers.content: Deploy an additional NAT gateway in the other Availability Zones. Update the route tables with appropriate routes. Modify the RDS for MySQL DB instance to turn on automatic backups and retain the backups for 7 days. Configure the Auto Scaling group to launch instances across all subnets in the VPC. Keep the minimum capacity and the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group at 1.
answers.explanation: Retaining minimum and maximum capacity at 1 does not provide fault tolerance across AZs; backups do not ensure real-time availability; automatic backups do not replace Multi-AZ for resilience.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. This includes thousands of virtualized Linux and Microsoft Windows servers, SAN storage, Java and PHP applications with MySQL, and Oracle databases. There are many dependent services hosted either in the same data center or externally. The technical documentation is incomplete and outdated. A solutions architect needs to understand the current environment and estimate the cloud resource costs after the migration.  Which tools or services should the solutions architect use to plan the cloud migration? (Choose three.)

answers.content: AWS Application Discovery Service
answers.explanation: This service discovers on-premises servers, applications, dependencies, and performance data. It is essential when documentation is outdated and helps estimate required AWS resources and costs.

answers.content: AWS SMS
answers.explanation: AWS SMS is used to migrate virtual machines, not to analyze or plan the existing environment. It does not help with discovery or cost estimation.

answers.content: AWS X-Ray
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray is for tracing distributed applications already running on AWS. It does not analyze on-premises infrastructure or support migration planning.

answers.content: AWS Cloud Adoption Readiness Tool (CART)
answers.explanation: CART helps assess organizational and technical readiness for cloud adoption. It identifies gaps across multiple perspectives (security, operations, skills) to support migration planning.

answers.content: Amazon Inspector
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector performs security and vulnerability assessments on AWS workloads. It is not designed for environment discovery or migration cost estimation.

answers.content: AWS Migration Hub
answers.explanation: AWS Migration Hub provides a central place to track discovered applications and migration progress across tools and accounts. It integrates with Application Discovery Service to give visibility into the current environment.

questions.content: A company has a project that is launching Amazon EC2 instances that are larger than required. The project's account cannot be part of the company's organization in AWS Organizations due to policy restrictions to keep this activity outside of corporate IT. The company wants to allow only the launch of t3.small EC2 instances by developers in the project's account. These EC2 instances must be restricted to the us-east-2 Region.  What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new developer account. Move all EC2 instances, users, and assets into us-east-2. Add the account to the company's organization in AWS Organizations. Enforce a tagging policy that denotes Region affinity.
answers.explanation: The account cannot be added to the company's organization due to policy restrictions, so this is not feasible.

answers.content: Create an SCP that denies the launch of all EC2 instances except t3.small EC2 instances in us-east-2. Attach the SCP to the project's account.
answers.explanation: SCPs require the account to be part of AWS Organizations, which is not allowed by company policy.

answers.content: Create and purchase a t3.small EC2 Reserved Instance for each developer in us-east-2. Assign each developer a specific EC2 instance with their name as the tag.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances do not restrict which instance types can be launched or regions used; they only provide billing discounts.

answers.content: Create an IAM policy than allows the launch of only t3.small EC2 instances in us-east-2. Attach the policy to the roles and groups that the developers use in the project's account.
answers.explanation: IAM policies are designed to restrict actions such as launching specific instance types and controlling regions within an AWS account. Since the project's account cannot be part of the company's organization, SCPs (Service Control Policies) from AWS Organizations cannot be used to enforce restrictions. IAM policies attached to users, groups, or roles in the project's account provide a managed, secure way to enforce launching only t3.small instances in the specific region, aligning with security best practices.

questions.content: A team of data scientists is using Amazon SageMaker instances and SageMaker APIs to train machine learning (ML) models. The SageMaker instances are deployed in a VPC that does not have access to or from the internet. Datasets for ML model training are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Interface VPC endpoints provide access to Amazon S3 and the SageMaker APIs.  Occasionally, the data scientists require access to the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository to update Python packages that they use as part of their workflow. A solutions architect must provide access to the PyPI repository while ensuring that the SageMaker instances remain isolated from the internet.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each package that the data scientists need to access. Configure code synchronization between the PyPI repository and the CodeCommit repository. Create a VPC endpoint for CodeCommit.
answers.explanation: CodeCommit is a source control service, not designed for package management or mirroring PyPI packages, making synchronization complex and nonstandard.

answers.content: Create a NAT gateway in the VPC. Configure VPC routes to allow access to the internet with a network ACL that allows access to only the PyPI repository endpoint.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway provides internet access which violates the requirement to keep SageMaker instances isolated from the internet.

answers.content: Create a NAT instance in the VPConfigure VPC routes to allow access to the internet. Configure SageMaker notebook instance firewall rules that allow access to only the PyPI repository endpoint.
answers.explanation: A NAT instance requires manual management and internet access, posing security risks and operational overhead; also firewall rules on SageMaker notebooks are not a supported control mechanism.

answers.content: Create an AWS CodeArtifact domain and repository. Add an external connection for public:pypi to the CodeArtifact repository. Configure the Python client to use the CodeArtifact repository. Create a VPC endpoint for CodeArtifact.
answers.explanation: AWS CodeArtifact allows creating a private repository with an external connection to the PyPI public repository, enabling controlled package access without direct internet access from the VPC. A VPC endpoint for CodeArtifact keeps traffic within the AWS network, maintaining SageMaker instances isolated from the internet. This method follows AWS best practices by using a managed service designed for secure access and distribution of packages, avoiding the need for NAT gateways or instances.

questions.content: A company is rearchitecting its applications to run on AWS. The company’s infrastructure includes multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The company's development team needs different levels of access. The company wants to implement a policy that requires all Windows EC2 instances to be joined to an Active Directory domain on AWS. The company also wants to implement enhanced security processes such as multi-factor authentication (MFA). The company wants to use managed AWS services wherever possibl Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory implementation. Launch an Amazon WorkspacConnect to and use the Workspace for domain security configuration tasks.
answers.explanation: AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory is a managed service that supports Windows EC2 instances joining an Active Directory domain. Using Amazon WorkSpaces provides a managed, secure desktop environment to perform domain security configuration tasks without managing traditional EC2 instance infrastructurThis approach aligns with the requirement for managed AWS services and the implementation of enhanced security such as MFA, which AWS Managed Microsoft AD and WorkSpaces support. Launching EC2 instances for domain configuration tasks is less secure and requires more manual management compared to using Amazon WorkSpaces.

answers.content: Create an AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory implementation. Launch an EC2 instancConnect to and use the EC2 instance for domain security configuration tasks.
answers.explanation: Uses EC2 instances for domain security tasks, which is less managed and less secure compared to WorkSpaces.

answers.content: Create an AWS Directory Service Simple AD implementation. Launch an EC2 instancConnect to and use the EC2 instance for domain security configuration tasks.
answers.explanation: Simple AD is not a full Microsoft Active Directory and may lack required domain features; also uses EC2 instead of managed WorkSpaces.

answers.content: Create an AWS Directory Service Simple AD implementation. Launch an Amazon WorkspacConnect to and use the Workspace for domain security configuration tasks.
answers.explanation: Simple AD lacks full Active Directory capabilities required by the scenario and uses WorkSpaces which is correct, but the directory choice is insufficient.

questions.content: A company has used infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision a set of two Amazon EC2 instances. The instances have remained the same for several years.  The company's business has grown rapidly in the past few months. In response, the company’s operations team has implemented an Auto Scaling group to manage the sudden increases in traffic. Company policy requires a monthly installation of security updates on all operating systems that are running.  The most recent security update required a reboot. As a result, the Auto Scaling group terminated the instances and replaced them with new, unpatched instances.  Which combination of steps should a solutions architect recommend to avoid a recurrence of this issue? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Modify the Auto Scaling group by setting the Update policy to target the oldest launch configuration for replacement.
answers.explanation: Replacing the oldest launch configuration first ensures outdated instances are removed. This helps keep instances aligned with newer configurations after updates.

answers.content: Create a new Auto Scaling group before the next patch maintenancDuring the maintenance window, patch both groups and reboot the instances.
answers.explanation: Creating a second Auto Scaling group increases operational complexity. It does not provide a scalable or automated patching solution.

answers.content: Create an Elastic Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group. Configure monitoring to ensure that target group health checks return healthy after the Auto Scaling group replaces the terminated instances.
answers.explanation: A load balancer only checks instance health and traffic routing. It does not prevent unpatched instances from being launched.

answers.content: Create automation scripts to patch an AMI, update the launch configuration, and invoke an Auto Scaling instance refresh.
answers.explanation: Baking a patched AMI and updating the launch configuration/template is the recommended Auto Scaling best practice. Instance Refresh ensures all new instances are launched from the patched AMI.

answers.content: Create an Elastic Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group. Configure termination protection on the instances.
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling groups ignore EC2 termination protection settings. Instances can still be terminated and replaced by the Auto Scaling group.

questions.content: A company is running an application on Amazon EC2 instances in the AWS Cloud. The application is using a MongoDB database with a replica set as its data tier. The MongoDB database is installed on systems in the company’s on-premises data center and is accessible through an AWS Direct Connect connection to the data center environment.  A solutions architect must migrate the on-premises MongoDB database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility).  Which strategy should the solutions architect choose to perform this migration?

answers.content: Create a fleet of EC2 instances. Install MongoDB Community Edition on the EC2 instances, and create a databasConfigure continuous synchronous replication with the database that is running in the on-premises data center.
answers.explanation: Manual setup with EC2 and MongoDB Community Edition adds operational complexity and does not leverage managed migration services.

answers.content: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instancCreate a source endpoint for the on-premises MongoDB database by using change data capture (CDC). Create a target endpoint for the Amazon DocumentDB databasCreate and run a DMS migration task.
answers.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) is a managed AWS service designed for database migrations and supports change data capture (CDC) for continuous replication. AWS DMS can create source and target endpoints for MongoDB and Amazon DocumentDB, enabling efficient and secure migration with minimal downtimUsing AWS DMS aligns with AWS best practices of relying on managed services over custom manual solutions, maintaining security and operational efficiency.

answers.content: Create a data migration pipeline by using AWS Data PipelinDefine data nodes for the on-premises MongoDB database and the Amazon DocumentDB databasCreate a scheduled task to run the data pipeline.
answers.explanation: AWS Data Pipeline is not designed specifically for database migration between MongoDB and DocumentDB and lacks CDC support.

answers.content: Create a source endpoint for the on-premises MongoDB database by using AWS Glue crawlers. Configure continuous asynchronous replication between the MongoDB database and the Amazon DocumentDB database.
answers.explanation: AWS Glue crawlers are for schema discovery and ETL, not continuous asynchronous replication between databases.

questions.content: A solutions architect has launched multiple Amazon EC2 instances in a placement group within a single Availability ZonBecause of additional load on the system, the solutions architect attempts to add new instances to the placement group. However, the solutions architect receives an insufficient capacity error.  What should the solutions architect do to troubleshoot this issue?

answers.content: Use a spread placement group. Set a minimum of eight instances for each Availability Zone.
answers.explanation: Spread placement groups are designed for spreading instances across hardware to reduce correlated failures, not for increasing capacity in a specific AZ or dealing with insufficient capacity errors.

answers.content: Stop and start all the instances in the placement group. Try the launch again.
answers.explanation: Stopping and starting instances in a placement group can help reallocate capacity and potentially resolve insufficient capacity errors. Placement groups are tied to specific Availability Zones and instance types, so restarting instances may allow them to be placed better by the AWS scheduler.

answers.content: Create a new placement group. Merge the new placement group with the original placement group.
answers.explanation: Placement groups cannot be merged; each placement group is independent and this will not solve capacity exhaustion in the original group.

answers.content: Launch the additional instances as Dedicated Hosts in the placement groups.
answers.explanation: Launching additional instances as Dedicated Hosts does not resolve capacity constraints within a placement group, and Dedicated Hosts have their own capacity limitations and management overhead.

questions.content: A company has a legacy application that runs on multiple NET Framework components. The components share the same Microsoft SQL Server database and communicate with each other asynchronously by using Microsoft Message Queueing (MSMQ).  The company is starting a migration to containerized .NET Core components and wants to refactor the application to run on AWS. The .NET Core components require complex orchestration. The company must have full control over networking and host configuration. The application's database model is strongly relational.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Host the INET Core components on AWS App Runner. Host the database on Amazon RDS for SQL Server. Use Amazon EventBiridge for asynchronous messaging.
answers.explanation: App Runner does not provide full control over networking and host configuration; EventBridge is an event bus, not a queue for asynchronous messaging like MSMQ.

answers.content: Host the .NET Core components on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the AWS Fargate launch typHost the database on Amazon DynamoDUse Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for asynchronous messaging.
answers.explanation: AWS Fargate does not provide full control over host configuration; DynamoD is a NoSQL database, not suitable for strongly relational data.

answers.content: Host the .NET Core components on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Host the database on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) for asynchronous messaging.
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is a managed service with limited host control; Aurora PostgreSQL is not SQL Server, which is required; Kafka is more complex than needed and not a direct replacement for MSMQ.

answers.content: Host the NET Core components on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch typHost the database on Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for asynchronous messaging.
answers.explanation: SQL Server must be hosted on AWS in the same region as AWS Transform, so a strongly relational database is required and Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 is a relational database that can support complex orchestration. The .NET Core components require complex orchestration and full control over networking and host configuration, which is best met with Amazon ECS using the Amazon EC2 launch type, as it provides control over the underlying host. For asynchronous messaging, using Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) fits the requirement for asynchronous communication similar to MSMQ. Other options either use unsupported databases (DynamoD) or managed services that do not provide full host control (App Runner, Elastic Beanstalk) and/or do not use SQL Server or close alternatives for relational DB.

questions.content: A company is building an application on AWS. The application sends logs to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for analysis. All data must be stored within a VPC.  Some of the company’s developers work from homOther developers work from three different company office locations. The developers need to access OpenSearch Service to analyze and visualize logs directly from their local development machines.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure and set up an AWS Client VPN endpoint. Associate the Client VPN endpoint with a subnet in the VPC. Configure a Client VPN self-service portal. Instruct the developers to connect by using the client for Client VPN.
answers.explanation: AWS Client VPN is a managed service that allows secure access to AWS resources within a VPC from any location, including remote developers working from home or other offices. Client VPN endpoints can be associated with VPC subnets, enabling secure encrypted VPN connections directly into the VPC where OpenSearch Service is hosted. This solution maintains all data within the VPC boundary as required and supports developer access from local machines securely. Options involving transit gateway and Site-to-Site VPNs (B and C) are designed for network connectivity between offices or data centers rather than individual remote developers, and are not optimal for remote developer access. Using a bastion host (D) exposes a single instance to public internet and requires SSH access management, which is less secure and less scalable compared to managed VPN solutions.

answers.content: Create a transit gateway, and connect it to the VPC. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Create an attachment to the transit gateway. Instruct the developers to connect by using an OpenVPN client.
answers.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN is intended to connect entire office networks, not individual remote developers, and adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Create a transit gateway, and connect it to the VPOrder an AWS Direct Connect connection. Set up a public VIF on the Direct Connect connection. Associate the public VIF with the transit gateway. Instruct the developers to connect to the Direct Connect connection.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect with public VIF is not suitable for remote user access and requires physical connectivity that remote developers cannot leverage.

answers.content: Create and configure a bastion host in a public subnet of the VPC. Configure the bastion host security group to allow SSH access from the company CIDR ranges. Instruct the developers to connect by using SSH.
answers.explanation: Bastion hosts require managing SSH access and expose a public instance, which is less secure than VPN and does not scale well for multiple remote users.

questions.content: A company needs to store and process image data that will be uploaded from mobile devices using a custom mobile app. Usage peaks between 8 AM and 5 PM on weekdays, with thousands of uploads per minutThe app is rarely used at any other timA user is notified when image processing is complet Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to ensure image processing can scale to handle the load? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Upload files from the mobile software directly to Amazon S3. Use S3 event notifications to create a message in an Amazon MQ queue.
answers.explanation: Amazon MQ adds unnecessary management complexity versus Amazon SQS, which is serverless and highly scalable.

answers.content: Upload files from the mobile software directly to Amazon S3. Use S3 event notifications to create a message in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue.
answers.explanation: Correct choice; SQS is the preferred managed queue service integrated with S3 event notifications.

answers.content: Invoke an AWS Lambda function to perform image processing when a message is available in the queue.
answers.explanation: Correct choice; Lambda is the appropriate scalable compute service for processing queue messages.

answers.content: Invoke an S3 Batch Operations job to perform image processing when a message is available in the queue.
answers.explanation: S3 Batch Operations is for bulk processing, not individual real-time events triggered from queues.

answers.content: Send a push notification to the mobile app by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when processing is complete.
answers.explanation: Correct choice; Amazon SNS is appropriate for sending push notifications on processing completion.

answers.content: Send a push notification to the mobile app by using Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) when processing is complete.
answers.explanation: SES is an email service, not a push-notification service, and it cannot deliver mobile push notifications to apps. Push notifications should be handled by services such as Amazon SNS or mobile push notification platforms, so SES does not fit the requirement.

questions.content: A company owns a chain of travel agencies and is running an application in the AWS Cloud. Company employees use the application to search for information about travel destinations. Destination content is updated four times each year.  Two fixed Amazon EC2 instances serve the application. The company uses an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone with a multivalue record of travel.example.com that returns the Elastic IP addresses for the EC2 instances. The application uses Amazon DynamoDB as its primary data storThe company uses a self-hosted Redis instance as a caching solution.  During content updates, the load on the EC2 instances and the caching solution increases drastically. This increased load has led to downtime on several occasions. A solutions architect must update the application so that the application is highly available and can handle the load that is generated by the content updates.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Set up DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as in-memory cachUpdate the application to use DAX. Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Set the Auto Scaling group as a target for the ALB. Update the Route 53 record to use a simple routing policy that targets the ALB's DNS alias. Configure scheduled scaling for the EC2 instances before the content updates.
answers.explanation: Using DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) provides a fully managed, highly available caching solution that integrates natively with DynamoDB, improving performance during high load periods such as content updates. Creating an Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances and placing them behind an Application Load Balancer increases availability and scalability during traffic spikes. Updating the Route 53 record to target the ALB's DNS alias with a simple routing policy ensures stable and resilient DNS-based load distribution. Configuring scheduled scaling proactively adjusts capacity before the anticipated load increase, avoiding downtimThis solution avoids increasing fragility by using managed services (DAX, ALB, Auto Scaling) and incorporates proper error handling and scaling best practices.

answers.content: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Update the application to use ElastiCachCreate an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution, and set the Auto Scaling group as an origin for the distribution. Update the Route 53 record to use a simple routing policy that targets the CloudFront distribution’s DNS alias. Manually scale up EC2 instances before the content updates.
answers.explanation: Using CloudFront with Auto Scaling group as origin is not optimal for dynamic application traffic; also, manual scaling is less reliable than scheduled scaling.

answers.content: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached. Update the application to use ElastiCachCreate an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Set the Auto Scaling group as a target for the ALB. Update the Route 53 record to use a simple routing policy that targets the ALB's DNS alias. Configure scheduled scaling for the application before the content updates.
answers.explanation: Using Memcached is less suitable since the existing cache is Redis; Memcached lacks features like data persistence and is not as tightly integrated with DynamoDB as DAX; also not specifying a managed Redis service reduces availability.

answers.content: Set up DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as in-memory cachUpdate the application to use DAX. Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution, and set the Auto Scaling group as an origin for the distribution. Update the Route 53 record to use a simple routing policy that targets the CloudFront distribution's DNS alias. Manually scale up EC2 instances before the content updates.
answers.explanation: Manual scaling is less reliable than scheduled scaling; using CloudFront as origin for Auto Scaling group is suboptimal for application traffic.

questions.content: A company hosts a software as a service (SaaS) solution on AWS. The solution has an Amazon API Gateway API that serves an HTTPS endpoint. The API uses AWS Lambda functions for computThe Lambda functions store data in an Amazon Aurora Serverless v1 databas The company used the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) to deploy the solution. The solution extends across multiple Availability Zones and has no disaster recovery (DR) plan.  A solutions architect must design a DR strategy that can recover the solution in another AWS Region. The solution has an RTO of 5 minutes and an RPO of 1 minut What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a read replica of the Aurora Serverless v1 database in the target Region. Use AWS SAM to create a runbook to deploy the solution to the target Region. Promote the read replica to primary in case of disaster.
answers.explanation: Aurora Serverless v1 does not support read replicas in other Regions, so this is not a valid DR approach.

answers.content: Change the Aurora Serverless v1 database to a standard Aurora MySQL global database that extends across the source Region and the target Region. Use AWS SAM to create a runbook to deploy the solution to the target Region.
answers.explanation: Using a runbook to deploy during disaster increases RTO beyond 5 minutes; a fully launched target Region solution is needed.

answers.content: Create an Aurora Serverless v1 DB cluster that has multiple writer instances in the target Region. Launch the solution in the target Region. Configure the two Regional solutions to work in an active-passive configuration.
answers.explanation: Aurora Serverless v1 does not support multiple writer instances or multi-Region configurations.

answers.content: Change the Aurora Serverless v1 database to a standard Aurora MySQL global database that extends across the source Region and the target Region. Launch the solution in the target Region. Configure the two Regional solutions to work in an active-passive configuration.
answers.explanation: Aurora MySQL global databases extend across multiple AWS Regions and support disaster recovery with low RTO and RPO. Using a standard Aurora MySQL global database is more appropriate than Aurora Serverless v1 because the latter does not support global databases or multi-writer replicas needed for active-passive DR. Launching the solution in the target Region and configuring it for active-passive failover meets the 5 minute RTO and 1 minute RPO requirements. AWS SAM can be used to automate deployment, but relying solely on read replicas or Serverless v1 multi-writer clusters is not suitable for cross-Region DR.

questions.content: A company is migrating an on-premises application and a MySQL database to AWS. The application processes highly sensitive data, and new data is constantly updated in the databasThe data must not be transferred over the internet. The company also must encrypt the data in transit and at rest.  The database is 5 TB in sizThe company already has created the database schema in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instancThe company has set up a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to AWS. The company also has set up a public VIF and a private VIF. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will migrate the data to AWS with the least possible downtim Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Perform a database backup. Copy the backup files to an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devicImport the backup to Amazon S3. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit. Import the data from Amazon S3 to the DB instance.
answers.explanation: Using Snowball Edge for database backup import is meant for large bulk data transfer but does not support ongoing data replication or minimal downtime for constant updates.

answers.content: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data to AWS. Create a DMS replication instance in a private subnet. Create VPC endpoints for AWS DMS. Configure a DMS task to copy data from the on-premises database to the DB instance by using full load plus change data capture (CDC). Use the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) default key for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit.
answers.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) supports continuous data replication with minimal downtime by using full load plus change data capture (CDC), which suits ongoing updates in the source databasUsing a DMS replication instance in a private subnet with VPC endpoints ensures data does not traverse the internet, satisfying the requirement for no internet data transfer. AWS DMS uses TLS to encrypt data in transit and AWS KMS to encrypt data at rest, satisfying the encryption requirements. This approach leverages managed AWS services designed for secure, low-downtime migration rather than manual backup and restores, aligning with best practices.

answers.content: Perform a database backup. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the backup files to Amazon S3. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit. Import the data from Amazon S3 to the DB instance.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is primarily used for file and object data transfer, not optimized for continuous database replication with minimal downtime and does not natively support database change capture.

answers.content: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway. Set up a private connection to Amazon S3 by using AWS PrivateLink. Perform a database backup. Copy the backup files to Amazon S3. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit. Import the data from Amazon S3 to the DB instance.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway is a storage gateway solution for on-premises file storage, not intended for database migration with minimal downtime or secure continuous replication.

questions.content: A car rental company has built a serverless REST API to provide data to its mobile app. The app consists of an Amazon API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless DB cluster. The company recently opened the API to mobile apps of partners. A significant increase in the number of requests resulted, causing sporadic database memory errors.  Analysis of the API traffic indicates that clients are making multiple HTTP GET requests for the same queries in a short period of timTraffic is concentrated during business hours, with spikes around holidays and other events.  The company needs to improve its ability to support the additional usage while minimizing the increase in costs associated with the solution.  Which strategy meets these requirements?

answers.content: Convert the API Gateway Regional endpoint to an edge-optimized endpoint. Enable caching in the production stage.
answers.explanation: Edge-optimized endpoints improve latency but do not reduce database load or memory errors caused by repeated queries.

answers.content: Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to store the results of the database calls. Modify the Lambda functions to use the cache.
answers.explanation: Implementing Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache database query results directly addresses the issue of multiple identical HTTP GET requests, reducing load on the Aurora Serverless cluster and mitigating memory errors. Modifying Lambda functions to use the cache aligns with best practice to improve scalability and performance without significantly increasing costs. This caching strategy reduces backend database load, especially during traffic spikes, supporting additional usage efficiently.

answers.content: Modify the Aurora Serverless DB cluster configuration to increase the maximum amount of available memory.
answers.explanation: Increasing Aurora Serverless memory may alleviate memory errors but does not address unnecessary repeated queries or control usage spikes, potentially increasing costs.

answers.content: Enable throttling in the API Gateway production stagSet the rate and burst values to limit the incoming calls.
answers.explanation: Throttling limits request rate but degrades user experience and does not optimize backend resource usage or reduce repeated query overhead.

questions.content: A financial company needs to create a separate AWS account for a new digital wallet application. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage its accounts. A solutions architect uses the IAM user Support1 from the management account to create a new member account with [email protected] [/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection] as the email address.  What should the solutions architect do to create IAM users in the new member account?

answers.content: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with AWS account root user credentials by using the 64-character password from the initial AWS Organizations email sent to [email protected] [/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection]. Set up the IAM users as required.
answers.explanation: Using root user credentials is less secure and should be avoided; root password is not intended for regular user access.

answers.content: From the management account, switch roles to assume the OrganizationAccountAccessRole role with the account ID of the new member account. Set up the IAM users as required.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations automatically creates the IAM role OrganizationAccountAccessRole in the new member account. IAM users in the management account with permissions can assume this role to gain administrative access to the member account. Using this role to switch roles from the management account to the member account follows AWS best practices for secure and centralized management. Avoids using root account credentials, which is less secure and against best practices.

answers.content: Go to the AWS Management Console sign-in pagChoose “Sign in using root account credentials.” Sign in in by using the email address finance [email protected] [/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection] and the management account's root password. Set up the IAM users as required.
answers.explanation: Root credentials for the management account cannot be used to sign in to the new member account; root passwords are not shared between accounts.

answers.content: Go to the AWS Management Console sign-in pagSign in by using the account ID of the new member account and the Support1 IAM credentials. Set up the IAM users as required.
answers.explanation: IAM users from the management account cannot sign in directly to the member account using the account ID and IAM user credentials; cross-account access is done via role assumption.

questions.content: A company is developing a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a public-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB). Only users from a specific country are allowed to access the application. The company needs the ability to log the access requests that have been blocked. The solution should require the least possible maintenanc Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create an IPSet containing a list of IP ranges that belong to the specified country. Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Configure a rule to block any requests that do not originate from an IP range in the IPSet. Associate the rule with the web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
answers.explanation: Requires manual IP range management, which increases maintenance compared to country-based blocking directly in WAF.

answers.content: Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Configure a rule to block any requests that do not originate from the specified country. Associate the rule with the web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF supports country-based blocking and logging of blocked requests. Configuring a WAF web ACL with a rule to block requests from countries other than the specified one aligns with the requirement to allow only users from a specific country. Associating the web ACL with the ALB enables the blocking functionality at the load balancer level. AWS WAF automatically logs blocked requests, satisfying the logging requirement with minimal maintenancUsing AWS WAF is a managed service solution preferred over manually maintaining IP sets or security group rules.

answers.content: Configure AWS Shield to block any requests that do not originate from the specified country. Associate AWS Shield with the ALB.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield is a managed DDoS protection service and does not provide country-based blocking capabilities.

answers.content: Create a security group rule that allows ports 80 and 443 from IP ranges that belong to the specified country. Associate the security group with the ALB.
answers.explanation: Security groups do not support filtering by country and are not designed to block or log requests based on geographic origin.

questions.content: A company provides a software as a service (SaaS) application that runs in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The instances are in an Auto Scaling group and are distributed across three Availability Zones in a single AWS Region.  The company is deploying the application into additional Regions. The company must provide static IP addresses for the application to customers so that the customers can add the IP addresses to allow lists. The solution must automatically route customers to the Region that is geographically closest to them.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Create a CloudFront origin group. Add the NLB for each additional Region to the origin group. Provide customers with the IP address ranges of the distribution’s edge locations.
answers.explanation: CloudFront IP ranges are not static application IPs and do not provide direct IP addresses for allow lists; origin groups cannot guarantee static IPs to customers.

answers.content: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator. Create a standard accelerator endpoint for the NLB in each additional Region. Provide customers with the Global Accelerator IP address.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator provides static IP addresses that act as a fixed entry point to your application endpoints in multiple AWS Regions. Global Accelerator automatically routes user traffic to the optimal endpoint based on latency, effectively routing customers to the geographically closest Region. The solution requires static IPs that customers can allow list; Global Accelerator IP addresses are static and stablNetwork Load Balancers support IPv4 and can be endpoints for Global Accelerator standard accelerators. CloudFront IP ranges are dynamic and represent edge locations, not static IP addresses specific to the application endpoints.

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Create a custom origin for the NLB in each additional Region. Provide customers with the IP address ranges of the distribution’s edge locations.
answers.explanation: CloudFront does not provide static IP addresses suitable for allow listing and is primarily for HTTP/HTTPS delivery, not for TCP/IP routing to NLBs.

answers.content: Create an AWS Global Accelerator custom routing accelerator. Create a listener for the custom routing accelerator. Add the IP address and ports for the NLB in each additional Region. Provide customers with the Global Accelerator IP address.
answers.explanation: Global Accelerator custom routing accelerators are for non-HTTP protocols and do not support IP address endpoints as required; standard accelerator is better for this use case.

questions.content: A company is migrating to the cloud. It wants to evaluate the configurations of virtual machines in its existing data center environment to ensure that it can size new Amazon EC2 instances accurately. The company wants to collect metrics, such as CPU, memory, and disk utilization, and it needs an inventory of what processes are running on each instancThe company would also like to monitor network connections to map communications between servers.  Which would enable the collection of this data MOST cost effectively?

answers.content: Use AWS Application Discovery Service and deploy the data collection agent to each virtual machine in the data center.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service with the data collection agent is designed to collect detailed process inventory and resource utilization metrics such as CPU, memory, and disk usagThe agent can also monitor network connections between servers, enabling communication mapping. Agent-based discovery provides more detailed and accurate data compared to agentless methods for these requirements. This approach is cost-effective because it targets required data collection without requiring extensive reconfiguration or infrastructure changes.

answers.content: Configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all servers within the local environment and publish metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch agent collects metrics but does not provide process inventory or network communication mapping in on-premises environments.

answers.content: Use AWS Application Discovery Service and enable agentless discovery in the existing virtualization environment.
answers.explanation: Agentless discovery cannot collect detailed process data or monitor network connections accurately, which are required here.

answers.content: Enable AWS Application Discovery Service in the AWS Management Console and configure the corporate firewall to allow scans over a VPN.
answers.explanation: Enabling AWS Application Discovery Service without deploying an agent limits the depth of data collected and requires complex firewall and VPN configurations, reducing cost-effectiveness.

questions.content: A company that provisions job boards for a seasonal workforce is seeing an increase in traffic and usagThe backend services run on a pair of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer with Amazon DynamoDB as the datastorApplication read and write traffic is slow during peak seasons.  Which option provides a scalable application architecture to handle peak seasons with the LEAST development effort?

answers.content: Migrate the backend services to AWS Lambda. Increase the read and write capacity of DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Migrating to AWS Lambda requires more development effort and manual capacity management increases operational overhead.

answers.content: Migrate the backend services to AWS Lambda. Configure DynamoDB to use global tables.
answers.explanation: Global tables add complexity and are more relevant for multi-region setups, increasing development effort unnecessarily.

answers.content: Use Auto Scaling groups for the backend services. Use DynamoDB auto scaling.
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling groups for EC2 instances provide a managed way to handle increases in traffic with minimal development. DynamoDB auto scaling automatically adjusts capacity to handle variable workloads without manual intervention. This solution uses managed services and balances scalability with operational simplicity and security best practices.

answers.content: Use Auto Scaling groups for the backend services. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) and an AWS Lambda function to write to DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Introducing SQS and Lambda adds architectural complexity and more development effort compared to simple Auto Scaling.

questions.content: A company built an ecommerce website on AWS using a three-tier web architecturThe application is Java-based and composed of an Amazon CloudFront distribution, an Apache web server layer of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group, and a backend Amazon Aurora MySQL databas Last month, during a promotional sales event, users reported errors and timeouts while adding items to their shopping carts. The operations team recovered the logs created by the web servers and reviewed Aurora DB cluster performance metrics. Some of the web servers were terminated before logs could be collected and the Aurora metrics were not sufficient for query performance analysis.  Which combination of steps must the solutions architect take to improve application performance visibility during peak traffic events? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Configure the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to publish slow query and error logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
answers.explanation: Configuring the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to publish slow query and error logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs directly addresses the problem of insufficient Aurora metrics for query performance analysis. By publishing these logs to CloudWatch, the operations team can analyze slow-running queries and errors even after high-traffic events, providing the necessary data for performance tuning.

answers.content: Implement the AWS X-Ray SDK to trace incoming HTTP requests on the EC2 instances and implement tracing of SQL queries with the X-Ray SDK for Java.
answers.explanation: Implementing the AWS X-Ray SDK is essential for tracing requests across the application components (CloudFront, EC2 web servers, and Aurora DB). X-Ray provides end-to-end visibility, allowing the solutions architect to pinpoint exactly where the errors and timeouts occurred within the three-tier architecture, including tracing the SQL queries executed against the database. This helps identify bottlenecks beyond just the server logs.

answers.content: Configure the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to stream slow query and error logs to Amazon Kinesis.
answers.explanation: Streaming logs to Amazon Kinesis is not the managed or standard method for Aurora log handling and adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Install and configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent on the EC2 instances to send the Apache logs to CloudWatch Logs.
answers.explanation: Installing and configuring the Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent on the EC2 instances to send Apache logs to CloudWatch Logs solves the issue of losing logs when EC2 instances are terminated (which is common in Auto Scaling groups under high load). Centralizing these logs ensures that all web server activity is captured and available for analysis, helping to understand the application layer's behavior during peak traffic.

answers.content: Enable and configure AWS CloudTrail to collect and analyze application activity from Amazon EC2 and Aurora
answers.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs management events and does not capture application activity or detailed database query performance.

answers.content: Enable Aurora MySQL DB cluster performance benchmarking and publish the stream to AWS X-Ray.
answers.explanation: X-Ray is designed for tracing application requests across services (such as EC2, ALB, and Lambda), not for collecting or streaming Aurora query performance data, so this option does not improve database-level performance visibility.

questions.content: A company has a solution that analyzes weather data from thousands of weather stations. The weather stations send the data over an Amazon API Gateway REST API that has an AWS Lambda function integration. The Lambda function calls a third-party service for data pre-processing. The third-party service gets overloaded and fails the pre-processing, causing a loss of data.  A solutions architect must improve the resiliency of the solution. The solutions architect must ensure that no data is lost and that data can be processed later if failures occur.  What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuConfigure the queue as the dead-letter queue for the API.
answers.explanation: A single SQS queue as dead-letter queue for API does not provide a mechanism to handle all messages reliably before Lambda processing.

answers.content: Create two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: a primary queue and a secondary queuConfigure the secondary queue as the dead-letter queue for the primary queuUpdate the API to use a new integration to the primary queuConfigure the Lambda function as the invocation target for the primary queue.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SQS queues between the API Gateway and Lambda improves resiliency and ensures no data loss by decoupling ingestion from processing. Configuring a primary queue and a secondary dead-letter queue prevents data loss by retaining messages that cannot be processed immediately. Updating the API to integrate with the SQS primary queue and triggering Lambda from SQS aligns with managed AWS service best practices and enhances scalability and fault tolerance.

answers.content: Create two Amazon EventBridge event buses: a primary event bus and a secondary event bus. Update the API to use a new integration to the primary event bus. Configure an EventBridge rule to react to all events on the primary event bus. Specify the Lambda function as the target of the rulConfigure the secondary event bus as the failure destination for the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: EventBridge event buses add complexity and do not provide the best mechanism to buffer and retry failed pre-processing data.

answers.content: Create a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus. Configure the event bus as the failure destination for the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Using just an EventBridge event bus as failure destination lacks the buffering and retry capabilities provided by SQS queues.

questions.content: A large company is migrating its entire IT portfolio to AWS. Each business unit in the company has a standalone AWS account that supports both development and test environments. New accounts to support production workloads will be needed soon.  The finance department requires a centralized method for payment but must maintain visibility into each group's spending to allocate costs.  The security team requires a centralized mechanism to control IAM usage in all the company’s accounts.  What combination of the following options meets the company’s needs with the LEAST effort? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use a collection of parameterized AWS CloudFormation templates defining common IAM permissions that are launched into each account. Require all new and existing accounts to launch the appropriate stacks to enforce the least privilege model.
answers.explanation: Using parameterized CloudFormation templates requires manual deployment and ongoing management in each account, increasing effort and complexity.

answers.content: Use AWS Organizations to create a new organization from a chosen payer account and define an organizational unit hierarchy. Invite the existing accounts to join the organization and create new accounts using Organizations.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations provides centralized billing (one payer account) while still giving cost visibility per account for chargeback, and it is the standard, low-effort way to manage many AWS accounts at scale.

answers.content: Require each business unit to use its own AWS accounts. Tag each AWS account appropriately and enable Cost Explorer to administer chargebacks.
answers.explanation: Having each business unit use separate accounts with tags and Cost Explorer lacks centralized payment control and does not address centralized IAM control.

answers.content: Enable all features of AWS Organizations and establish appropriate service control policies that filter IAM permissions for sub-accounts.
answers.explanation: Service control policies (SCPs) give the security team a centralized, organization-wide way to control and restrict IAM usage across all accounts, without needing to manage IAM policies individually in each account.

answers.content: Consolidate all of the company's AWS accounts into a single AWS account. Use tags for billing purposes and the IAM’s Access Advisor feature to enforce the least privilege model.
answers.explanation: Consolidating all workloads into a single account is not recommended due to security and management complexity; tagging alone does not enforce IAM permissions.

questions.content: A company has a web application that securely uploads pictures and videos to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company requires that only authenticated users are allowed to post content. The application generates a presigned URL that is used to upload objects through a browser interfacMost users are reporting slow upload times for objects larger than 100 MB.  What can a solutions architect do to improve the performance of these uploads while ensuring only authenticated users are allowed to post content?

answers.content: Set up an Amazon API Gateway with an edge-optimized API endpoint that has a resource as an S3 service proxy. Configure the PUT method for this resource to expose the S3 PutObject operation. Secure the API Gateway using a COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer. Have the browser interface use API Gateway instead of the presigned URL to upload objects.
answers.explanation: Using API Gateway as a proxy increases complexity and may introduce latency instead of improving performance.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon API Gateway with a regional API endpoint that has a resource as an S3 service proxy. Configure the PUT method for this resource to expose the S3 PutObject operation. Secure the API Gateway using an AWS Lambda authorizer. Have the browser interface use API Gateway instead of the presigned URL to upload objects.
answers.explanation: Similar to A, using API Gateway with Lambda authorizer adds complexity and does not necessarily improve upload speed for large files.

answers.content: Enable an S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint on the S3 bucket. Use the endpoint when generating the presigned URL. Have the browser interface upload the objects to this URL using the S3 multipart upload API.
answers.explanation: Enabling S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload speed for large files by optimizing network paths. Using S3 Transfer Acceleration with presigned URLs maintains secure, authenticated upload access as the presigned URL respects IAM permissions. This solution leverages a managed AWS service designed for performance and security optimization without altering the security model. It aligns with the best practice of using managed AWS services and preserving security controls via presigned URLs rather than adding complexity.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the destination S3 bucket. Enable PUT and POST methods for the CloudFront cache behavior. Update the CloudFront origin to use an origin access identity (OAI). Give the OAI user 3: PutObject permissions in the bucket policy. Have the browser interface upload objects using the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: CloudFront is not intended for PUT/POST uploads; enabling these methods is less common and not designed for upload acceleration, hence may not improve performance or security effectively.

questions.content: A company that provides image storage services wants to deploy a customer-facing solution to AWS. Millions of individual customers will use the solution. The solution will receive batches of large image files, resize the files, and store the files in an Amazon S3 bucket for up to 6 months.  The solution must handle significant variance in demand. The solution must also be reliable at enterprise scale and have the ability to rerun processing jobs in the event of failur Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use AWS Step Functions to process the S3 event that occurs when a user stores an imagRun an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image in place and replaces the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy to expire all stored images after 6 months.
answers.explanation: AWS Step Functions provide a reliable way to orchestrate the image resizing process and handle retries in case of failures, meeting the requirement to rerun processing jobs. Using S3 Lifecycle expiration policies to automatically expire images after 6 months aligns with cost-effective storage management. Lambda functions are suitable for resizing images on the fly with automatic scaling for demand variancReplacing the original file in the S3 bucket simplifies storage management and cost control.

answers.content: Use Amazon EventBridge to process the S3 event that occurs when a user uploads an imagRun an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image in place and replaces the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy to expire all stored images after 6 months.
answers.explanation: Amazon EventBridge is not typically used to process S3 events when S3 Event Notifications is the direct and simpler solution.

answers.content: Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a user stores an imagUse the Lambda function to resize the image in place and to store the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move all stored images to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 6 months.
answers.explanation: Moving images to S3 Standard-IA after 6 months does not meet the requirement to expire the images after 6 months; it would incur costs unnecessarily.

answers.content: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to process the S3 event that occurs when a user stores an imagRun an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image and stores the resized file in an S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move all stored images to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 6 months.
answers.explanation: Storing resized files in S3 Standard-IA and moving to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 6 months introduces complexity and cost that does not align with the expiration requirement.

questions.content: A company runs an intranet application on premises. The company wants to configure a cloud backup of the application. The company has selected AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery for this solution.  The company requires that replication traffic does not travel through the public internet. The application also must not be accessible from the internet. The company does not want this solution to consume all available network bandwidth because other applications require bandwidth.  Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a VPC that has at least two private subnets, two NAT gateways, and a virtual private gateway.
answers.explanation: Correct part of the solution; private subnets and virtual private gateway provide private networking required.

answers.content: Create a VPC that has at least two public subnets, a virtual private gateway, and an internet gateway.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because public subnets and an internet gateway would expose application to the internet, violating security requirements.

answers.content: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises network and the target AWS network.
answers.explanation: While VPN provides private connectivity, Direct Connect is a preferred managed service for dedicated bandwidth control and does not consume internet bandwidth, better meeting the bandwidth constraint.

answers.content: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection and a Direct Connect gateway between the on-premises network and the target AWS network.
answers.explanation: Correct part of the solution; provides private dedicated connection and bandwidth control preventing internet use.

answers.content: During configuration of the replication servers, select the option to use private IP addresses for data replication.
answers.explanation: Correct part of the solution; ensures replication uses private IPs and thus private network traffic.

answers.content: During configuration of the launch settings for the target servers, select the option to ensure that the Recovery instance’s private IP address matches the source server's private IP address.
answers.explanation: This option is incorrect because preserving the source server’s private IP address does not help keep replication traffic off the public internet, restrict application internet access, or control bandwidth usage. It only affects post-recovery network compatibility, which is not part of the stated requirements.

questions.content: A live-events company is designing a scaling solution for its ticket application on AWS. The application has high peaks of utilization during sale events. Each sale event is a one-time event that is scheduled. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses PostgreSQL for the database layer.  The company needs a scaling solution to maximize availability during the sale events.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use a predictive scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 Multi-AZ DB instance with automatically scaling read replicas. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to run parallel AWS Lambda functions to pre-warm the database before a sale event. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the state machine.
answers.explanation: Predictive scaling policies are recommended to handle scheduled and predictable scaling needs effectively, maximizing availability during peak events. Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 with Multi-AZ and automatically scaling read replicas provides high availability and seamless scalability for the database layer. Using AWS Step Functions and Lambda to pre-warm the database ensures readiness and optimal performance at the start of the event, supporting availability. An EventBridge rule to schedule these actions aligns with managing scaling for one-time scheduled events.

answers.content: Use a scheduled scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Mulli-AZ DB instance with automatically scaling read replicas. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to create a larger read replica before a sale event. Fail over to the larger read replica. Create another EventBridge rule that invokes another Lambda function to scale down the read replica after the sale event.
answers.explanation: Relies on scheduled scaling and manual Lambda scaling of read replicas, which is less automated and scalable than predictive scaling and Aurora Serverless.

answers.content: Use a predictive scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL MultiAZ DB instance with automatically scaling read replicas. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to run parallel AWS Lambda functions to pre-warm the database before a sale event. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the state machine.
answers.explanation: Uses RDS for PostgreSQL which does not have the seamless scaling and serverless capabilities of Aurora Serverless v2, reducing scalability and availability benefits.

answers.content: Use a scheduled scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB cluster. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to create a larger Aurora Replica before a sale event. Fail over to the larger Aurora Replica. Create another EventBridge rule that invokes another Lambda function to scale down the Aurora Replica after the sale event.
answers.explanation: Involves manual Lambda functions to scale Aurora replicas up and down, less preferable than automatic scaling capabilities and predictive scaling policy for EC2.

questions.content: A company has multiple AWS accounts. The company recently had a security audit that revealed many unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes attached to Amazon EC2 instances.  A solutions architect must encrypt the unencrypted volumes and ensure that unencrypted volumes will be detected automatically in the futurAdditionally, the company wants a solution that can centrally manage multiple AWS accounts with a focus on compliance and security.  Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Set up AWS Control Tower, and turn on the strongly recommended controls (guardrails). Join all accounts to the organization. Categorize the AWS accounts into OUs.
answers.explanation: Turning on strongly recommended controls is less strict than mandatory controls; best to enforce mandatory guardrails for security compliance.

answers.content: Use the AWS CLI to list all the unencrypted volumes in all the AWS accounts. Run a script to encrypt all the unencrypted volumes in place.
answers.explanation: Running a script to encrypt volumes in place is not possible; no direct in-place encryption exists for unencrypted EBS volumes.

answers.content: Create a snapshot of each unencrypted volumCreate a new encrypted volume from the unencrypted snapshot. Detach the existing volume, and replace it with the encrypted volume.
answers.explanation: EBS volumes cannot be encrypted in place, so the only supported way to encrypt existing unencrypted volumes is to create a snapshot, create a new encrypted volume from that snapshot, and replace the original volume.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Set up AWS Control Tower, and turn on the mandatory controls (guardrails). Join all accounts to the organization. Categorize the AWS accounts into OUs.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower provides centralized, multi-account governance and compliance, and its mandatory guardrails help ensure security baselines (including encryption-related controls and visibility) across all accounts with minimal operational effort.

answers.content: Turn on AWS CloudTrail. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect and automatically encrypt unencrypted volumes.
answers.explanation: No automated encryption can be triggered by EventBridge for unencrypted volumes; detection might be possible, but automatic encryption is not supported.

questions.content: A company hosts a VPN in an on-premises data center. Employees currently connect to the VPN to access files in their Windows home directories. Recently, there has been a large growth in the number of employees who work remotely. As a result, bandwidth usage for connections into the data center has begun to reach 100% during business hours.  The company must design a solution on AWS that will support the growth of the company's remote workforce, reduce the bandwidth usage for connections into the data center, and reduce operational overhead.  Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Mount a volume from the Volume Gateway to the on-premises file server.
answers.explanation: The Volume Gateway is used to store data in Amazon S3 while providing low-latency access to on-premises applications via iSCSI. While it uses cloud storage, the files are still being accessed by employees via the on-premises VPN and file server. This would not reduce the bandwidth usage for connections into the data center; in fact, it may increase bandwidth usage between the gateway and AWS as data is synced/cached. (Reference: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html>)

answers.content: Migrate the home directories to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed, highly reliable, and scalable file storage that is natively compatible with Windows file systems (SMB protocol). Migrating the home directories to FSx for Windows File Server allows remote employees to access their files directly in AWS, bypassing the on-premises data center VPN and significantly reducing the on-premises bandwidth strain. Being a fully managed service, it inherently reduces operational overhead compared to running and maintaining a file server on EC2 or on-premises. (Reference: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html>) Choose D: Migrate remote users to AWS Client VPN. AWS Client VPN is a managed client-based VPN service that enables secure access to AWS resources (like the FSx file server) and on-premises networks. By using AWS Client VPN, the company supports the growing remote workforce with a fully elastic, scalable, and managed VPN solution that eliminates the operational burden of deploying and maintaining a self-managed, on-premises VPN. This addresses the need to support the remote workforce and reduces operational overhead. (Reference: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/what-is.html>) The combination of B and D meets all requirements: supporting growth (D), reducing on-premises bandwidth usage (B, as traffic moves to AWS), and reducing operational overhead (B and D, as both are fully managed AWS services).

answers.content: Migrate the home directories to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) workloads and parallel file systems, not typically for general-purpose Windows home directories that require SMB protocol compatibility. Using FSx for Lustre would require migrating data to a non-Windows native file system and might increase complexity and operational overhead unnecessarily for this use case. (Reference: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html>)

answers.content: Migrate remote users to AWS Client VPN.
answers.explanation: AWS Client VPN is a managed client-based VPN service that enables secure access to AWS resources (like the FSx file server) and on-premises networks. By using AWS Client VPN, the company supports the growing remote workforce with a fully elastic, scalable, and managed VPN solution that eliminates the operational burden of deploying and maintaining a self-managed, on-premises VPN. This addresses the need to support the remote workforce and reduces operational overhead. (Reference: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/what-is.html>)

answers.content: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection from the on-premises data center to AWS.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection between the data center and AWS. While this could improve the network connection quality, it does not fundamentally change the architecture: employees still connect via the on-premises VPN, and the file access traffic still passes through the on-premises data center, consuming the high bandwidth. It also does not reduce operational overhead; it adds another service to manage.

questions.content: An enterprise company is building an infrastructure services platform for its users. The company has the following requirements:  • Provide least privilege access to users when launching AWS infrastructure so users cannot provision unapproved services. • Use a central account to manage the creation of infrastructure services. • Provide the ability to distribute infrastructure services to multiple accounts in AWS Organizations. • Provide the ability to enforce tags on any infrastructure that is started by users.  Which combination of actions using AWS services will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Develop infrastructure services using AWS CloudFormation templates. Add the templates to a central Amazon S3 bucket and add the IAM roles or users that require access to the S3 bucket policy.
answers.explanation: Storing CloudFormation templates in Amazon S3 does not prevent users from modifying templates or provisioning unapproved services, and it does not enforce centralized governance or mandatory tagging.

answers.content: Develop infrastructure services using AWS CloudFormation templates. Upload each template as an AWS Service Catalog product to portfolios created in a central AWS account. Share these portfolios with the Organizations structure created for the company.
answers.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows centrally managed CloudFormation-based products to be shared across multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations, ensuring users can launch only approved infrastructure.

answers.content: Allow user IAM roles to have AWSCloudFormationFullAccess and AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess permissions. Add an Organizations SCP at the AWS account root user level to deny all services except AWS CloudFormation and Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Granting AWSCloudFormationFullAccess violates the principle of least privilege, and using SCPs to restrict services is overly broad and does not provide fine-grained control or tagging enforcement.

answers.content: Allow user IAM roles to have ServiceCatalogEndUserAccess permissions only. Use an automation script to import the central portfolios to local AWS accounts, copy the TagOption, assign users access, and apply launch constraints.
answers.explanation: Granting only ServiceCatalogEndUserAccess enforces least-privilege access, while launch constraints ensure resources are created using controlled IAM roles.

answers.content: Use the AWS Service Catalog TagOption Library to maintain a list of tags required by the company. Apply the TagOption to AWS Service Catalog products or portfolios.
answers.explanation: AWS Service Catalog TagOption Library enforces mandatory tags on all launched resources, preventing users from bypassing tagging requirements.

answers.content: Use the AWS CloudFormation Resource Tags property to enforce the application of tags to any CloudFormation templates that will be created for users.
answers.explanation: CloudFormation resource tags can be removed or altered by users and do not provide centralized enforcement across accounts, unlike Service Catalog TagOptions.

questions.content: A company is running multiple workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company has separate units for software development. The company uses AWS Organizations and federation with SAML to give permissions to developers to manage resources in their AWS accounts. The development units each deploy their production workloads into a common production account.  Recently, an incident occurred in the production account in which members of a development unit terminated an EC2 instance that belonged to a different development unit.
