A solutions architect must create a solution that prevents a similar incident from happening in the futurThe solution also must allow developers the possibility to manage the instances used for their workloads.  Which strategy will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create separate OUs in AWS Organizations for each development unit. Assign the created OUs to the company AWS accounts. Create separate SCP with a deny action and a StringNotEquals condition for the DevelopmentUnit resource tag that matches the development unit namAssign the SCP to the corresponding OU.
answers.explanation: SCPs with deny actions at OU level are less flexible and cannot enforce user session tag conditions during runtime effectively.

answers.content: Pass an attribute for DevelopmentUnit as an AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) session tag during SAML federation. Update the IAM policy for the developers’ assumed IAM role with a deny action and a StringNotEquals condition for the DevelopmentUnit resource tag and aws:PrincipalTag/DevelopmentUnit.
answers.explanation: Using AWS STS session tags during SAML federation allows attribute-based access control that directly ties the developer's identity to resource tags. An IAM policy with deny action and StringNotEquals condition on resource tags ensures developers cannot manage resources outside their scopThis approach enforces strict permission boundaries without relying on organizational units or service control policies, meeting security best practices. It allows developers the ability to manage only their designated development unit's instances.

answers.content: Pass an attribute for DevelopmentUnit as an AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) session tag during SAML federation. Create an SCP with an allow action and a StringEquals condition for the DevelopmentUnit resource tag and aws:PrincipalTag/DevelopmentUnit. Assign the SCP to the root OU.
answers.explanation: SCPs with allow actions on the root OU are less granular and less practical for enforcing developer-level permissions.

answers.content: Create separate IAM policies for each development unit. For every IAM policy, add an allow action and a StringEquals condition for the DevelopmentUnit resource tag and the development unit namDuring SAML federation, use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to assign the IAM policy and match the development unit name to the assumed IAM role.
answers.explanation: Assigning separate IAM policies during federation by matching development unit names is operationally complex and less secure than using session tags with conditions.

questions.content: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations that includes a separate AWS account for each of the company’s departments. Application teams from different departments develop and deploy solutions independently.  The company wants to reduce compute costs and manage costs appropriately across departments. The company also wants to improve visibility into billing for individual departments. The company does not want to lose operational flexibility when the company selects compute resources.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Budgets for each department. Use Tag Editor to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans.
answers.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans limit flexibility compared to Compute Savings Plans; AWS Budgets alone do not provide tagging or consolidated billing benefits.

answers.content: Configure AWS Organizations to use consolidated billing. Implement a tagging strategy that identifies departments. Use SCPs to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans.
answers.explanation: SCPs cannot be used to apply tags to resources and may reduce operational flexibility; also EC2 Instance Savings Plans limit compute flexibility.

answers.content: Configure AWS Organizations to use consolidated billing. Implement a tagging strategy that identifies departments. Use Tag Editor to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations consolidated billing allows cost visibility across departments while maintaining account separation. A tagging strategy enables identification of resources per department for detailed billing and cost management. Using Tag Editor to apply tags aligns with best practices for managing resource metadata. Compute Savings Plans provide flexibility across compute usage without restricting to EC2 instance types or regions, preserving operational flexibility. Therefore, option C best meets the cost visibility, flexibility, and cost reduction requirements.

answers.content: Use AWS Budgets for each department. Use SCPs to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.
answers.explanation: SCPs are not appropriate for applying tags and lack consolidated billing setup; AWS Budgets do not directly manage tagging or billing visibility.

questions.content: A company is using multiple AWS accounts and has multiple DevOps teams running production and non-production workloads in these accounts. The company would like to centrally-restrict access to some of the AWS services that the DevOps teams do not usThe company decided to use AWS Organizations and successfully invited all AWS accounts into the Organization. They would like to allow access to services that are currently in-use and deny a few specific services. Also they would like to administer multiple accounts together as a single unit.  What combination of steps should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Use a Deny list strategy.
answers.explanation: Correct because it directly supports denying specific services.

answers.content: Review the Access Advisor in AWS IAM to determine services recently used
answers.explanation: Correct because Access Advisor is the tool to review service usage and inform policy decisions.

answers.content: Review the AWS Trusted Advisor report to determine services recently used.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because Trusted Advisor is not used to determine recent service usage for access control.

answers.content: Remove the default FullAWSAccess SCP.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because removing the default FullAWSAccess SCP could unintentionally block needed permissions; not indicated as a needed step.

answers.content: Define organizational units (OUs) and place the member accounts in the OUs.
answers.explanation: Correct as OUs enable grouping accounts for collective management.

answers.content: Remove the default DenyAWSAccess SCP.
answers.explanation: The option “Remove the default DenyAWSAccess SCP” is incorrect because the default DenyAWSAccess SCP is applied only to the root of the organization to prevent accounts from using services until explicitly allowed, and it is not meant to be removed to manage service-level restrictions. Service access should instead be controlled by creating and attaching custom SCPs to OUs that allow required services and explicitly deny unused ones, while keeping the organization’s baseline protections intact.

questions.content: A company has a website that serves many visitors. The company deploys a backend service for the website in a primary AWS Region and a disaster recovery (DR) Region.  A single Amazon CloudFront distribution is deployed for the websitThe company creates an Amazon Route 53 record set with health checks and a failover routing policy for the primary Region’s backend servicThe company configures the Route 53 record set as an origin for the CloudFront distribution. The company configures another record set that points to the backend service's endpoint in the DR Region as a secondary failover record typThe TTL for both record sets is 60 seconds.  Currently, failover takes more than 1 minutA solutions architect must design a solution that will provide the fastest failover tim Which solution will achieve this goal?

answers.content: Deploy an additional CloudFront distribution. Create a new Route 53 failover record set with health checks for both CloudFront distributions.
answers.explanation: Adding another CloudFront distribution with Route 53 failover complicates the architecture without improving actual failover speed.

answers.content: Set the TTL to 4 second for the existing Route 53 record sets that are used for the backend service in each Region.
answers.explanation: Setting the TTL to 4 seconds may reduce DNS caching time but does not guarantee faster failover due to client and resolver caching behaviors.

answers.content: Create new record sets for the backend services by using a latency routing policy. Use the record sets as an origin in the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: Latency routing does not provide a failover mechanism; it routes based on latency, which won't ensure immediate failover on failure.

answers.content: Create a CloudFront origin group that includes two origins, one for each backend service Region. Configure origin failover as a cache behavior for the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: Using a CloudFront origin group with origin failover provides the fastest failover because CloudFront handles failover at the edge location level, which reduces latency and failover timRoute 53 failover with health checks and a 60-second TTL already causes failover delays, and reducing TTL to 4 seconds may not guarantee faster failover due to DNS caching behavior. Latency routing policy does not inherently provide failover capability but directs traffic based on latency, which may not address fast failover requirements. Deploying an additional CloudFront distribution and Route 53 failover records adds complexity and does not improve failover time as effectively as CloudFront origin failover. AWS best practices recommend using managed services and built-in failover mechanisms (CloudFront origin groups) for faster and more reliable failover.

questions.content: A company hosts an intranet web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Currently, users authenticate to the application against an internal user databas The company needs to authenticate users to the application by using an existing AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory directory. All users with accounts in the directory must have access to the application.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new app client in the directory. Create a listener rule for the ALB. Specify the authenticate-oidc action for the listener rulConfigure the listener rule with the appropriate issuer, client ID and secret, and endpoint details for the Active Directory servicConfigure the new app client with the callback URL that the ALB provides.
answers.explanation: The authenticate-oidc action requires an OIDC compatible IdP, but AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD is not an OIDC provider.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool. Configure the user pool with a federated identity provider (ldP) that has metadata from the directory. Create an app client. Associate the app client with the user pool. Create a listener rule for the ALSpecify the authenticate-cognito action for the listener rulConfigure the listener rule to use the user pool and app client.
answers.explanation: Amazon Cognito user pools can be configured with federated identity providers using metadata from AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Cognito supports authentication via federated IdPs and can be integrated with an ALB using the authenticate-cognito action in listener rules. This approach leverages managed AWS services, follows best practices for secure authentication, and avoids custom or unsupported configurations.

answers.content: Add the directory as a new IAM identity provider (ldP). Create a new IAM role that has an entity type of SAML 2.0 federation. Configure a role policy that allows access to the ALB. Configure the new role as the default authenticated user role for the ldP. Create a listener rule for the ALB. Specify the authenticate-oidc action for the listener rule.
answers.explanation: AWS IAM does not support adding an Active Directory as a SAML identity provider directly for ALB authentication, and the authenticate-oidc action is incorrectly mentioned here.

answers.content: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure the directory as an external identity provider (ldP) that uses SAML. Use the automatic provisioning method. Create a new IAM role that has an entity type of SAML 2.0 federation. Configure a role policy that allows access to the ALB. Attach the new role to all groups. Create a listener rule for the ALB. Specify the authenticate-cognito action for the listener rule.
answers.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) is not directly integrated with ALB listener rules using authenticate-cognito action, and this is an unnecessarily complex approach for the requirement.

questions.content: A company hosts a community forum site using an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a Docker application hosted in an Amazon ECS cluster. The site data is stored in Amazon RDS for MySQL and the container image is stored in ECR. The company needs to provide their customers with a disaster recovery SLA with an RTO of no more than 24 hours and RPO of no more than 8 hours.  Which of the following solutions is the MOST cost-effective way to meet the requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation to deploy identical ALB, EC2, ECS and RDS resources in two regions. Schedule RDS snapshots every 8 hours. Use RDS multi-region replication to update the secondary region's copy of the databasIn the event of a failure, restore from the latest snapshot, and use an Amazon Route 53 DNS failover policy to automatically redirect customers to the ALB in the secondary region.
answers.explanation: Maintaining identical full environments in two regions is less cost-effective and more complex, unnecessary for the RTO and RPO requirements.

answers.content: Store the Docker image in ECR in two regions. Schedule RDS snapshots every 8 hours with snapshots copied to the secondary region. In the event of a failure, use AWS CloudFormation to deploy the ALB, EC2, ECS and RDS resources in the secondary region, restore from the latest snapshot, and update the DNS record to point to the ALB in the secondary region.
answers.explanation: Deploying resources only after a failure causes longer RTO than allowed; no existing environment in secondary region.

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation to deploy identical ALB, EC2, ECS, and RDS resources in a secondary region. Schedule hourly RDS MySQL backups to Amazon S3 and use cross-region replication to replicate data to a bucket in the secondary region. In the event of a failure, import the latest Docker image to Amazon ECR in the secondary region, deploy to the EC2 instance, restore the latest MySQL backup, and update the DNS record to point to the ALB in the secondary region.
answers.explanation: Restoring backups manually to a new environment increases RTO beyond 24 hours and is operationally intensive.

answers.content: Deploy a pilot light environment in a secondary region with an ALB and a minimal resource EC2 deployment for Docker in an AWS Auto Scaling group with a scaling policy to increase instance size and number of nodes. Create a cross-region read replica of the RDS data. In the event of a failure, promote the replica to primary, and update the DNS record to point to the ALB in the secondary region.
answers.explanation: Deploying a pilot light environment in the secondary region with an ALB and minimal EC2 resources allows faster recovery than restoring from snapshots, meeting the RTO of no more than 24 hours. Creating a cross-region read replica of the RDS database provides continuous data replication, supporting an RPO of no more than 8 hours. Using a cross-region read replica is more cost-effective than deploying full identical environments across regions or restoring from backups on demand. Automated promotion of the read replica and DNS update aligns with AWS best practices for managed disaster recovery solutions.

questions.content: A company orchestrates a multi-account structure on AWS by using AWS Control Tower. The company is using AWS Organizations, AWS Config, and AWS Trusted Advisor. The company has a specific OU for development accounts that developers use to experiment on AWS. The company has hundreds of developers, and each developer has an individual development account.  The company wants to optimize costs in these development accounts. Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS instances in these accounts must be burstablThe company wants to disallow the use of other services that are not relevant.  What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a custom SCP in AWS Organizations to allow the deployment of only burstable instances and to disallow services that are not relevant. Apply the SCP to the development OU.
answers.explanation: SCPs do not prevent resource creation immediately; they act as permission boundaries but allow broader configurations if not explicitly denied.

answers.content: Create a custom detective control (guardrail) in AWS Control Tower. Configure the control (guardrail) to allow the deployment of only burstable instances and to disallow services that are not relevant. Apply the control (guardrail) to the development OU.
answers.explanation: Detective controls only detect violations post-deployment and do not prevent usage of non-burstable instances or disallowed services.

answers.content: Create a custom preventive control (guardrail) in AWS Control Tower. Configure the control (guardrail) to allow the deployment of only burstable instances and to disallow services that are not relevant. Apply the control (guardrail) to the development OU.
answers.explanation: Preventive controls (guardrails) in AWS Control Tower actively enforce policies to disallow undesired actions, which meets the requirement to restrict instance types and disallow irrelevant services. AWS Control Tower is designed to orchestrate multi-account environments and integrates with AWS Organizations, making it the preferred managed service for applying such restrictions. Using SCPs (option A) allows control but preventive guardrails provide stronger enforcement and better integration within Control Tower. Detective controls (option B) only detect policy violations but do not prevent deployment, which is less secure and less compliant with best practices. AWS Config rules (option D) are useful for detection and remediation but are not as directly integrated into Control Tower's guardrail framework for direct enforcement.

answers.content: Create an AWS Config rule in the AWS Control Tower account. Configure the AWS Config rule to allow the deployment of only burstable instances and to disallow services that are not relevant. Deploy the AWS Config rule to the development OU by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules are for compliance checking and remediation but do not provide direct preventive enforcement within Control Tower like guardrails.

questions.content: A company maintains information on premises in approximately 1 million.csv files that are hosted on a VM. The data initially is 10 TB in size and grows at a rate of 1 TB each week. The company needs to automate backups of the data to the AWS Cloud.  Backups of the data must occur daily. The company needs a solution that applies custom filters to back up only a subset of the data that is located in designated source directories. The company has set up an AWS Direct Connect connection.  Which solution will meet the backup requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Use the Amazon S3 CopyObject API operation with multipart upload to copy the existing data to Amazon S3. Use the CopyObject API operation to replicate new data to Amazon S3 daily.
answers.explanation: CopyObject is not designed for large-scale incremental daily backups and involves high manual overhead.

answers.content: Create a backup plan in AWS Backup to back up the data to Amazon S3. Schedule the backup plan to run daily.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup doesn’t natively backup on-premises file systems directly without agent integration or additional setup.

answers.content: Install the AWS DataSync agent as a VM that runs on the on-premises hypervisor. Configure a DataSync task to replicate the data to Amazon S3 daily.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync can be installed as an agent on-premises to automate data transfer to Amazon S3. DataSync supports filtering to replicate only subsets of data, matching the requirement to filter by specific directories. It integrates with AWS managed services and operates over the AWS Direct Connect connection, minimizing operational overhead. Using DataSync is a managed service solution, preferred over manual methods or custom scripts. Snowball Edge is operationally heavier for ongoing weekly backups compared to DataSync for incremental backups. Backup plans with AWS Backup do not natively support direct backup of on-premises files without agents. The CopyObject API is manual and high overhead for daily large volume incremental backups.

answers.content: Use an AWS Snowball Edge device for the initial backup. Use AWS DataSync for incremental backups to Amazon S3 daily.
answers.explanation: Snowball Edge adds operational complexity; better for initial bulk transfer but not lowest overhead for daily incremental backups.

questions.content: A financial services company sells its software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform for application compliance to large global banks. The SaaS platform runs on AWS and uses multiple AWS accounts that are managed in an organization in AWS Organizations. The SaaS platform uses many AWS resources globally.  For regulatory compliance, all API calls to AWS resources must be audited, tracked for changes, and stored in a durable and secure data stor Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create a new AWS CloudTrail trail. Use an existing Amazon S3 bucket in the organization's management account to store the logs. Deploy the trail to all AWS Regions. Enable MFA delete and encryption on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Uses an existing S3 bucket, which may not be ideally configured for new audit logs, and does not specify organization-wide trail deployment explicitly, potentially increasing management complexity.

answers.content: Create a new AWS CloudTrail trail in each member account of the organization. Create new Amazon S3 buckets to store the logs. Deploy the trail to all AWS Regions. Enable MFA delete and encryption on the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: Creates multiple trails and separate S3 buckets per member account, increasing operational overhead significantly.

answers.content: Create a new AWS CloudTrail trail in the organization's management account. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with versioning turned on to store the logs. Deploy the trail for all accounts in the organization. Enable MFA delete and encryption on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Creating a single AWS CloudTrail trail in the organization's management account with organization-wide logging minimizes operational overhead by eliminating the need to manage multiple trails. Using a new Amazon S3 bucket with versioning, MFA delete, and encryption ensures durability, security, and proper audit trail protection. Deploying the trail for all accounts in the organization meets the requirement of auditing all API calls globally. This approach aligns with AWS best practices for centralized logging and secure storage with minimal operational complexity.

answers.content: Create a new AWS CloudTrail trail in the organization's management account. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send log-file delivery notifications to an external management system that will track the logs. Enable MFA delete and encryption on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Includes an unnecessary external SNS notification system adding complexity without fulfilling auditing and storage requirements alone.

questions.content: A scientific company needs to process text and image data from an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is collected from several radar stations during a live, time-critical phase of a deep space mission. The radar stations upload the data to the source S3 bucket. The data is prefixed by radar station identification number.  The company created a destination S3 bucket in a second account. Data must be copied from the source S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket to meet a compliance objectivThis replication occurs through the use of an S3 replication rule to cover all objects in the source S3 bucket.  One specific radar station is identified as having the most accurate data. Data replication at this radar station must be monitored for completion within 30 minutes after the radar station uploads the objects to the source S3 bucket.  What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Setup an AWS DataSync agent to replicate the prefixed data from the source S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket. Select to use all available bandwidth on the task, and monitor the task to ensure that itis in the TRANSFERRING status. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert if this status changes.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is not intended for S3-to-S3 replication and monitoring replication at the object level; it's also more complex and less native for this use case.

answers.content: In the second account, create another S3 bucket to receive data from the radar station with the most accurate data. Set up a new replication rule for this new S3 bucket to separate the replication from the other radar stations. Monitor the maximum replication time to the destination. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert when the time exceeds the desired threshold.
answers.explanation: Creating an additional S3 bucket and replication rule in the second account adds unnecessary complexity; it does not use S3 RTC, so replication time is not guaranteed or easily monitored.

answers.content: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source S3 bucket, and configure the radar station with the most accurate data to use the new endpoint. Monitor the S3 destination bucket's TotalRequestLatency metric. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert if this status changes.
answers.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload speed but does not guarantee replication time or provide replication monitoring; monitoring TotalRequestLatency does not reflect replication status.

answers.content: Create a new S3 replication rule on the source S3 bucket that filters for the keys that use the prefix of the radar station with the most accurate data. Enable S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC). Monitor the maximum replication time to the destination. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert when the time exceeds the desired threshold.
answers.explanation: Using an S3 replication rule filtered by prefix aligns with the need to monitor replication of data from the specific radar station. Enabling S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) provides guaranteed replication within 15 minutes, which meets the 30-minute monitoring requirement. Monitoring replication time and creating an EventBridge alert follows AWS best practices for automated monitoring and alerting of replication delays. This solution uses native managed AWS S3 replication features, which is preferred over custom or manual solutions.

questions.content: A company is using AWS CodePipeline for the CI/CD of an application to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. All AWS resources are defined in AWS CloudFormation templates. The application artifacts are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and deployed to the Auto Scaling group using instance user data scripts. As the application has become more complex, recent resource changes in the CloudFormation templates have caused unplanned downtim How should a solutions architect improve the CI/CD pipeline to reduce the likelihood that changes in the templates will cause downtime?

answers.content: Adapt the deployment scripts to detect and report CloudFormation error conditions when performing deployments. Write test plans for a testing team to run in a non-production environment before approving the change for production.
answers.explanation: Relies on manual testing and error reporting without automation and automated validations, which is less reliable and slower.

answers.content: Implement automated testing using AWS CodeBuild in a test environment. Use CloudFormation change sets to evaluate changes before deployment. Use AWS CodeDeploy to leverage blue/green deployment patterns to allow evaluations and the ability to revert changes, if needed.
answers.explanation: Implementing automated testing in a test environment follows best practices for reducing downtime and errors before production deployment. Using CloudFormation change sets allows evaluating changes safely before applying them, minimizing risk. AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployments minimize downtime by shifting traffic without impacting running instances. Automated validations and the ability to revert changes align with safe deployment practices and reduce unplanned downtime.

answers.content: Use plugins for the integrated development environment (IDE) to check the templates for errors, and use the AWS CLI to validate that the templates are correct. Adapt the deployment code to check for error conditions and generate notifications on errors. Deploy to a test environment and run a manual test plan before approving the change for production.
answers.explanation: Relies on manual test plans and manual error notifications rather than automated testing and deployment strategies.

answers.content: Use AWS CodeDeploy and a blue/green deployment pattern with CloudFormation to replace the user data deployment scripts. Have the operators log in to running instances and go through a manual test plan to verify the application is running as expected.
answers.explanation: Manual testing by operators increases risk and slows response; manual verification is less reliable and scalable than automated solutions.

questions.content: A company migrated an application to the AWS Cloud. The application runs on two Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Application data is stored in a MySQL database that runs on an additional EC2 instancThe application's use of the database is read-heavy.  The application loads static content from Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instancThe static content is updated frequently and must be copied to each EBS volum The load on the application changes throughout the day. During peak hours, the application cannot handle all the incoming requests. Trace data shows that the database cannot handle the read load during peak hours.  Which solution will improve the reliability of the application?

answers.content: Migrate the application to a set of AWS Lambda functions. Set the Lambda functions as targets for the ALB. Create a new single EBS volume for the static content. Configure the Lambda functions to read from the new EBS volumMigrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster.
answers.explanation: Uses EBS for static content, which does not support shared access or frequent updates well; Lambda functions cannot directly read from EBS volumes, and running a single EBS volume is not suitable for distributed access.

answers.content: Migrate the application to a set of AWS Step Functions state machines. Set the state machines as targets for the ALCreate an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for the static content. Configure the state machines to read from the EFS file system. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 with a reader DB instance.
answers.explanation: Uses Step Functions for application hosting, which is not meant for serving web applications; Step Functions are orchestration services, not compute hosts for applications.

answers.content: Containerize the application. Migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Use the AWS Fargate launch type for the tasks that host the application. Create a new single EBS volume for the static content. Mount the new EBS volume on the ECS cluster. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the ECS cluster. Set the ECS service as a target for the ALB. Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster.
answers.explanation: Uses EBS for static content in a containerized ECS application, which is not feasible since EBS volumes cannot be shared across multiple containers dynamically; does not address the static content update issue effectively.

answers.content: Containerize the application. Migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Use the AWS Fargate launch type for the tasks that host the application. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for the static content. Mount the EFS file system to each container. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the ECS cluster. Set the ECS service as a target for the ALB. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 with a reader DB instance.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate launch type for the application provides managed container hosting with auto scaling, improving reliability during peak loads. Migrating the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 with a reader DB instance addresses read-heavy database load and improves scalability and reliability. Using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for static content supports frequent updates and allows consistent and scalable shared access without manual copying, which is better than using EBS volumes attached to individual instances or containers. Setting the ECS service as a target for the ALB ensures proper load balancing and scaling of the application containers.

questions.content: A company is using AWS Control Tower to manage AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company has an OU that contains accounts. The company must prevent any new or existing Amazon EC2 instances in the OU's accounts from gaining a public IP address.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure all instances in each account in the OU to use AWS Systems Manager. Use a Systems Manager Automation runbook to prevent public IP addresses from being attached to the instances.
answers.explanation: Systems Manager runbooks work post-launch and cannot prevent public IP assignment proactively.

answers.content: Implement the AWS Control Tower proactive control to check whether instances in the OU's accounts have a public IP address. Set the AssociatePublicIpAddress property to FalsAttach the proactive control to the OU.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower proactive controls do not exist specifically to set AssociatePublicIpAddress property to False on instances.

answers.content: Create an SCP that prevents the launch of instances that have a public IP address. Additionally, configure the SCP to prevent the attachment of a public IP address to existing instances. Attach the SCP to the OU.
answers.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) allow centralized control over what actions can be performed in accounts within an OU in AWS Organizations. An SCP can explicitly prevent the launch of instances with a public IP address and block attaching public IPs to existing instances. Control Tower itself does not have a built-in proactive control specifically for controlling public IP assignment on EC2 instances. AWS Systems Manager runbooks do not inherently prevent assignment of public IPs—they operate post-launch and are not preventivCustom AWS Config rules and Lambda remediation cannot proactively prevent IP assignment; they only detect and potentially remediate after the fact. Security best practices favor prevention of misconfiguration through policy enforcement rather than detection and remediation.

answers.content: Create an AWS Config custom rule that detects instances that have a public IP address. Configure a remediation action that uses an AWS Lambda function to detach the public IP addresses from the instances.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules detect noncompliance but cannot prevent instances from obtaining public IPs in the first place.

questions.content: A company is deploying AWS Lambda functions that access an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databasThe company needs to launch the Lambda functions in a QA environment and in a production environment.  The company must not expose credentials within application code and must rotate passwords automatically.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Systems Manager Parameter StorEncrypt the credentials by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Within the application code of the Lambda functions, pull the credentials from the Parameter Store parameter by using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3). Add a role to the Lambda functions to provide access to the Parameter Store parameter.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store does not support automatic password rotation, which is a key requirement.

answers.content: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Secrets Manager with distinct key entry for the QA environment and the production environment. Turn on rotation. Provide a reference to the Secrets Manager key as an environment variable for the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is designed for managing database credentials with secure storage, automatic password rotation, and environment-specific secrets. Using Secrets Manager aligns with best practices for avoiding credentials in application code and automating secret rotation. Providing secrets via environment variables referencing Secrets Manager is a common and secure pattern. Parameter Store (Option A) does not natively support automatic secret rotation, which is required. AWS KMS (Option C) is a key management service and does not store or rotate database credentials. Storing secrets in S3 buckets (Option D) is less secure and not recommended for managing credentials due to difficulty in automatic rotation and higher risk exposure.

answers.content: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Turn on rotation. Provide a reference to the credentials that are stored in AWS KMS as an environment variable for the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: AWS KMS is for encryption keys, not credential storage or rotation; it cannot manage database credentials directly.

answers.content: Create separate S3 buckets for the QA environment and the production environment. Turn on server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the S3 buckets. Use an object naming pattern that gives each Lambda function’s application code the ability to pull the correct credentials for the function's corresponding environment. Grant each Lambda function's execution role access to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials in S3, even with encryption, is not secure nor suitable for automatic password rotation, violating best practices.

questions.content: A company has AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company wants to track Amazon EC2 usage as a metric. The company’s architecture team must receive a daily alert if the EC2 usage is more than 10% higher the average EC2 usage from the last 30 days.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure AWS Budgets in the organization's management account. Specify a usage type of EC2 running hours. Specify a daily period. Set the budget amount to be 10% more than the reported average usage for the last 30 days from AWS Cost Explorer. Configure an alert to notify the architecture team if the usage threshold is met
answers.explanation: AWS Budgets can be configured to track EC2 usage metrics and set thresholds for alerts. It allows specifying usage type (such as EC2 running hours) and setting the budget period (daily). Budgets support alerting when usage exceeds a defined threshold compared to historical averages. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection provides alerts on cost anomalies but does not specifically track usage percentage increases against historical averages. Trusted Advisor is focused on cost optimization recommendations, not usage tracking or alerts. Amazon Detective is a security service focused on investigations and anomalies, not cost or usage monitoring.

answers.content: Configure AWS Cost Anomaly Detection in the organization's management account. Configure a monitor type of AWS ServicApply a filter of Amazon EC2. Configure an alert subscription to notify the architecture team if the usage is 10% more than the average usage for the last 30 days.
answers.explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection focuses on cost anomalies, not daily EC2 usage thresholds relative to historical averages.

answers.content: Enable AWS Trusted Advisor in the organization's management account. Configure a cost optimization advisory alert to notify the architecture team if the EC2 usage is 10% more than the reported average usage for the last 30 days.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor does not provide daily EC2 usage alerts or track usage increases relative to past data.

answers.content: Configure Amazon Detective in the organization's management account. Configure an EC2 usage anomaly alert to notify the architecture team if Detective identifies a usage anomaly of more than 10%.
answers.explanation: Amazon Detective is meant for security investigation, not resource usage alerts.

questions.content: A company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a web application. The application runs in a single AWS Region.  The application uses microservices that run in containers. The containers are hosted on AWS Fargate in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application has an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance as its data layer and uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS resolution. An Amazon CloudWatch alarm invokes an Amazon EventBridge rule if the application experiences a failur A solutions architect must design a DR solution to provide application recovery to a separate Region. The solution must minimize the time that is necessary to recover from a failur Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the following actions: take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance, copy the snapshot to the separate Region, create a new RDS DB instance from the snapshot, and update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Uses manual snapshot copy and restore on failover which increases recovery time.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function that creates a second ECS cluster and ECS service in the separate Region. Configure the Lambda function to perform the following actions: take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance, copy the snapshot to the separate Region, create a new RDS DB instance from the snapshot, and update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Creating ECS cluster via Lambda during failover is slower and manual snapshot restore increases downtime.

answers.content: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Create a cross-Region read replica of the RDS DB instance in the separate Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to promote the read replica to the primary databasConfigure the Lambda function to update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Setting up a second ECS cluster and ECS service in the DR Region follows best practice to have the application ready in advancUsing a cross-Region read replica for the Amazon RDS MySQL instance allows for minimal recovery time by promoting the replica to primary quickly. This approach avoids the delay involved in snapshot copying and restore during failover. Updating Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster ensures DNS-level failover. The Lambda function automates promotion and DNS update triggered by EventBridge, providing automated failover orchestration.

answers.content: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Take a snapshot of the RDS DB instancConvert the snapshot to an Amazon DynamoDB global tablCreate an AWS Lambda function to update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Converting a snapshot to DynamoDB global table is not supported and does not align with RDS MySQL use.

questions.content: A company has mounted sensors to collect information about environmental parameters such as humidity and light throughout all the company's factories. The company needs to stream and analyze the data in the AWS Cloud in real timIf any of the parameters fall out of acceptable ranges, the factory operations team must receive a notification immediately.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use AWS Step Functions to consume and analyze the data in the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team.
answers.explanation: Kinesis Data Firehose is designed for loading streaming data to destinations like S3 or Redshift, not ideal for real-time processing and immediate alerts.

answers.content: Stream the data to an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster. Set up a trigger in Amazon MSK to invoke an AWS Fargate task to analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the operations team.
answers.explanation: Amazon MSK involves more operational complexity and SES is less suitable for immediate notifications than SNS.

answers.content: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the Kinesis data stream and to analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team.
answers.explanation: Amazon Kinesis data streams are designed for real-time streaming data ingestion. AWS Lambda can directly consume Kinesis data streams and analyze data with minimal operational overhead. Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) provides immediate and reliable notification delivery to the operations team. This solution uses managed AWS services that are scalable and secure for real-time processing and alerting.

answers.content: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application. Use an automatically scaled and containerized service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to consume and analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the operations team.
answers.explanation: Kinesis Data Analytics combined with ECS adds unnecessary complexity; SES is less appropriate for immediate notifications.

questions.content: A company is running a serverless application that consists of several AWS Lambda functions and Amazon DynamoDB tables. The company has created new functionality that requires the Lambda functions to access an Amazon Neptune DB cluster. The Neptune DB cluster is located in three subnets in a VPC.  Which of the possible solutions will allow the Lambda functions to access the Neptune DB cluster and DynamoDB tables? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create three public subnets in the Neptune VPC, and route traffic through an internet gateway. Host the Lambda functions in the three new public subnets.
answers.explanation: Hosting Lambda functions in public subnets with an internet gateway is unnecessary and not recommended for accessing private databases like Neptune.

answers.content: Create three private subnets in the Neptune VPC, and route internet traffic through a NAT gateway. Host the Lambda functions in the three new private subnets.
answers.explanation: Placing Lambda functions in private subnets in the same VPC as the Neptune cluster allows direct access to Neptune, while a NAT gateway enables the Lambdas to access DynamoDB and other AWS services over the internet.

answers.content: Host the Lambda functions outside the VPUpdate the Neptune security group to allow access from the IP ranges of the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Lambda functions do not have fixed IP ranges that can be reliably allowed in security groups.

answers.content: Host the Lambda functions outside the VPC. Create a VPC endpoint for the Neptune database, and have the Lambda functions access Neptune over the VPC endpoint.
answers.explanation: Amazon Neptune does not support VPC endpoints; it must be accessed from within the same VPC.

answers.content: Create three private subnets in the Neptune VPC. Host the Lambda functions in the three new isolated subnets. Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB, and route DynamoDB traffic to the VPC endpoint.
answers.explanation: Hosting Lambda functions in private (isolated) subnets enables access to Neptune within the VPC, and using a DynamoDB VPC endpoint allows private connectivity to DynamoDB without requiring internet or a NAT gateway.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate its website from an on-premises data center onto AWS. At the same time, it wants to migrate the website to a containerized microservice-based architecture to improve the availability and cost efficiency. The company’s security policy states that privileges and network permissions must be configured according to best practice, using least privileg A solutions architect must create a containerized architecture that meets the security requirements and has deployed the application to an Amazon ECS cluster.  What steps are required after the deployment to meet the requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create tasks using the bridge network mode.
answers.explanation: Bridge network mode does not allow assigning security groups directly to tasks, limiting network isolation and least privilege enforcement.

answers.content: Create tasks using the awsvpc network mode.
answers.explanation: The awsvpc network mode is the recommended and most feature-rich networking mode for Amazon ECS tasks, especially when using the Fargate launch type (though the question is general to ECS clusters). When a task uses awsvpc network mode, Amazon ECS assigns an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) to the task. This allows the task to receive its own private IP address within the VPC, making it a first-class citizen in the VPC network. This is crucial because it allows you to associate security groups directly with the task ENI, enabling granular network control (least privilege).

answers.content: Apply security groups to Amazon EC2 instances, and use IAM roles for EC2 instances to access other resources.
answers.explanation: Applying security groups to EC2 instances and using EC2 instance IAM roles grants broader permissions than necessary to tasks, violating least privilege principle.

answers.content: Apply security groups to the tasks, and pass IAM credentials into the container at launch time to access other resources.
answers.explanation: Passing IAM credentials into containers at launch time is insecure and not recommended; IAM roles for tasks should be used instead.

answers.content: Apply security groups to the tasks, and use IAM roles for tasks to access other resources.
answers.explanation:
To meet the security requirements of least privilege:1.  Apply security groups directly to the tasks (enabled by awsvpc network mode) to control network traffic (inbound and outbound) at the task level, rather than at the host level.
2.  Use IAM roles for tasks (Task IAM Roles) to grant permissions to the containers running in the task. This ensures that the application only has the minimum permissions necessary to interact with other AWS services (e.g., S3, DynamoDB), fulfilling the least privilege principle for resource access.

questions.content: A company is collecting a large amount of data from a fleet of IoT devices. Data is stored as Optimized Row Columnar (ORC) files in the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) on a persistent Amazon EMR cluster. The company's data analytics team queries the data by using SQL in Apache Presto deployed on the same EMR cluster. Queries scan large amounts of data, always run for less than 15 minutes, and run only between 5 PM and 10 PM.  The company is concerned about the high cost associated with the current solution. A solutions architect must propose the most cost-effective solution that will allow SQL data queries.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Store data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query data.
answers.explanation: Redshift Spectrum requires a Redshift cluster which incurs cost; Athena is generally more cost-effective for ad-hoc queries without needing managed clusters.

answers.content: Store data in Amazon S3. Use the AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Athena to query data.
answers.explanation: Storing data in Amazon S3 reduces storage costs compared to a persistent EMR cluster. Amazon Athena allows serverless, on-demand SQL queries over data in S3 with no infrastructure to manage, which aligns with cost savings. Using the AWS Glue Data Catalog provides a managed metadata repository, improving query efficiency and integration with Athena. Presto on EMR requires a persistent cluster, which is costlier than Athena for infrequent querying within specified time windows.

answers.content: Store data in EMR File System (EMRFS). Use Presto in Amazon EMR to query data.
answers.explanation: Using EMRFS and Presto on a persistent EMR cluster is more expensive than serverless Athena for intermittent queries.

answers.content: Store data in Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift to query data.
answers.explanation: Storing data in Amazon Redshift involves higher costs for the cluster storage and compute, less cost-effective for this use case.

questions.content: A company is running a containerized application in the AWS Cloud. The application is running by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on a set of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group.  The company uses Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) to store its container images. When a new image version is uploaded, the new image version receives a unique tag.  The company needs a solution that inspects new image versions for common vulnerabilities and exposures. The solution must automatically delete new image tags that have Critical or High severity findings. The solution also must notify the development team when such a deletion occurs.  Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Configure scan on push on the repository. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Step Functions state machine when a scan is complete for images that have Critical or High severity findings. Use the Step Functions state machine to delete the image tag for those images and to notify the development team through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: Amazon ECR supports scan on push, which allows automatic scanning of images when they are uploaded. Amazon EventBridge can be used to detect when a scan completes and trigger actions accordingly. AWS Step Functions provide a managed workflow service to coordinate the deletion of image tags and send notifications, adhering to managed service preferencAmazon SNS is a native and suitable service to notify the development team, aligning with AWS best practices for notifications. This solution is automatic, uses managed AWS services, and ensures security by deleting images with critical or high vulnerabilities.

answers.content: Configure scan on push on the repository. Configure scan results to be pushed to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuInvoke an AWS Lambda function when a new message is added to the SQS queuUse the Lambda function to delete the image tag for images that have Critical or High severity findings. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
answers.explanation: Amazon ECR does not support pushing scan results to SQS; also SES is less suited for simple notifications compared to SNS.

answers.content: Schedule an AWS Lambda function to start a manual image scan every hour. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke another Lambda function when a scan is completUse the second Lambda function to delete the image tag for images that have Critical or High severity findings. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: Manual hourly scans are less efficient and do not leverage automated scan-on-push capabilities, reducing security responsiveness.

answers.content: Configure periodic image scan on the repository. Configure scan results to be added to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuInvoke an AWS Step Functions state machine when a new message is added to the SQS queuUse the Step Functions state machine to delete the image tag for images that have Critical or High severity findings. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
answers.explanation: Periodic scans are less effective than scan on push for immediate detection; also SQS integration for scan results is unsupported.

questions.content: A company uses a load balancer to distribute traffic to Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability ZonThe company is concerned about security and wants a solutions architect to re-architect the solution to meet the following requirements:  • Inbound requests must be filtered for common vulnerability attacks. • Rejected requests must be sent to a third-party auditing application. • All resources should be highly availabl Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Configure a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group using the application's AMI. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and select the previously created Auto Scaling group as the target. Use Amazon Inspector to monitor traffic to the ALB and EC2 instances. Create a web ACL in WAF. Create an AWS WAF using the web ACL and ALB. Use an AWS Lambda function to frequently push the Amazon Inspector report to the third-party auditing application.
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector is not intended for real-time filtering of inbound requests and does not directly integrate with WAF for rejecting requests or streaming logs to a third-party tool.

answers.content: Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and add the EC2 instances as targets. Create a web ACL in WAF. Create an AWS WAF using the web ACL and ALB name and enable logging with Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use an AWS Lambda function to frequently push the logs to the third-party auditing application.
answers.explanation: Pushing logs via AWS Lambda to the third-party auditing application adds operational overhead and potential delays; it also does not mention high availability through Multi-AZ deployment.

answers.content: Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) along with a target group adding the EC2 instances as targets. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with the destination of the third-party auditing application. Create a web ACL in WAF. Create an AWS WAF using the web ACL and ALB then enable logging by selecting the Kinesis Data Firehose as the destination. Subscribe to AWS Managed Rules in AWS Marketplace, choosing the WAF as the subscriber.
answers.explanation: Does not include a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group, which is essential for high availability; also lacks explicit mention of Multi-AZ deployment for the EC2 instances.

answers.content: Configure a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group using the application's AMI. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and select the previously created Auto Scaling group as the target. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with a destination of the third-party auditing application. Create a web ACL in WAF. Create an AWS WAF using the WebACL and ALB then enable logging by selecting the Kinesis Data Firehose as the destination. Subscribe to AWS Managed Rules in AWS Marketplace, choosing the WAF as the subscriber.
answers.explanation: Option D meets the high availability requirement by using a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer. It uses AWS WAF with a web ACL to filter inbound requests for common vulnerability attacks, which addresses the security requirement. D enables WAF logging with Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to directly stream rejected request data to the third-party auditing application, meeting the auditing requirement securely and efficiently. Using AWS Managed Rules from AWS Marketplace is a best practice for protecting against common attacks without custom rule management.

questions.content: A solutions architect is designing an AWS account structure for a company that consists of multiple teams. All the teams will work in the same AWS Region. The company needs a VPC that is connected to the on-premises network. The company expects less than 50 Mbps of total traffic to and from the on-premises network.  Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions a VPC and the required subnets. Deploy the template to each AWS account.
answers.explanation: This is not cost-effective or scalable because it creates unnecessary VPCs in every team's account, leading to duplicated network configurations and management overhead. Sharing the VPC resources via AWS RAM (Option B) is the recommended approach for centralized networking.

answers.content: Create an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions a VPC and the required subnets. Deploy the template to a shared services account. Share the subnets by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
answers.explanation:
the subnets by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
This is a cost-effective and scalable approach for a company with multiple teams/accounts that need to share the same on-premises connectivity via a single VPC. By creating the VPC in a shared services account and using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share subnets, other team accounts can deploy resources into the centralized VPC, minimizing VPC sprawl and centralizing network management.

answers.content: Use AWS Transit Gateway along with an AWS Site-to-Site VPN for connectivity to the on-premises network. Share the transit gateway by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
answers.explanation: While AWS Transit Gateway is the preferred solution for connecting multiple VPCs to on-premises networks at scale, the problem states the company needs only "a VPC" connected to the on-premises network, and all teams work in the "same AWS Region." If the goal is cost-effectiveness for a single, centralized VPC connection, Transit Gateway adds unnecessary complexity and cost compared to simply using an AWS Site-to-Site VPN on the shared VPC.

answers.content: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN for connectivity to the on-premises network.
answers.explanation: (less than 50 Mbps). Direct Connect (Option E) would be significantly more expensive and is typically used for higher bandwidth (1 Gbps and higher) or dedicated low-latency connections.

answers.content: Use AWS Direct Connect for connectivity to the on-premises network.
answers.explanation: AWS Direct Connect is designed for high-throughput, low-latency, and dedicated private connections. Given the traffic expectation of "less than 50 Mbps," Direct Connect is significantly more expensive than AWS Site-to-Site VPN (Option D) and is therefore not the MOST cost-effective option.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate to AWS. The company is running thousands of VMs in a VMware ESXi environment. The company has no configuration management database and has little knowledge about the utilization of the VMware portfolio.  A solutions architect must provide the company with an accurate inventory so that the company can plan for a cost-effective migration.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to deploy Migration Evaluator to each VM. Review the collected data in Amazon QuickSight. Identify servers that have high utilization. Remove the servers that have high utilization from the migration list. Import the data to AWS Migration Hub.
answers.explanation: Deploying Patch Manager and agents on each VM adds unnecessary operational overhead.

answers.content: Export the VMware portfolio to a .csv filCheck the disk utilization for each server. Remove servers that have high utilization. Export the data to AWS Application Migration ServicUse AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) to migrate the remaining servers.
answers.explanation: Manual export and checking via CSV files is error-prone, lacks automation, and is not a scalable solution.

answers.content: Deploy the Migration Evaluator agentless collector to the ESXi hypervisor. Review the collected data in Migration Evaluator. Identify inactive servers. Remove the inactive servers from the migration list. Import the data to AWS Migration Hub.
answers.explanation: Migration Evaluator provides an agentless collector for VMware ESXi, reducing operational overhead compared to deploying agents on each VM. Migration Evaluator gives accurate utilization and inventory data to plan cost-efficient migration. Data from Migration Evaluator can be imported into AWS Migration Hub, providing centralized tracking for migrations. This approach aligns with best practices for minimizing operational overhead while gathering detailed VMware portfolio data.

answers.content: Deploy the AWS Application Migration Service Agent to each VM. When the data is collected, use Amazon Redshift to import and analyze the data. Use Amazon QuickSight for data visualization.
answers.explanation: Deploying agents on each VM increases overhead and using Redshift for analysis adds complexity.

questions.content: A company needs to migrate its customer transactions database from on premises to AWS. The database resides on an Oracle DB instance that runs on a Linux server. According to a new security requirement, the company must rotate the database password each year.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Convert the database to Amazon DynamoDB by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter StorCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function for yearly passtard rotation.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is a NoSQL service, not suitable for relational transaction databases, and using Systems Manager Parameter Store with CloudWatch alarms and Lambda for rotation adds operational overhead compared to Secrets Manager.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for OraclStore the password in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation. Configure a yearly rotation schedule.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS for Oracle is a managed service that supports Oracle databases and reduces operational overhead. AWS Secrets Manager is designed for managing secrets securely and supports automatic password rotation, which aligns with the security requirement. Turning on automatic rotation in Secrets Manager minimizes manual intervention and meets the yearly rotation schedulUsing managed services like Amazon RDS and Secrets Manager is preferred over custom Lambda functions or manual rotation, aligning with AWS best practices for security and low operational overhead.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon EC2 instancUse AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to keep and rotate the connection string by using an AWS Lambda function on a yearly schedule.
answers.explanation: Running Oracle on EC2 is not a managed service and maintaining rotation with Parameter Store and Lambda incurs more operational overhead and does not leverage advanced secret management features.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Neptune by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function for yearly password rotation.
answers.explanation: Amazon Neptune is a graph database, not suitable for an Oracle transaction database, and the manual rotation with Lambda adds operational overhead compared to automatic rotation in Secrets Manager.

questions.content: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage the company's AWS accounts. The company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy all infrastructurA finance team wants to build a chargeback model. The finance team asked each business unit to tag resources by using a predefined list of project values.  When the finance team used the AWS Cost and Usage Report in AWS Cost Explorer and filtered based on project, the team noticed noncompliant project values. The company wants to enforce the use of project tags for new resources.  Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

answers.content: Create a tag policy that contains the allowed project tag values in the organization's management account. Create an SCP that denies the cloudformation:CreateStack API operation unless a project tag is added. Attach the SCP to each OU.
answers.explanation: SCPs cannot enforce specific tag values and cannot conditionally deny CreateStack based on tag existence or values.

answers.content: Create a tag policy that contains the allowed project tag values in each OU. Create an SCP that denies the cloudformation:CreateStack API operation unless a project tag is added. Attach the SCP to each OU.
answers.explanation: Tag policies do not enforce tag usage and managing tag policies per OU adds complexity; SCPs lack tag value enforcement capabilities.

answers.content: Create a tag policy that contains the allowed project tag values in the AWS management account. Create an IAM policy that denies the cloudformation:CreateStack API operation unless a project tag is added. Assign the policy to each user.
answers.explanation: IAM policies assigned to users do not scale well and increase management overhead; they do not guarantee all resources are tagged properly on creation.

answers.content: Use AWS Service Catalog to manage the CloudFormation stacks as products. Use a TagOptions library to control project tag values. Share the portfolio with all OUs that are in the organization.
answers.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows centralized management and enforces tagging rules using TagOptions for controlled and compliant deployment of CloudFormation stacks. Using TagOptions ensures that only allowed project tag values can be used, enforcing compliance with minimal manual effort. Sharing the Service Catalog portfolio with all OUs ensures consistent enforcement across the organization. SCPs cannot enforce tag values, only deny actions, and IAM policies assigned individually to users increase management overhead and are prone to noncompliancTag policies alone do not enforce tag usage but only provide guidelines or recommendations.

questions.content: A company runs an IoT application in the AWS Cloud. The company has millions of sensors that collect data from houses in the United States. The sensors use the MQTT protocol to connect and send data to a custom MQTT broker. The MQTT broker stores the data on a single Amazon EC2 instancThe sensors connect to the broker through the domain named iot.example.com. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS servicThe company stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB.  On several occasions, the amount of data has overloaded the MQTT broker and has resulted in lost sensor data. The company must improve the reliability of the solution.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an Auto Scaling group for the MQTT broker. Use the Auto Scaling group as the target for the ALB. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to an alias record. Point the alias record to the ALB. Use the MQTT broker to store the data.
answers.explanation: Scaling the MQTT broker on EC2 with ALB and Auto Scaling still relies on a custom solution and does not provide the reliability and managed scaling of AWS IoT Core.

answers.content: Set up AWS IoT Core to receive the sensor data. Create and configure a custom domain to connect to AWS IoT CorUpdate the DNS record in Route 53 to point to the AWS IoT Core Data-ATS endpoint. Configure an AWS IoT rule to store the data.
answers.explanation: AWS IoT Core is a fully managed service designed to securely connect and scale millions of IoT devices using MQTT. Using AWS IoT Core improves reliability and scalability compared to a custom MQTT broker on EC2. AWS IoT Core supports custom domains and rules to route/store data (e.g., into DynamoDB), aligning with best practices for handling IoT data. Using AWS IoT Core leverages a managed service specifically for IoT device connectivity and data ingestion, which is preferred over manual management of EC2 brokers.

answers.content: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Set the MQTT broker as the target. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator. Set the NLB as the endpoint for the accelerator. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to a multivalue answer record. Set the Global Accelerator IP addresses as values. Use the MQTT broker to store the data.
answers.explanation: Global Accelerator and NLB route traffic to a single MQTT broker, which does not solve the single point of failure or scaling issue and is not a managed IoT service.

answers.content: Set up AWS IoT Greengrass to receive the sensor data. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to point to the AWS IoT Greengrass endpoint. Configure an AWS IoT rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to store the data.
answers.explanation: AWS IoT Greengrass is for edge processing and local compute rather than a managed cloud ingestion service; it does not directly address MQTT ingestion and reliability as AWS IoT Core does.

questions.content: A company runs a microservice as an AWS Lambda function. The microservice writes data to an on-premises SQL database that supports a limited number of concurrent connections. When the number of Lambda function invocations is too high, the database crashes and causes application downtimThe company has an AWS Direct Connect connection between the company's VPC and the on-premises data center. The company wants to protect the database from crashes.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Write the data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuConfigure the Lambda function to read from the queue and write to the existing databasSet a reserved concurrency limit on the Lambda function that is less than the number of connections that the database supports.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SQS decouples the Lambda function invocation rate from the direct number of database connections, allowing controlled processing of data writes. Setting a reserved concurrency limit on the Lambda function ensures the number of concurrent database connections stays below the database's limit, protecting the database from overload. This approach aligns with best practices to protect backend systems from being overwhelmed by bursts of requests. Options involving SNS or RDS Proxy do not directly control concurrent connections or offer queue-based throttling to protect the database in this scenario.

answers.content: Create a new Amazon Aurora Serverless DB cluster. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the existing database to Aurora Serverless. Reconfigure the Lambda function to write to Aurora.
answers.explanation: Migrating to Aurora Serverless changes the database but does not address controlling the connection rate or protecting the existing database from overload.

answers.content: Create an Amazon RDS Proxy DB instancAttach the RDS Proxy DB instance to the Amazon RDS DB instancReconfigure the Lambda function to write to the RDS Proxy DB instance.
answers.explanation: RDS Proxy is meant for Amazon RDS databases, not on-premises databases, so it cannot be used with the on-premises SQL database.

answers.content: Write the data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Invoke the Lambda function to write to the existing database when the topic receives new messages. Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function to be equal to the number of connections that the database supports.
answers.explanation: Using SNS is a pub/sub model and does not inherently control concurrent executions; provisioned concurrency does not guarantee limiting database connections below the supported limit.

questions.content: A solutions architect works for a government agency that has strict disaster recovery requirements. All Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots are required to be saved in at least two additional AWS Regions. The agency also is required to maintain the lowest possible operational overhead.  Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Configure a policy in Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to run once daily to copy the EBS snapshots to the additional Regions.
answers.explanation: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) supports policies that automate the copying of EBS snapshots to additional AWS Regions, meeting strict disaster recovery requirements with low operational overhead. Using DLM is a managed AWS service designed specifically to automate snapshot lifecycle management, which aligns with best practices and reduces manual operational tasks. Other options involve custom automation (Lambda) or services unsuitable for direct EBS snapshot cross-region copying or add unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function to copy the EBS snapshots to the additional Regions.
answers.explanation: Using EventBridge and Lambda requires custom automation, increasing operational overhead, which does not meet the requirement for lowest operational overhead.

answers.content: Setup AWS Backup to create the EBS snapshots. Configure Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy the EBS snapshots to the additional Regions.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication does not apply to EBS snapshots, so this solution is not feasible.

answers.content: Schedule Amazon EC2 Image Builder to run once daily to create an AMI and copy the AMI to the additional Regions.
