answers.explanation: Custom Lambda solution for tagging is not preferred over managed AWS services and is less secure and operationally complex than SCP enforcement.

answers.content: Use Tag Editor to tag existing resources. Create cost allocation tags to define the cost center and project ID. Use SCPs to restrict resource creation that do not have the cost center and project ID on the resource.
answers.explanation: Tag Editor can be used to tag existing resources, fulfilling the need to add cost center and project ID tags to existing RDS and DynamoDB resources. Creating cost allocation tags for cost center and project ID is necessary to enable cost tracking and reporting. Service Control Policies (SCPs) can enforce compliance by restricting resource creation without required tags, ensuring tagging consistency for future resources across accounts. This solution leverages managed AWS services (Tag Editor, SCPs) to enforce tagging policies, aligning with best practices of security and centralized control.

answers.content: Create cost allocation tags to define the cost center and project ID and allow 24 hours for tags to propagate to existing resources. Update existing federated roles to restrict privileges to provision resources that do not include the cost center and project ID on the resource.
answers.explanation: Restricting privileges via federated roles is less manageable and less comprehensive than SCPs across multiple accounts; also federated roles update is manual and error-prone.

questions.content: A company has IoT sensors that monitor traffic patterns throughout a large city. The company wants to read and collect data from the sensors and perform aggregations on the data. A solutions architect designs a solution in which the IoT devices are streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Several applications are reading from the stream. However, several consumers are experiencing throttling and are periodically encountering a ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded error. Which actions should the solutions architect take to resolve this issue? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Reshard the stream to increase the number of shards in the stream.
answers.explanation: Increasing the number of shards increases read throughput capacity, reducing the likelihood of ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors.

answers.content: Use the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL). Adjust the polling frequency.
answers.explanation: KPL and polling frequency adjustments apply to producers, not consumers, and do not address read throttling.

answers.content: Use consumers with the enhanced fan-out feature.
answers.explanation: Enhanced fan-out provides dedicated read throughput (2 MB/s per consumer per shard), preventing multiple consumers from contending for the same shard capacity.

answers.content: Reshard the stream to reduce the number of shards in the stream.
answers.explanation: Reducing the number of shards would further decrease read throughput and worsen throttling.

answers.content: Use an error retry and exponential backoff mechanism in the consumer logic.
answers.explanation: Implementing retries with exponential backoff helps consumers gracefully handle throttling without overwhelming the stream.

answers.content: Configure the stream to use dynamic partitioning.
answers.explanation: Dynamic partitioning is a feature of Kinesis Data Firehose, not Kinesis Data Streams.

questions.content: A company has set up its entire infrastructure on AWS. The company uses Amazon EC2 instances to host its ecommerce website and uses Amazon S3 to store static data. Three engineers at the company handle the cloud administration and development through one AWS account. Occasionally, an engineer alters an EC2 security group configuration of another engineer and causes noncompliance issues in the environment. A solutions architect must set up a system that tracks changes that the engineers makThe system must send alerts when the engineers make noncompliant changes to the security settings for the EC2 instances. What is the FASTEST way for the solutions architect to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Set up AWS Organizations for the company. Apply SCPs to govern and track noncompliant security group changes that are made to the AWS account.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations and SCPs cannot track or alert on changes; SCPs only enforce permissions and do not provide change tracking or alerts.

answers.content: Enable AWS CloudTrail to capture the changes to EC2 security groups. Enable Amazon CloudWatch rules to provide alerts when noncompliant security settings are detected.
answers.explanation: CloudTrail logs changes but does not natively detect compliance or send alerts about noncompliant security group changes without additional complex setup.

answers.content: Enable SCPs on the AWS account to provide alerts when noncompliant security group changes are made to the environment.
answers.explanation: SCPs do not provide alerting capabilities; they only restrict permissions and cannot send notifications.

answers.content: Enable AWS Config on the EC2 security groups to track any noncompliant changes. Send the changes as alerts through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
answers.explanation: AWS Config is designed to track configurations and compliance changes in AWS resources, including EC2 security groups. AWS Config can be set up to automatically evaluate changes against compliance rules and send alerts via Amazon SNS. This provides a managed, secure, and fast way to monitor noncompliant changes and notify teams immediately.

questions.content: A solutions architect at a large company needs to set up network security for outbound traffic to the internet from all AWS accounts within an organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has more than 100 AWS accounts, and the accounts route to each other by using a centralized AWS Transit Gateway. Each account has both an internet gateway and a NAT gateway for outbound traffic to the internet. The company deploys resources only into a single AWS Region. The company needs the ability to add centrally managed rule-based filtering on all outbound traffic to the internet for all AWS accounts in the organization. The peak load of outbound traffic will not exceed 25 Gbps in each Availability ZonWhich solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new VPC for outbound traffic to the internet. Connect the existing transit gateway to the new VPC. Configure a new NAT gateway. Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances that run an open-source internet proxy for rule-based filtering across all Availability Zones in the Region. Modify all default routes to point to the proxy's Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Using an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances with open-source proxies is a custom solution, which is less secure, less scalable, and more operationally complex than a managed firewall.

answers.content: Create a new VPC for outbound traffic to the internet. Connect the existing transit gateway to the new VPC. Configure a new NAT gateway. Use an AWS Network Firewall firewall for rule-based filtering. Create Network Firewall endpoints in each Availability ZonModify all default routes to point to the Network Firewall endpoints.
answers.explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed service that provides rule-based filtering for network traffic and is designed to integrate with AWS Transit Gateway. Creating a new VPC with a Network Firewall and connecting it to the Transit Gateway allows centralized outbound filtering for all AWS accounts in the organization. Network Firewall endpoints can be deployed in each Availability Zone to meet high availability and scalability requirements up to the needed 25 Gbps. This solution adheres to security best practices by using a managed service designed for firewall rule enforcement rather than custom proxy solutions. Modifying default routes to point to Network Firewall endpoints is the proper method for centralized inspection and filtering, leveraging AWS services.

answers.content: Create an AWS Network Firewall firewall for rule-based filtering in each AWS account. Modify all default routes to point to the Network Firewall firewalls in each account.
answers.explanation: Deploying Network Firewall in each account does not provide centralized management and scaling via Transit Gateway; it increases operational overhead.

answers.content: In each AWS account, create an Auto Scaling group of network-optimized Amazon EC2 instances that run an open-source internet proxy for rule-based filtering. Modify all default routes to point to the proxy's Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Deploying EC2 proxies in each account similarly increases complexity and operational burden and lacks centralized control via Transit Gateway.

answers.content: undefined

questions.content: A company has a Windows-based desktop application that is packaged and deployed to the users' Windows machines. The company recently acquired another company that has employees who primarily use machines with a Linux operating system. The acquiring company has decided to migrate and rehost the Windows-based desktop application to AWS. All employees must be authenticated before they use the application. The acquiring company uses Active Directory on premises but wants a simplified way to manage access to the application on AWS for all the employees. Which solution will rehost the application on AWS with the LEAST development effort?

answers.content: Set up and provision an Amazon Workspaces virtual desktop for every employeImplement authentication by using Amazon Cognito identity pools. Instruct employees to run the application from their provisioned Workspaces virtual desktops.
answers.explanation: Amazon Workspaces would require provisioning and managing virtual desktops for every employee, which is more management overhead and not as simplified as AppStream 2.0 streaming.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group of Windows-based Amazon EC2 instances. Join each EC2 instance to the company's Active Directory domain. Implement authentication by using the Active Directory that is running on premises. Instruct employees to run the application by using a Windows remote desktop.
answers.explanation: Joining EC2 instances to on-premises Active Directory and requiring remote desktop access increases operational complexity and management burden, thus more development and management effort.

answers.content: Use an Amazon AppStream 2.0 image builder to create an image that includes the application and the required configurations. Provision an AppStream 2.0 On-Demand fleet with dynamic Fleet Auto Scaling policies for running the imagImplement authentication by using AppStream 2.0 user pools. Instruct the employees to access the application by starting browser-based AppStream 2.0 streaming sessions.
answers.explanation: Amazon AppStream 2.0 allows packaging and streaming a Windows-based application to users without requiring them to run it locally, which works across different OS platforms including Linux. AppStream 2.0 supports integration with user pools for authentication, simplifying access management on AWS. This solution requires the least development effort since it does not demand refactoring or containerizing the application. Using AppStream 2.0 leverages a managed AWS service designed for application streaming and user authentication, aligning with security best practices and minimal management overhead.

answers.content: Refactor and containerize the application to run as a web-based application. Run the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate with step scaling policies. Implement authentication by using Amazon Cognito user pools. Instruct the employees to run the application from their browsers.
answers.explanation: Refactoring and containerizing the application for ECS and Fargate requires significant redevelopment effort, which is not aligned with minimizing development effort.

questions.content: A company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy applications within multiple VPCs that are all attached to a transit gateway. Each VPC that sends traffic to the public internet must send the traffic through a shared services VPC. Each subnet within a VPC uses the default VPC route table, and the traffic is routed to the transit gateway. The transit gateway uses its default route table for any VPC attachment. A security audit reveals that an Amazon EC2 instance that is deployed within a VPC can communicate with an EC2 instance that is deployed in any of the company's other VPCs. A solutions architect needs to limit the traffic between the VPCs. Each VPC must be able to communicate only with a predefined, limited set of authorized VPCs. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Update the network ACL of each subnet within a VPC to allow outbound traffic only to the authorized VPCs. Remove all deny rules except the default deny rule.
answers.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless and typically apply at the subnet level but do not provide granular control for specific VPC destinations and are less preferred compared to managed routing.

answers.content: Update all the security groups that are used within a VPC to deny outbound traffic to security groups that are used within the unauthorized VPCs.
answers.explanation: Security groups control instance-level traffic and do not filter traffic between VPCs as security groups cannot reference security groups in other VPCs; they also cannot explicitly deny traffic, only allow.

answers.content: Create a dedicated transit gateway route table for each VPC attachment. Route traffic only to the authorized VPCs.
answers.explanation: Using a dedicated transit gateway route table for each VPC attachment allows granular control over route distribution, so traffic can be limited to authorized VPCs only. The default route table sends traffic to all attached VPCs, so creating dedicated route tables is necessary to restrict traffic per AWS best practices. Transit gateway route tables are the appropriate place to control inter-VPC routing, which aligns with the provided key fact about managing routes through transit gateway route tables.

answers.content: Update the main route table of each VPC to route traffic only to the authorized VPCs through the transit gateway.
answers.explanation: Updating the main route table of each VPC to only route to authorized VPCs is insufficient because the transit gateway route table controls route propagation; the transit gateway route tables need to be configured accordingly, not just the VPC route tables.

answers.content: undefined

questions.content: A company plans to deploy a new private intranet service on Amazon EC2 instances inside a VPC. An AWS Site-to-Site VPN connects the VPC to the company's on-premises network. The new service must communicate with existing on-premises services. The on-premises services are accessible through the use of hostnames that reside in the company.example DNS zonThis DNS zone is wholly hosted on premises and is available only on the company's private network.  A solutions architect must ensure that the new service can resolve hostnames on the company.example domain to integrate with existing services.  Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create an empty private zone in Amazon Route 53 for company.examplAdd an additional NS record to the company's on-premises company.example zone that points to the authoritative name servers for the new private zone in Route 53.
answers.explanation: Creating an empty private hosted zone duplicates the DNS zone and would require complex NS delegation without guaranteeing correct resolution.

answers.content: Turn on DNS hostnames for the VPC. Configure a new outbound endpoint with Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Create a Resolver rule to forward requests for company.example to the on-premises name servers.
answers.explanation: Turning on DNS hostnames in the VPC is required. Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints allow forwarding DNS queries for specific domains to on-premises DNS servers. Creating a Resolver rule to forward company.example queries to on-premises DNS servers enables EC2 instances in the VPC to resolve private on-premises hostnames securely. This approach uses a managed AWS service designed for secure and scalable DNS forwarding without manual host file management.

answers.content: Turn on DNS hostnames for the VPConfigure a new inbound resolver endpoint with Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Configur&the on-premises DNS server to forward requests for company.example to the new resolver.
answers.explanation: Inbound resolver endpoints are used for forwarding DNS queries from on-premises to AWS, not for queries originating inside the VPC.

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager to configure a run document that will install a hosts file that contains any required hostnames. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the document when an instance is entering the running state.
answers.explanation: Using Systems Manager and hosts files is manual, not scalable, and does not follow AWS best practices for DNS resolution across networks.

questions.content: A company has implemented an ordering system using an event-driven architecturDuring initial testing, the system stopped processing orders. Further log analysis revealed that one order message in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue was causing an error on the backend and blocking all subsequent order messages. The visibility timeout of the queue is set to 30 seconds, and the backend processing timeout is set to 10 seconds. A solutions architect needs to analyze faulty order messages and ensure that the system continues to process subsequent messages.  Which step should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Increase the backend processing timeout to 30 seconds to match the visibility timeout.
answers.explanation: Increasing backend timeout does not prevent message blocking caused by repeated failures on a single message.

answers.content: Reduce the visibility timeout of the queue to automatically remove the faulty message.
answers.explanation: Reducing visibility timeout risks immediate message reprocessing without isolating faulty messages for analysis.

answers.content: Configure a new SQS FIFO queue as a dead-letter queue to isolate the faulty messages.
answers.explanation: Using an SQS FIFO queue as a DLQ for a standard queue is not appropriate and adds complexity.

answers.content: Configure a new SQS standard queue as a dead-letter queue to isolate the faulty messages.
answers.explanation: Using a dead-letter queue (DLQ) allows isolation of faulty messages without blocking subsequent message processing. SQS standard queues support dead-letter queues for handling messages that can't be processed successfully. Configuring a new SQS standard queue as the DLQ fits the existing architecture and helps analyze faulty messages safely. Increasing backend processing timeout or reducing visibility timeout does not solve message blocking caused by faulty messages. Using an SQS FIFO queue as a DLQ is unnecessary and mismatched, given the original queue is standard.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate an Amazon RDS for Oracle database to an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in another AWS account. A solutions architect needs to design a migration strategy that will require no downtime and that will minimize the amount of time necessary to complete the migration. The migration strategy must replicate all existing data and any new data that is created during the migration. The target database must be identical to the source database at completion of the migration process.  All applications currently use an Amazon Route 53 CNAME record as their endpoint for communication with the RDS for Oracle DB instancThe RDS for Oracle DB instance is in a private subnet.  Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a new RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in the target account. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database schema from the source database to the target database.
answers.explanation: AWS SCT is required when migrating Oracle → PostgreSQL to convert and apply the schema. Creating the target DB separately and migrating only the schema is the correct and controlled approach.

answers.content: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create a new RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in the target account with the schema and initial data from the source database.
answers.explanation: AWS SCT does not create RDS instances or migrate data; it converts schemas only; instance creation and migration must be done separately.

answers.content: Configure VPC peering between the VPCs in the two AWS accounts to provide connectivity to both DB instances from the target account. Configure the security groups that are attached to each DB instance to allow traffic on the database port from the VPC in the target account.
answers.explanation: Both databases are in private subnets, so private connectivity is required. VPC peering allows AWS DMS in the target account to access the source Oracle DB securely without exposing it to the public internet.

answers.content: Temporarily allow the source DB instance to be publicly accessible to provide connectivity from the VPC in the target account. Configure the security groups that are attached to each DB instance to allow traffic on the database port from the VPC in the target account.
answers.explanation: Making the source DB publicly accessible is a security risk and contradicts best practices; VPC peering is preferred.

answers.content: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) in the target account to perform a full load plus change data capture (CDC) migration from the source database to the target databasWhen the migration is complete, change the CNAME record to point to the target DB instance endpoint.
answers.explanation:
DMS full load + CDC ensures:All existing data is migrated

New data changes are continuously replicated

No downtime
Switching the Route 53 CNAME enables a clean cutover with minimal disruption and keeps the target DB identical at completion.

answers.content: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) in the target account to perform a change data capture (CDC) migration from the source database to the target database. When the migration is complete, change the CNAME record to point to the target DB instance endpoint.
answers.explanation: CDC-only migration does not migrate existing data, so the target DB would not be complete.

questions.content: A company has an application that generates reports and stores them in an Amazon S3 bucket. When a user accesses their report, the application generates a signed URL to allow the user to download the report. The company's security team has discovered that the files are public and that anyone can download them without authentication. The company has suspended the generation of new reports until the problem is resolved.  Which set of actions will immediately remediate the security issue without impacting the application's normal workflow?

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function that applies a deny all policy for users who are not authenticated. Create a scheduled event to invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: A Lambda function with deny policies is indirect and slower to remediate; it also requires management overhead.

answers.content: Review the AWS Trusted Advisor bucket permissions check and implement the recommended actions.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations but does not immediately enforce changes or block public access.

answers.content: Run a script that puts a private ACL on all of the objects in the bucket.
answers.explanation: Applying private ACLs via a script is manual, error-prone, and slower than using the Block Public Access feature.

answers.content: Use the Block Public Access feature in Amazon S3 to set the IgnorePublicAcIs option to TRUE on the bucket.
answers.explanation: Using the Block Public Access feature in Amazon S3 to set the IgnorePublicAcls option to TRUE immediately stops all public access granted by ACLs, remediating the exposure without changing application workflows. This leverages a managed S3 security feature designed to protect buckets and objects from unintended public access, aligning with AWS best practices. Other options involve more complex or indirect methods that do not immediately ensure no public access or require custom scripts or Lambda functions.

questions.content: A company is using AWS Organizations to manage multiple accounts. Due to regulatory requirements, the company wants to restrict specific member accounts to certain AWS Regions, where they are permitted to deploy resources. The resources in the accounts must be tagged, enforced based on a group standard, and centrally managed with minimal configuration.  What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS Config rule in the specific member accounts to limit Regions and apply a tag policy.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules run in each individual account and require more configuration per account, which is not minimal central management.

answers.content: From the AWS Billing and Cost Management console, in the management account, disable Regions for the specific member accounts and apply a tag policy on the root.
answers.explanation: Billing console does not support disabling Regions per account; this is not a valid AWS Organizations management feature.

answers.content: Associate the specific member accounts with the root. Apply a tag policy and an SCP using conditions to limit Regions.
answers.explanation: Applying SCPs and tag policies at the root level affects all member accounts rather than just specific accounts, losing granularity and precise control.

answers.content: Associate the specific member accounts with a new OU. Apply a tag policy and an SCP using conditions to limit Regions.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations allows applying Service Control Policies (SCPs) that can restrict access based on conditions such as allowed Regions, which ensures centralized and enforced region restrictions. Applying SCPs at the Organizational Unit (OU) level facilitates management of multiple accounts collectively with minimal configuration. Tag policies in AWS Organizations enforce tagging standards centrally across accounts, meeting the requirement for resource tagging based on group standards. Using SCPs and tag policies leverages managed AWS services designed for centralized governance and security compliance, aligning with AWS best practices.

questions.content: A company hosts a web application on AWS in the us-east-1 Region. The application servers are distributed across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. The database is hosted in a MySQL database on an Amazon EC2 instancA solutions architect needs to design a cross-Region data recovery solution using AWS services with an RTO of less than 5 minutes and an RPO of less than 1 minutThe solutions architect is deploying application servers in us-west-2, and has configured Amazon Route 53 health checks and DNS failover to us-west-2.  Which additional step should the solutions architect take?

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL instance with a cross-Region read replica in us-west-2.
answers.explanation: Cross-Region read replicas on RDS for MySQL do not guarantee less than 1 minute RPO or less than 5 minute RTO due to potential replication lag.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora global database with the primary in us-east-1 and the secondary in us-west-2.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora global database provides a managed cross-Region replication solution with low latency, supporting fast recovery (RTO less than 5 minutes and RPO less than 1 minute). It is a managed AWS service designed for cross-Region disaster recovery with high availability and minimal data loss. Migrating to Aurora global database aligns with security best practices by leveraging a fully managed service rather than manually managing standby databases on EC2.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL instance with a Multi-AZ deployment.
answers.explanation: Multi-AZ deployment is within a single Region and does not provide cross-Region disaster recovery.

answers.content: Create a MySQL standby database on an Amazon EC2 instance in us-west-2.
answers.explanation: Managing a MySQL standby database on EC2 in another Region is a manual and less secure approach compared to using managed AWS services.

questions.content: A company wants to refactor its retail ordering web application that currently has a load-balanced Amazon EC2 instance fleet for web hosting, database API services, and business logic. The company needs to create a decoupled, scalable architecture with a mechanism for retaining failed orders while also minimizing operational costs.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon S3 for web hosting with Amazon API Gateway for database API services. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for order queuing. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) for business logic with Amazon SQS long polling for retaining failed orders.
answers.explanation: Amazon ECS requires management of clusters and is less serverless than Lambda; long polling in ECS is operationally heavier than using dead-letter queues.

answers.content: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk for web hosting with Amazon API Gateway for database API services. Use Amazon MQ for order queuing. Use AWS Step Functions for business logic with Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive for retaining failed orders.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon MQ increases operational complexity and cost compared to SQS; Glacier Deep Archive is inappropriate for retaining failed orders due to retrieval latency.

answers.content: Use Amazon S3 for web hosting with AWS AppSync for database API services. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for order queuing. Use AWS Lambda for business logic with an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue for retaining failed orders.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is a suitable and cost-effective static web hosting solution. AWS AppSync is a managed GraphQL service appropriate for database API services, providing scalability and a decoupled architecturAmazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that allows decoupling of components and handling order queuing as required. AWS Lambda provides serverless business logic processing, which scales automatically and reduces operational overhead. Using Amazon SQS dead-letter queues to retain failed orders aligns with best practices for handling failures and retry mechanisms without incurring additional cost or complex setups.

answers.content: Use Amazon Lightsail for web hosting with AWS AppSync for database API services. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) for order queuing. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) for business logic with Amazon OpenSearch Service for retaining failed orders.
answers.explanation: Amazon SES is for email and not suitable for order queuing; Amazon Lightsail and EKS add more operational overhead compared to serverless options.

questions.content: A company is expanding. The company plans to separate its resources into hundreds of different AWS accounts in multiple AWS Regions. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that denies access to any operations outside of specifically designated Regions.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create IAM roles for each account. Create IAM policies with conditional allow permissions that include only approved Regions for the accounts.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM roles and policies per account is not scalable or centrally enforceable for hundreds of accounts and does not leverage AWS Organizations SCPs.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Create IAM users for each account. Attach a policy to each user to block access to Regions where an account cannot deploy infrastructure.
answers.explanation: IAM user policies cannot centrally enforce restrictions across accounts as effectively as SCPs and can be bypassed.

answers.content: Launch an AWS Control Tower landing zonCreate OUs and attach SCPs that deny access to run services outside of the approved Regions.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower supports the creation of organizational units (OUs) and allows the attachment of Service Control Policies (SCPs) that can restrict access to AWS services in only approved Regions, which is a managed, scalable solution for multiple accounts. Using SCPs in AWS Organizations is the recommended approach to consistently deny access outside designated Regions across many accounts. IAM roles and policies (Option A) alone are not as scalable or centrally enforceable across hundreds of accounts compared to SCPs attached via Control Tower. IAM user policies (Option B) are less manageable and less secure than SCPs for this type of restriction at the organizational level. AWS Security Hub (Option D) is for security posture monitoring and compliance checks, not for blocking access or restricting Regions.

answers.content: Enable AWS Security Hub in each account. Create controls to specify the Regions where an account can deploy infrastructure.
answers.explanation: AWS Security Hub is for security assessments and does not enforce access restrictions or deny operations in Regions.

questions.content: A company wants to optimize AWS data-transfer costs and compute costs across developer accounts within the company's organization in AWS Organizations. Developers can configure VPCs and launch Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The EC2 instances retrieve approximately 1 TB of data each day from Amazon S3.  The developer activity leads to excessive monthly data-transfer charges and NAT gateway processing charges between EC2 instances and S3 buckets, along with high compute costs. The company wants to proactively enforce approved architectural patterns for any EC2 instance and VPC infrastructure that developers deploy within the AWS accounts. The company does not want this enforcement to negatively affect the speed at which the developers can perform their tasks.  Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Create SCPs to prevent developers from launching unapproved EC2 instance types. Provide the developers with an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy an approved VPC configuration with S3 interface endpoints. Scope the developers' IAM permissions so that the developers can launch VPC resources only with CloudFormation.
answers.explanation: SCPs cannot enforce VPC endpoint usage or VPC configuration, and restricting VPC launches only through CloudFormation is operationally restrictive and less flexible than Service Catalog.

answers.content: Create a daily forecasted budget with AWS Budgets to monitor EC2 compute costs and S3 data-transfer costs across the developer accounts. When the forecasted cost is 75% of the actual budget cost, send an alert to the developer teams. If the actual budget cost is 100%, create a budget action to terminate the developers' EC2 instances and VPC infrastructure.
answers.explanation: Budgets only provide monitoring and alerts, not proactive enforcement, and terminating resources after budget limits harms developer productivity and does not prevent initial cost incurrence.

answers.content: Create an AWS Service Catalog portfolio that users can use to create an approved VPC configuration with S3 gateway endpoints and approved EC2 instances. Share the portfolio with the developer accounts. Configure an AWS Service Catalog launch constraint to use an approved IAM rolScope the developers' IAM permissions to allow access only to AWS Service Catalog.
answers.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows defining and enforcing approved infrastructure patterns, promoting consistent, compliant deployment. Using Service Catalog launch constraints with approved IAM roles ensures developers use only approved EC2 instances and VPC configurations, including S3 gateway endpoints for cost savings. Limiting developers' IAM permissions to AWS Service Catalog prevents unapproved manual resource creation, enforcing architecture standards proactively without impacting developer speed. Service Catalog is a managed AWS service designed for this purpose and is more cost-effective and less operationally complex than continuous monitoring or enforcement after deployment.

answers.content: Create and deploy AWS Config rules to monitor the compliance of EC2 and VPC resources in the developer AWS accounts. If developers launch unapproved EC2 instances or if developers create VPCs without S3 gateway endpoints, perform a remediation action to terminate the unapproved resources.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules detect and remediate noncompliance reactively, which may interrupt developer workflows and incur additional costs before remediation; also less proactive than Service Catalog enforcement.

questions.content: A company has a website that runs on four Amazon EC2 instances that are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). When the ALB detects that an EC2 instance is no longer available, an Amazon CloudWatch alarm enters the ALARM statA member of the company's operations team then manually adds a new EC2 instance behind the ALB.  A solutions architect needs to design a highly available solution that automatically handles the replacement of EC2 instances. The company needs to minimize downtime during the switch to the new solution.  Which set of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Delete the existing ALB. Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Create a new ALB. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the new ALB. Attach the existing EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Deleting the existing ALB and creating a new one may cause downtime, which conflicts with the requirement to minimize downtime.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the existing ALAttach the existing EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Creating an Auto Scaling group to handle traffic ensures automatic replacement of unhealthy EC2 instances, improving high availability and reducing manual intervention. Attaching the Auto Scaling group to the existing ALB avoids downtime by keeping the current load balancer in place, maintaining user traffic flow. Using a launch template ensures consistent configuration for all EC2 instances launched by the Auto Scaling group. Attaching existing EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group allows the group to manage current instances and scale as needed without deleting resources.

answers.content: Delete the existing ALB and the EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Create a new ALB. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the new ALB. Wait for the Auto Scaling group to launch the minimum number of EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Deleting the existing ALB and EC2 instances will cause downtime and is not necessary for adding Auto Scaling capabilities.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the existing ALB. Wait for the existing ALB to register the existing EC2 instances with the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Existing EC2 instances cannot be simply 'registered' to an Auto Scaling group for management; they must be launched or replaced by the group.

questions.content: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The company uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy the application. The instances that run in the Auto Scaling group are constantly changing because of scaling events.  When the company deploys new application code versions, the company installs the AWS CodeDeploy agent on any new target EC2 instances and associates the instances with the CodeDeploy deployment group. The application is set to go live within the next 24 hours.  What should a solutions architect recommend to automate the application deployment process with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answers.content: Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a new EC2 instance is launched into the Auto Scaling group. Code the Lambda function to associate the EC2 instances with the CodeDeploy deployment group.
answers.explanation: Requires custom Lambda code and manual association, increasing operational overhead and complexity.

answers.content: Write a script to suspend Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling operations before the deployment of new codWhen the deployment is complete, create a new AMI and configure the Auto Scaling group's launch template to use the new AMI for new launches. Resume Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling operations.
answers.explanation: Involves suspending scaling and manual AMI creation, which adds operational overhead and risks downtime.

answers.content: Create a new AWS CodeBuild project that creates a new AMI that contains the new codConfigure CodeBuild to update the Auto Scaling group’s launch template to the new AMI. Run an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling instance refresh operation.
answers.explanation: CodeBuild and instance refresh add complexity and operational overhead compared to directly updating the launch template with an AMI.

answers.content: Create a new AMI that has the CodeDeploy agent installed. Configure the Auto Scaling group’s launch template to use the new AMI. Associate the CodeDeploy deployment group with the Auto Scaling group instead of the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Using an AMI with the CodeDeploy agent installed ensures every new instance launched by the Auto Scaling group is ready for deployments without additional manual or Lambda automation. Associating the deployment group directly with the Auto Scaling group automates target management seamlessly as instances are launched or terminated. This approach leverages managed AWS services and least operational overhead, aligning with recommended best practices for automated deployments in Auto Scaling environments.

questions.content: A company’s interactive web application uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve images from an Amazon S3 bucket. Occasionally, third-party tools ingest corrupted images into the S3 bucket. This image corruption causes a poor user experience in the application later. The company has successfully implemented and tested Python logic to detect corrupt images.  A solutions architect must recommend a solution to integrate the detection logic with minimal latency between the ingestion and serving.  Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use a Lambda@Edge function that is invoked by a viewer-response event.
answers.explanation: Lambda@Edge viewer-response triggers after content is served, adding latency rather than minimizing it.

answers.content: Use a Lambda@Edge function that is invoked by an origin-response event.
answers.explanation: Lambda@Edge origin-response triggers after the origin sends the response; it does not prevent corrupted images from being served initially.

answers.content: Use an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Using an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function is the preferred managed service approach to process and detect corrupted images immediately after ingestion in S3. This method has minimal latency between the ingestion of images and the execution of the detection logic because S3 events trigger the Lambda function asynchronously and quickly. Lambda@Edge functions triggered by CloudFront viewer-response or origin-response events occur after serving content and would increase latency and degrade user experience rather than reduce it. Using AWS Step Functions (option D) adds orchestration complexity and latency compared to a direct Lambda invocation, which is unnecessary since the detection logic is already implemented in Python and can run directly in Lambda.

answers.content: Use an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Step Functions state machine.
answers.explanation: Using Step Functions adds unnecessary orchestration overhead and latency when a Lambda function alone suffices.

questions.content: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage more than 1,000 AWS accounts. The company has created a new developer organization. There are 540 developer member accounts that must be moved to the new developer organization. All accounts are set up with all the required information so that each account can be operated as a standalone account.  Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to move all of the developer accounts to the new developer organization? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Call the MoveAccount operation in the Organizations API from the old organization's management account to migrate the developer accounts to the new developer organization.
answers.explanation: MoveAccount only works within the same organization, not between two different organizations.

answers.content: From the management account, remove each developer account from the old organization using the RemoveAccountFromOrganization operation in the Organizations API.
answers.explanation: An AWS account cannot belong to two organizations at the same time, so each developer account must first be removed from the old organization by the old management account.

answers.content: From each developer account, remove the account from the old organization using the RemoveAccountFromOrganization operation in the Organizations API.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because RemoveAccountFromOrganization cannot be called from the member account; it must be called from the management account.

answers.content: Sign in to the new developer organization's management account and create a placeholder member account that acts as a target for the developer account migration.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because creating placeholder accounts is not a required or supported step for migrating accounts between organizations.

answers.content: Call the InviteAccountToOrganization operation in the Organizations API from the new developer organization's management account to send invitations to the developer accounts.
answers.explanation: Correct because the new organization's management account must invite the accounts to join by calling InviteAccountToOrganization.

answers.content: Have each developer sign in to their account and confirm to join the new developer organization.
answers.explanation: An account must explicitly accept an organization invitation before it can join the new organization.
